'''Rory William McKenzie''' (born 7 October 1993) is a Scottish [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)#Midfielder|midfielder]] for  {{Scottish football updater|Kilmarno}} club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kilmarnockfc.co.uk/TeamsPlayer?sPlayer=460&sTeam=398|title=Kilmarnock Profile|accessdate=11 July 2014}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Kilmarnock===
Born in [[Irvine, North Ayrshire|Irvine]], raised in [[Troon]] and a produced by the [[youth system]] at [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]],<ref>[http://www.youthfootballscotland.co.uk/south-west-region/item/18033-kilmarnock-fc-s-rory-mckenzie-first-team-football-so-important-for-young-pros.html Kilmarnock FC's Rory McKenzie: 'First-team football so important for young pros'], Youth Football Scotland, 2014</ref> McKenzie made his senior debut for the club as a substitute in a 1–1 draw against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] on 9 April 2011.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/9450635.stm|title=Inverness 1 V Kilmarnock 1|date=9 April 2011 | work=BBC News}}</ref>

In the [[2012–13 Kilmarnock F.C. season|2012–13]] season, he came on as a sub in the first two fixtures. He then started his first game against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee Utd]] on 25 August 2012, where he scored a minute into the second half, as ''Killie'' went on to win 3–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19304309|title=Kilmarnock 3–1 Dundee United|work=BBC Sport |date=24 August 2012 |access-date=August 25, 2012}}</ref>

On 14 May 2013, McKenzie signed a new contract, keeping him at Kilmarnock until Summer 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rory McKenzie and Lee Ashcroft sign new Kilmarnock deals|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22534076|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 May 2013|access-date=9 December 2013}}</ref> In the [[2014–15 Kilmarnock F.C. season|2014–15]] season, McKenzie scored the only goal in a 1–0 win over [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] in the [[Ayrshire Derby]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/28847354|title=Kilmarnock 1-0 Ayr United|work=BBC Sport |date=25 August 2014 |accessdate=January 10, 2020}}</ref>

He signed a further contract in summer 2016, and was the only one of several home-grown players to remain at the club after the squad was overhauled following an 11th-place finish in the [[Scottish Premiership]] which required them to defeat [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] to keep their place in the top division.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kilmarnock striker Rory McKenzie admits it was sad to see youth team pals go ... but says things must change at club|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/kilmarnock-striker-rory-mckenzie-admits-8263385|publisher=Daily Record|last=Wren|first=David|date=23 June 2016|accessdate=22 October 2019}}</ref>

===Brechin City loan===
On 27 January 2012, McKenzie signed for [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] on loan until the end of the 2011–12 season.<ref>{{cite web|last=Hoey|first=John|title=Young Killie Striker Signs For City|url=http://www.brechincity.com/bcfc/servlet/BCFCFrontControllerServlet?action=News&page_id=1117&category=2|publisher=brechincity.com|date=27 January 2012|accessdate=9 December 2013}}</ref> He scored 7 goals in his stint at the club, including a double in a 2–2 draw with [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/17883944|title=Brechin City 2-2 Cowdenbeath|work=BBC Sport |date=28 April 2012 |accessdate=January 10, 2020}}</ref>

==International career==
McKenzie was selected for the [[Scotland national under-19 football team|Scotland under-19s]], making his debut in May 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_.player_profile.cfm?page=106&playerID=69652&squadID=9|title=Rory McKenzie – U19 Squad|publisher=[[Scottish Football Association]]}}</ref>

He is also eligible to play for the [[Trinidad and Tobago national football team]] through a grandmother.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/kilmarnock-s-mckenzie-pondering-trinidad-tobago-3547851|title=Kilmarnock's McKenzie pondering Trinidad & Tobago - Tribal Football|publisher=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11791/8106806/killie-striker-considers-tt|title=Killie striker considers T&T|publisher=Sky Sports|date=24 September 2012}}</ref>

'''Stephen Gerard O'Donnell''' (born 11 May 1992) is a Scottish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe}} club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] and the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]]. He has previously played for [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] and [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], and was [[Cap (sport)|capped]] once by the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21 team]] in 2013 before being selected 26 times at full level from 2018, including at the [[UEFA Euro 2020]] tournament.

==Club career==
===Early career===
A pupil at [[St Aidan's High School]] in [[Wishaw]],<ref>[https://www.tes.com/magazine/archived/scotland-players-old-schools-send-good-luck-messages Scotland players' old schools send good luck messages], Henry Hepburn, [[TES (magazine)]], 11 June 2021</ref> O'Donnell began his career as a youth player with Wishaw Wycombe Wanderers and [[Captain (association football)|captained]] the [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] under-17 team.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/school-pals-captain-celtic-aberdeen-2623131 |title=School pals captain Celtic and Aberdeen U-17s |newspaper=Daily Record |location=Glasgow |date=1 October 2008 |access-date=30 May 2018}}</ref> He then joined [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football.co.uk/hibernian/hibs-offer-trial-to-freed-celtic-youngster-stephen-odonnell/1655372 |title=Hibs offer trial to freed Celtic youngster Stephen O'Donnell |website=football.co.uk |publisher=Digital Sports Group |date=3 May 2011 |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref> where he was part of the team that won the [[Scottish Youth Cup]]<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/13218209 |title=Celtic U19 2–1 Rangers U19 (aet) |website=BBC Sport |date=27 April 2011 |access-date=10 April 2016}}</ref> and under-19 league title in 2010–11.

===Partick Thistle===
O'Donnell was released by Celtic in 2011<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/news/13226003.stephen-will-go-through-hoops-for-hero-jackie/ |title=Stephen will go through Hoops for hero Jackie |newspaper=Evening Times |location=Glasgow |date=14 September 2011 |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref> and on 23 August 2011 signed for [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] on a one-year contract after impressing on [[Trial (association football)|trial]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ptfc.co.uk/news/2011-2012/august_2011/thistle_complete_signing_of_new_defender |title=Thistle complete signing of new Defender |publisher=Partick Thistle F.C. |date=23 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160420054158/http://ptfc.co.uk/news/2011-2012/august_2011/thistle_complete_signing_of_new_defender |archive-date=20 April 2016}}</ref> He went on to make his debut on 17 September as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in a 4–0 win at home to [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].<ref name=Soccerway/> In [[2012–13 Partick Thistle F.C. season|2012–13]], O'Donnell played in 38 matches as Partick Thistle won [[Promotion and relegation|promotion]] to the [[Scottish Premiership]] and reached the final of the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]].<ref name=Soccerway/> He was named in the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#First Division 3|PFA Scotland First Division Team of the Year]] as a result of his performances.<ref name=PFATOTY1213>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/pictures-pfa-scotland-team-year-1865526 |title=In pictures: PFA Scotland Team of the Year |first=Fraser |last=Wilson |newspaper=Daily Record |location=Glasgow |date=2 May 2013 |access-date=30 May 2018}}</ref> [[File:SOD vs Limassol.jpg|thumb|right|O'Donnell playing for [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] against [[AEL Limassol]] during a friendly in 2013.]]

On 27 January 2015, [[EFL Championship|Championship]] club [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] upped an initial offer of £50,000 for O'Donnell to £125,000.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/partick-thistle-accept-125000-blackpool-5051330 |title=Partick Thistle accept £125,000 Blackpool bid for Stephen O'Donnell |first=Gavin |last=Berry |newspaper=Daily Record |location=Glasgow |date=27 January 2015 |access-date=30 May 2018}}</ref> This offer was accepted by Partick Thistle; however, O'Donnell rejected the personal terms on offer at Blackpool in favour of seeing out the remaining six months of his contract.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31004271 |title=Jags' O'Donnell rejects Blackpool |first=Kenny |last=Crawford |website=BBC Sport |date=27 January 2015 |access-date=10 April 2016}}</ref> He left Partick Thistle upon the expiry of his contract at the end of the [[2014–15 Scottish Premiership|2014–15 season]],<ref name=Luton>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33230906 |title=Stephen O'Donnell: Luton Town sign Partick Thistle defender |website=BBC Sport |date=22 June 2015 |access-date=22 June 2015}}</ref> having made 139 appearances for the club.<ref name=Soccerway/>

===Luton Town===
On 22 June 2015, O'Donnell signed a two-year contract with [[EFL League Two|League Two]] club [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]].<ref name=Luton/> He made his Luton debut in a 3–1 win at home to newly promoted Championship club [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] in the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] on 11 August.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lutontoday.co.uk/sport/football/luton-town/jacks-lad-hatters-shock-robins-2210319 |title=Jack's the lad as Hatters shock Robins |first=Mike |last=Simmonds |newspaper=Luton Today |date=11 August 2015 |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref> O'Donnell's first goal for the club was a 90th-minute winner in a 2–1 win at home to [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]] in the [[Football League Trophy]] on 1 September.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lutontoday.co.uk/sport/football/luton-town/odonnells-fluke-sends-hatters-through-2206635 |title=O'Donnell's fluke sends Hatters through |first=Mike |last=Simmonds |newspaper=Luton Today |date=1 September 2015 |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref> He finished the [[2015–16 Luton Town F.C. season|2015–16 season]] with 33 appearances and one goal.<ref name=sb1516/> O'Donnell netted his second Luton goal in [[2016–17 Luton Town F.C. season|2016–17]] from a 25-yard shot in a 1–1 draw at home to [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]] on 13 August 2016.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lutontoday.co.uk/sport/football/hatters-held-after-odonnells-stunner-1211159 |title=Hatters held after O'Donnell's stunner |newspaper=Luton Today |date=13 August 2016 |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref>

However, a loss of form saw O'Donnell lose his place in the team to academy graduate [[James Justin]] after a 2–0 defeat away to [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]] on 17 September.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lutontoday.co.uk/sport/football/odonnell-doesnt-want-hatters-youngsters-be-given-chance-his-expense-1188483 |title=O'Donnell doesn't want Hatters youngsters to be given a chance at his expense |newspaper=Luton Today |date=20 October 2016 |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref> He regained his place in the team to make his first league start in five matches after Justin suffered a calf injury in the warm up before Luton's 2–1 win away to Leyton Orient on 15 October.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lutontoday.co.uk/sport/football/odonnells-display-praised-after-late-call-orient-1189597 |title=O'Donnell's display praised after late call-up at Orient |newspaper=Luton Today |date=17 October 2016 |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref> O'Donnell lost his place once more when Justin returned from injury for Luton's 3–1 win away to [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]] in the [[FA Cup]] on 5 November, but a [[half-time]] substitute appearance in the next round at home to [[National League (division)|National League]] club [[Solihull Moors F.C.|Solihull Moors]] on 3 December saw him score twice as Luton overturned a 2–0 deficit to win 6–2.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lutontoday.co.uk/sport/football/odonnell-not-overly-worried-criticism-hatters-fans-1174193 |title=O'Donnell not overly worried by criticism from Hatters fans |newspaper=Luton Today |date=5 December 2016 |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref> He was then recalled to the [[starting lineup]] by manager [[Nathan Jones (Welsh footballer)|Nathan Jones]] for the subsequent league match at home to [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]], which resulted in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lutontoday.co.uk/sport/football/hatters-are-held-home-cumbrians-1172327 |title=Hatters are held at home by Cumbrians |newspaper=Luton Today |date=10 December 2016 |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref> O'Donnell was released when his contract expired at the end of 2016–17.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39992090 |title=Luton Town: Craig King & Dan Potts offered deals, but five depart |website=BBC Sport |date=21 May 2017 |access-date=25 June 2017}}</ref>

===Kilmarnock===
O'Donnell signed a three-year contract with Scottish Premiership club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on 4 July 2017.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40494464 |title=Stephen O'Donnell signs for Kilmarnock after release by Luton Town |website=BBC Sport |date=4 July 2017 |access-date=4 July 2017}}</ref> O'Donnell performed well following the appointment of Steve Clarke as Kilmarnock manager, and he was selected for the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] squad in May 2018. Kilmarnock offered O'Donnell a new three-year contract in August 2019, but he opted to evaluate his contract situation at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50225520 |title=Kilmarnock: Stephen O'Donnell to hold off on contract decision |website=BBC Sport |date=29 October 2019 |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref> During January 2020 [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]] made an offer for O'Donnell,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51319883 |title=Stephen O'Donnell: Oxford make approach for Kilmarnock & Scotland defender |first=Scott |last=Mullen |website=BBC Sport |date=30 January 2020 |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref> but a deal was not completed before the closure of the transfer window. He rejected a new contract with Kilmarnock at the end of the [[2019–20 Kilmarnock F.C. season|2019–20 season]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11791/11991230/stephen-odonnell-rejects-kilmarnock-deal-and-will-leave-this-summer |title=Stephen O'Donnell rejects Kilmarnock deal and will leave this summer |first=Andrew |last=Dickson |website=Sky Sports |date=19 May 2020 |access-date=19 May 2020}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
On 13 August 2020, [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] announced the signing of O'Donnell on a contract until the next transfer window.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2020/08/13/stephen-odonnell-signs-for-motherwell/ |title=Stephen O'Donnell signs for Motherwell |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |date=13 August 2020 |access-date=13 August 2020}}</ref> On 1 February 2021, he agreed a new contract with Motherwell until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2021/02/01/stephen-odonnell-extends-motherwell-deal/|title=Stephen O'Donnell extends Motherwell deal|publisher=Motherwell FC|date=1 February 2021|access-date=1 February 2021}}</ref> On 13 April 2021, O'Donnell signed a new two-year contract with Motherwell, keeping him at the club until the summer of 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=STEPHEN O'DONNELL SIGNS NEW DEAL |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2021/04/13/stephen-odonnell-signs-new-deal/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk/ |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=13 April 2021 |date=13 April 2021}}</ref>

On 3 June 2024, Motherwell announced that O'Donnell had signed a new two-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web |title=STEPHEN O'DONNELL EXTENDS HIS STAY AT THE CLUB |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2024/06/03/stephen-odonnell-extends-his-stay-at-the-club/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk/ |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |accessdate=3 June 2024 |date=3 June 2024}}</ref> On 18 March 2025, Motherwell announced that they had triggered their one-year contract extension with O'Donnell.<ref>{{cite web |title=SLATTERY AND O'DONNELL SIGN ON FOR NEXT SEASON |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2025/03/18/slattery-and-odonnell-sign-on-for-next-season/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=18 March 2025 |date=18 March 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
O'Donnell made one appearance for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21 team]] in February 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=42237 |title=Stephen O'Donnell |publisher=Scottish Football Association |access-date=30 May 2018}}</ref> He received his first call-up to the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]] in May 2018, for [[Exhibition game#Association football|friendly]] matches against [[Peru national football team|Peru]] and [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44132990 |title=Scotland: Ryan Fraser, Matt Ritchie & Barry Douglas withdraw from squad |website=BBC Sport |date=16 May 2018 |access-date=30 May 2018}}</ref> O'Donnell made his full Scotland debut on 29 May 2018, in a 2–0 defeat to Peru.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44219810 |title=Peru 2–0 Scotland |first=Alasdair |last=Lamont |website=BBC Sport |date=30 May 2018 |access-date=30 May 2018}}</ref> He retained his place in the squad for the matches in September 2018, and "excelled" in the 2–0 win against [[Albania national football team|Albania]] on 10 September.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45392473 |title=Uefa Nations League: Scotland beat Albania 2–0 in group opener |first=Tom |last=English |website=BBC Sport |date=10 September 2018 |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref>

O'Donnell was selected in the Scotland squad for [[UEFA Euro 2020]] and played in all three of their matches at the tournament.<ref name = euros/> His performance in the opening game against the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] was criticised, but was then praised after the goalless draw against [[England national football team|England]] in the second match.<ref name = euros>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57708853 |title=Stephen O'Donnell says reaction to his Euros displays 'over the top' |website=BBC Sport |date=3 July 2021 |accessdate=9 September 2021}}</ref> In September 2021 he gained his 23rd cap overall and 12th as a Motherwell player in a 1–0 away win over [[Austria national football team|Austria]] during [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification]];<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58386792|title=Austria 0–1 Scotland|website=bbc.co.uk|first=Martin|last=Watt|date=7 September 2021|access-date=10 September 2021}}</ref> as well as being praised for aspects of his performance against the highly regarded [[David Alaba]], he also equalled a long-standing Motherwell club caps record set by [[George Stevenson (footballer)|George Stevenson]] in the 1930s.<ref>{{cite news|last=Thomson|first=Paul|date=7 September 2021|title=Scotland's Stephen O'Donnell equals 87-year-old Motherwell record in Austria win|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/scotland-star-stephen-odonnell-equals-24933141|access-date=10 September 2021|website=Daily Record|language=en}}</ref>

'''Jordan McGhee''' (born 24 July 1996)<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.hydc.co.uk/jordan_mcghee.html | title=Jordan McGhee | publisher=Heart of Midlothian Youth Development Committee | work=hydc.co.uk | accessdate=10 May 2013 | url-status=dead | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120509140108/http://www.hydc.co.uk/jordan_mcghee.html | archivedate=9 May 2012 }}</ref> is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who currently plays for {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe}} club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]. He can play as either a [[Defender (association football)|defender]], both as a [[Centre Back|centre-back]] and [[Full back (association football)|full back]], or as a [[midfielder]]. He began his career at [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] and had a spell on loan at [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]]. He then spent two years at [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]], and was team captain from January 2019 until his departure in the summer of that year for [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]]. McGhee spent 6 years at the ''Dee'', earning two promotions to the [[Scottish Premiership]] and a top six finish in nearly 200 appearances before leaving the club in 2025.

==Club career==

===Heart of Midlothian===
McGhee signed for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] (Hearts) in 2007, having previously played for Claremont Boys Club.<ref name="Joy">{{cite web | url=http://www.eastkilbridenews.co.uk/lanarkshire-sport/lanarkshire-football/2012/06/20/jordan-s-joy-at-three-year-hearts-deal-68653-31216929/ | title=Jordan's joy at three-year Hearts deal | publisher=East Kilbride News | work=eastkilbridenews.co.uk | date=20 June 2012 | accessdate=10 May 2013}}</ref> In July 2012, he signed a three-year professional contract, tying him to the club until 2015.<ref name = "Joy"/> A member of the club's under-20 squad<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scotsman.com/edinburgh-evening-news/football/top-stories/gary-locke-could-give-teenager-jordan-mcghee-debut-1-2910988 | title=Gary Locke could give teenager Jordan McGhee debut | work=[[The Scotsman]] | date=26 April 2013 | accessdate=18 May 2013}}</ref> McGhee made his first team debut<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scotsman.com/edinburgh-evening-news/football/hearts/hearts-3-0-st-mirren-buddies-fall-at-tynecastle-1-2920621 | title=Hearts 3–0 St Mirren: Buddies fall at Tynecastle | work=[[The Scotsman]] | date=4 May 2013 | accessdate=19 May 2013}}</ref> aged 16,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/spl/hearts-exact-revenge-for-league-cup-misery-1-2921286 | title=Hearts exact revenge for League Cup misery | work=[[The Scotsman]] | date=6 May 2013 | accessdate=19 May 2013}}</ref> on 4 May 2013, coming on as an 86th-minute substitute at [[Tynecastle Stadium|Tynecastle]] in a [[Scottish Premier League]] match against [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], replacing [[Mehdi Taouil]] in a 3–0 win.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22320527 | title=Hearts 3–0 St Mirren | publisher=[[BBC Sport]]  | date=4 May 2013 | access-date=19 May 2013}}</ref> The following season on 24 August 2013, in only his second substitute appearance,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/hearts-2-aberdeen-1-17-year-old-2218744 | title=17-year-old McGhee hits winner to continue Jambos fightback | work=Daily Record|location=Glasgow | date=25 August 2013 | accessdate=25 August 2013}}</ref> he scored his first professional goal,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23827738 | title=Gary Locke lavishes praise on Jordan McGhee | publisher=[[BBC Sport]] | date=24 August 2013 | access-date=25 August 2013}}</ref> an 88th-minute winner in a 2–1 win over [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/scottish-premiership-hearts-v-aberdeen-2215466 | title=Jordan McGhee is the hero as brave Hearts stun Dons with late winner | work=Daily Record|location=Glasgow | date=24 August 2013 | accessdate=25 August 2013}}</ref> The following week he made his first start against [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]], in a 2–0 defeat.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23822889 | title=Inverness remain top of the Scottish Premiership following a convincing victory over 10 man Hearts | publisher=[[BBC Sport]] | date=31 August 2013 | access-date=31 August 2013}}</ref>

In January 2015, McGhee signed a contract with Hearts that was due to run until the end of the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30816413 |title=Hearts: Defender Jordan McGhee commits to new deal |publisher=BBC Sport |date=14 January 2015 |access-date=4 August 2015}}</ref> [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] made two offers of around £250,000 for McGhee in August 2015, but these were both rejected by Hearts.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33777219|title=Hearts reject Ipswich Town bids for Jordan McGhee |first=Alasdair |last=Lamont |publisher=BBC Sport  |date=4 August 2015 |access-date=4 August 2015}}</ref>

In January 2016 McGhee almost moved to [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] on loan but the move collapsed after paperwork failed to be completed in time.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jordan McGhee's move from Hearts to Middlesbrough collapses|url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/jordan-mcghee-s-move-from-hearts-to-middlesbrough-collapses-1-4017882|publisher=Edinburgh Evening News|last=Anderson|first=Barry|date=1 February 2016|access-date=11 February 2016|archive-date=23 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181123154327/https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/jordan-mcghee-s-move-from-hearts-to-middlesbrough-collapses-1-4017882|url-status=dead}}</ref> In July 2016, Middlesbrough returned to sign McGhee on a season-long loan to play in the club's [[Middlesbrough F.C. Reserves and Academy|development team]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hearts: Jordan McGhee heads for Middlesbrough as Viktor Noring is offered deal|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36706010|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mfc.co.uk/news/article/2016/boro-jordan-mcghee-hearts-heart-of-midlothian-3170079.aspx |title=Boro Take Scotland U21 Captain on Season Long Loan |publisher=Middlesbrough FC |date=5 July 2016 |accessdate=5 July 2016}}</ref>

===Falkirk===
McGhee moved to [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Falkirk F.C.|Falkirk]] in August 2017 for an undisclosed transfer fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41115639 |title=Falkirk sign defenders Jordan McGhee and Conrad Balatoni |publisher=BBC Sport |date=31 August 2017 |accessdate=31 August 2017}}</ref> He made his debut two days later on 2 September 2017, starting at centre-back as his new side defeated [[Sligo Rovers]] in the [[Scottish Challenge Cup|Challenge Cup]] 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/falkirkbairns/status/904037774575198208|title=Sligo v Falkirk line ups| publisher= Falkirk FC| date=2 September 2017}}</ref> McGhee was named as team captain in January 2019. Despite the team's best efforts, the Bairns were relegated to the [[Scottish League One]] at the end of the 2018–19 season.

===Dundee===

==== 2019–20 season ====
In June 2019, McGhee signed a two-year deal with [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], who had been relegated to the [[Scottish Championship|Championship]] the previous season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/jordan-signs/|title=Jordan Signs|date=17 June 2019|website=Dundee FC Official Website|access-date=17 June 2019}}</ref> McGhee became a key figure for the Dark Blues, impressing in a variety of different positions, scoring two important goals in consecutive games, and playing in every game until getting surgery on his hand in February 2020, which sidelined him for a couple of weeks.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/injury-bombshell-for-dundee-after-key-defensive-pair-go-under-knife/|title=Injury bombshell for Dundee after key defensive pair go under knife|last=Cran|first=George|date=7 February 2020|website=Evening Telegraph|access-date=20 April 2020}}</ref> McGhee would be voted by his teammates as Dundee's Player's Player of the Year at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/jordan-wins-players-player/|title=Jordan wins Player's Player|date=29 April 2020|website=Dundee FC|access-date=29 April 2020}}</ref> At the beginning of July, McGhee would be announced as team captain.<ref>{{Cite web|date=1 July 2020|title=Jordan McGhee appointed club captain|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/jordan-mcghee-appointed-club-captain/|access-date=1 July 2020|website=Dundee FC}}</ref>

==== 2020–21 season ====
In his second season with Dundee, McGhee would be employed further up the pitch as a [[box-to-box midfielder]] by manager [[James McPake]] and would find success in this role.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cran|first=George|date=15 December 2020|title=Dundee boss James McPake says Jordan McGhee can make box-to-box midfield slot his own and be the Dark Blues' Murray Davidson|url=https://www.eveningtelegraph.co.uk/fp/dundee-boss-james-mcpake-says-jordan-mcghee-can-make-box-to-box-midfield-slot-his-own-and-be-the-dark-blues-murray-davidson/|access-date=8 January 2021|website=eveningtelegraph.co.uk}}</ref> In January 2021, McGhee signed a two-year extension with Dundee, keeping him at the club until 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|date=8 January 2021|title=Jordan signs extension|url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/jordan-signs-extension-2/|access-date=8 January 2021|website=dundeefc.co.uk}}</ref> Later that month, McGhee would suffer a torn pectoral muscle that would require surgery and looked likely to have ended his season.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cran|first=George|date=5 February 2021|title=James McPake sees similarities between Dundee new boy Jason Cummings and ==== 2021–22 season ====
During the [[2021–22 Dundee F.C. season|2021–22 season]], McGhee would require minor surgery to fix a persistent knee issue, which would sideline him for several weeks.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cran|first=George|title=Dundee injury update: Surgery for Jordan McGhee to sort persistent knee problem, doubts over Max Anderson but positive news on Shaun Byrne and Alex Jakubiak|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/2760513/dundeefc-injury-jordan-mcghee-surgery-max-anderson-shaun-byrne-alex-jakubiak/|access-date=2021-12-06|website=The Courier|date=24 November 2021 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Dundee midfielder Jordan McGhee to miss Motherwell clash after knee surgery|url=https://www.bt.com/sport/news/2021/november/dundee-midfielder-jordan-mcghee-to-miss-motherwell-clash-after-knee-surgery|access-date=2021-12-06|website=BT.com|language=en}}</ref> Throughout the season he would return to his usual centre back role under McPake and [[Mark McGhee]], and play his most games for the club in a single season yet, though this would not be enough to avoid relegation and a return to the Championship.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee relegated from Scottish Premiership after St Johnstone beat Aberdeen |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11781/12610699/dundee-relegated-from-scottish-premiership-after-st-johnstone-beat-aberdeen |access-date=2022-08-08 |publisher=Sky Sports |language=en }}</ref>

Partick Thistle clash as Gary Bowyer provides Jordan McGhee update |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/3541612/dundee-partick-thistle-gary-bowyer-jordan-mcghee-update/ |access-date=2022-08-08 |website=The Courier |date=19 July 2022 |language=en-GB}}</ref> He would make his first appearance of the season on 20 August 2022, coming off the bench away to [[Greenock |website=The Courier |date=25 February 2023 |language=en-GB}}</ref> McGhee would mark his 100th appearance for Dundee with a clean sheet in an away victory over [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton name=":1">{{Cite news |title=Dundee back in Premiership after eight-goal epic |language=en-GB |publisher=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65420805 |access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref>

==== 2023–24 season ====
On 10 June 2023, Dundee announced that McGhee had signed a new two-year deal with the club, keeping him there until the summer of 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-10 |title=McGhee extends stay |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/mcghee-extends-stay/ |access-date=2023-06-10 |website=Dundee Football Club – Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> McGhee played his 150th game with the ''Dark Blues'' on 23 January 2024, in a comfortable away win over [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Martindale future a 'conundrum' as Dundee thrash Livingston |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68039655 |access-date=2024-01-31 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Under [[Tony Docherty]], McGhee played largely at centre back in a back 3 early on before cementing a role at [[right wing back]], and bagged a trio of goals early on in 2024, including a late winner against [[Tayside derby|local rivals]] [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dundee snatch dramatic derby win over St Johnstone |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67821044 |access-date=2024-02-11 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> McGhee's purple patch was stopped by a calf injury sidelining him for several weeks, before returning off the bench in another win over St Johnstone.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |date=2024-03-05 |title=Dundee suffer injury blow with Jordan McGhee set to miss key matches as Dens kid turns out for Scotland |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/4912944/dundee-fc-injury-blow-jordan-mcghee-miss-key-matches/ |access-date=2024-03-06 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=St Johnstone v Dundee |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68644008 |access-date=2024-03-30 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==== 2024–25 season ====
Returning to his traditional place at centre back, McGhee scored his first goal of the season on 17 August 2024 in a dominant [[Scottish League Cup|League Cup]] knockout victory over [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee vs Airdrieonians: Scottish League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4gdpz2162nt |access-date=2024-08-17 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> After being out with an injury, McGhee returned to playing in November, and came off the bench on his return to score in Dundee's comeback victory over [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee vs Kilmarnock: Scottish Premiership |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cx2n4g57w57t |access-date=2024-11-03 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 16 March 2025, McGhee scored two goals against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in Dundee's first [[Dundee derby|derby victory]] at [[Tannadice Park|Tannadice]] in over twenty years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee United vs Dundee: Scottish Premiership LIVE - line ups, updates, radio, stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cr42d1wpe9vt |access-date=2025-03-16 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> At the end of the season, after [[BBC Sport]] reported in January 2025 that McGhee had signed a pre-contract agreement with fellow [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], Dundee confirmed that McGhee was leaving the club under freedom of contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-16 |title=Jordan McGhee: Motherwell agree pre-contract with versatile Dundee player |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c74mxge9n8xo |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-21 |title=Jordan McGhee Departs |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/jordan-mcghee-thanks/ |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Motherwell ===
On 2 June 2025, Motherwell officially announced the signing of McGhee on a two-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Club |first1=Motherwell Football |last2=Gibson |first2=Scott |date=2025-06-02 |title=Jordan McGhee arrives in ML1 |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2025/06/02/jordan-mcghee-arrives-in-ml1/ |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=Motherwell Football Club |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-02 |title=Jordan McGhee joins Motherwell following Dundee exit |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c62v6dypgp4o |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==International career==
McGhee earned caps at under-15, [[Scotland national under-16 football team|under-16]] and [[Scotland national under-18 football team|under-18]] level before earning a call up to the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] squad aged just 17 after some impressive performances for Hearts.

After establishing himself as a regular at centre back alongside [[Stuart Findlay]], he captained the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21]] side for the first time in a friendly against [[Switzerland national under-21 football team|Switzerland]] on 18 November 2014 which ended in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite web|title=Switzerland 1–1 Scotland|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/international_fixture_details.cfm?page=1921&matchid=147876|publisher=Scottish Football Association|date=18 November 2014}}</ref>

'''Greg Kiltie''' (born 18 January 1997) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] for [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].

==Early life==
Kiltie was born in [[Irvine, North Ayrshire|Irvine]].<ref name = "KFC">{{cite web|url=http://www.kilmarnockfc.co.uk/TeamsPlayer?sPlayer=469&sTeam=398|title=Profile|access-date=6 September 2015|publisher=Kilmarnock F.C.}}</ref> As a nine-year-old child he was a mascot in the Brazil-Australia group game at the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]], after winning a competition organised by the ''[[Sunday Mail (Scotland)|Sunday Mail]]''.<ref name = "DR">{{cite web|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/news/real-life/killie-starlet-greg-kiltie-reveals-3175379|title=Killie starlet Greg Kiltie reveals he hit the big time as a kid at World Cup in 2006 thanks to Sunday Mail|date=23 February 2014|access-date=6 September 2015|author=Norman Silvester|work=Daily Record}}</ref> His father Jim is a BT engineer.<ref name = "DR"/>

==Club career==
He signed a professional contract with [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] at the age of 16.<ref name = "KFC"/> He made his senior debut for Kilmarnock on 18 May 2013, as they lost 3–1 at home to [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in a [[Scottish Premier League]] game.<ref name = "DR"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22491346|title=Kilmarnock 1–3 St Mirren|date=18 May 2013|access-date=6 September 2015|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/kilmarnock/257607-fourteen-for-14-meet-kilmarnocks-next-rising-star-greg-kiltie/|title=Fourteen for '14: Meet Kilmarnock's next rising star Greg Kiltie|date=23 December 2013|access-date=6 September 2015|author=Scott McClymont|publisher=STV}}</ref> His debut came at the age of 16 years and four months, making him Kilmarnock's youngest player for 50 years.<ref name = "DR"/>

On 3 October 2014, Kiltie signed for [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] on a one-month loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.qosfc.com/content-news.aspx?newsid=2503|title=Greg Kiltie Signs on Loan|date=3 October 2014|access-date=6 September 2015|publisher=Queen of the South F.C.}}</ref>

During the [[2016–17 Kilmarnock F.C. season|2016–17 season]], Kiltie was out for six months following knee surgery in October,<ref>{{cite web|title=Lillie ace Greg Kiltie raring to go after injury he'll scuppered his season|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/killie-ace-greg-kiltie-raring-10220987.amp|website=Daily Record|date=13 April 2017|access-date=1 August 2017}}</ref> then on 20 May 2017, during Kilmarnock's final match of the season against [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] he was injured during the first half.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kilmarnock 1–2 Ross County|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39905633|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Sutherland|first=Jonathan|date=20 May 2017|access-date=1 August 2017}}</ref> It was later announced he had suffered a broken ankle and following an operation, he was not able to play again for seven months.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/42391474|title=Scottish Gossip: Celtic, Hearts, Rangers, Ross County, Hamilton, Kilmarnock, Chelsea, Dundee, Preston|work=BBC Sport |date=18 December 2017}}</ref>

In January 2019 he moved on loan to [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Morton sign Kilmarnock star Greg Kiltie on loan|url=https://www.greenocktelegraph.co.uk/news/17395805.morton-sign-kilmarnock-star-greg-kiltie-on-loan/|date=30 January 2019|access-date=6 February 2019|author=Adam Thomas|website=Greenock Telegraph}}</ref>

Kiltie moved on a season-long loan to [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on 2 September 2019, with both clubs having a recall option on the loan in January.<ref>{{cite web|title=GREG KILTIE SIGNED FROM KILLIE|url=https://dafc.co.uk/story.php?t=Greg_Kiltie_signed_from_Killie&ID=11436|publisher=Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|date=2 September 2019|access-date=3 September 2019}}</ref> Kiltie said that he made the move after Kilmarnock manager [[Angelo Alessio]] didn't give him a "fair chance".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49577383|title=Greg Kiltie: Kilmarnock's Angelo Alessio did not give me 'a fair chance' before Dunfermline move|work=BBC Sport |date=4 September 2019}}</ref> While on loan at Dunfermline, Kiltie scored the opener in a 3–2 win against his parent club's rivals [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]] on 19 October 2019.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50024540|title=Dunfermline Athletic 3-2 Ayr United: First home win of season for Pars|work=BBC Sport |date=19 October 2019|access-date=20 October 2019}}</ref> Kiltie returned to his parent club in January 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/officialdafc/status/1215272515318231042|title=Thanks Greg|last=Dunfermline Athletic|date=9 January 2020|website=Twitter|access-date=9 January 2020}}</ref> On 1 June 2020 he signed a new one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/trio-extend-deals-for-2020-2021-season/|title=Trio extend deals for 2020/2021 season|date=1 June 2020}}</ref> He left Kilmarnock in June 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/player-update-as-broadfoot-kiltie-and-lafferty-depart/|title=Player Update as Broadfoot, Kiltie and Lafferty depart|date=4 June 2021}}</ref>

He signed for [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on 6 June 2021, on a two-year contract.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57387411|title=Forwards Main & Kiltie join St Mirren|work=BBC Sport }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-transfer-news/greg-kiltie-agrees-st-mirren-24267408|title=Greg Kiltie agrees St Mirren transfer after leaving Kilmarnock|first=Scott|last=Burns|date=7 June 2021|website=Daily Record}}</ref>

Kilt re-signed for [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in June 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/greg-kiltie-returns-to-kilmarnock/|title=Greg Kiltie returns to Kilmarnock|first=Lochlin|last=Highet|date=17 June 2025|website=Kilmarnock FC}}</ref>

==International career==
Kiltie has represented Scotland at every youth international level from [[Scotland national under-15 football team|under-15]] to [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/football_player_profile.cfm?page=1848&playerID=126623&squadID=13|title=Profile|access-date=6 September 2015|publisher=Scottish FA}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=2986&newsCategoryID=6&newsID=13947|title=Under-19 squad announced for Dutch friendly|date=31 October 2014|access-date=6 September 2015|publisher=Scottish FA}}</ref>

'''Paul McGinn''' (born 22 October 1990) is a Scottish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|right-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe}} club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], whom he captains, and for the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland national team]].

Starting his career at [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]] in the youth team, McGinn has spent the majority of his career playing in Scotland. After leaving Queen's Park in 2012, he played for [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]] and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]], as well as a stint at English club [[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]], before joining [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] in 2022. He made his Scotland debut in 2021.

==Career ==

===Queen's Park===
Raised in [[Clydebank]],<ref name=making>{{cite web|url= https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/making-john-mcginn-how-aston-20905748|title= The making of John McGinn and how Aston Villa star defied fears he'd never make it|work=Daily Record |date=18 November 2019|access-date=16 September 2020}}</ref> McGinn started his career as a youth player at [[Queen's Park F.C.|Queen's Park]]. He made his debut on 2 May 2009, in Queen's Park's 1–0 defeat to [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]]. Having come on as a substitute, he was sent off in the 90th minute.<ref>{{cite web|title=Champs see off the Spiders|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/champs-see-off-the-spiders-2610684|publisher=Rutherglen Reformer|date=6 May 2009|access-date=23 August 2014}}</ref>

===St Mirren===
On 18 September 2012, McGinn signed for [[Scottish Premier League]] side [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/mcginn-follows-in-the-family-tradition-by-joining-st-mirren.18917292 | title=McGinn follows in the family tradition by joining St Mirren | work=The Herald|location=Glasgow | date=19 September 2012 | access-date=5 April 2013}}</ref> until the end of the season, despite interest from [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]]<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/aberdeen-leading-race-to-sign-queens-1165873 | title=Aberdeen leading race to sign Queen's Park star Paul McGinn | work=Daily Record|location=Glasgow | date=2 July 2012 | access-date=5 April 2013}}</ref> and [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.express.co.uk/sport/football/330471/Dundee-United-target-Queen-s-Park-Paul-McGinn | title=Dundee United target Queen's Park Paul McGinn | work=[[Daily Express]] | date=3 July 2012 | access-date=5 April 2013}}</ref> On 24 November 2012, he went out on loan to former his club Queen's Park.<ref name="On Loan">{{cite web | url=http://www.saintmirren.net/pages/?p=17809 | title=Players Out on Loan | publisher=[[St Mirren F.C.]] | work=saintmirren.net | date=24 November 2012 | access-date=5 April 2013 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140104000135/http://www.saintmirren.net/pages/?p=17809 | archive-date=4 January 2014 }}</ref> The loan was necessary to give him game time, as he was registered as an amateur and unable to play in the SPL until January.<ref name="On Loan"/> He then finished the season on loan to [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]].<ref>{{cite web|title=McGinn Signs|url=http://www.dumbartonfootballclub.com/news/?mode=view&id=806|publisher=Dumbarton F.C.|last=Findlay|first=Alan|date=31 January 2013|access-date=23 August 2014}}</ref> Despite being offered a new contract, McGinn opted to leave St Mirren at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=McGinn opts to leave St Mirren|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/mcginn-opts-to-leave-st-mirren/|publisher=Scottish Professional Football League|date=22 May 2013|access-date=23 August 2014}}</ref>

===Dumbarton===
After his successful loan spell, on 4 June 2013, McGinn agreed a one-year deal with [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dumbarton sign Paul McGinn from St Mirren|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22763017|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 June 2013|access-date=23 August 2014}}</ref> In all he made 42 appearances in all competitions that season<ref>{{Soccerbase season|51423|2013|name=Paul McGinn|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref> as the side finished fifth in the [[2013–14 Scottish Championship|Scottish Championship]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://spfl.co.uk/championship/archive/2013-2014/ | title=SPFL Archive 2013/2014 | publisher=[[Scottish Professional Football League]] | work=spfl.co.uk | access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref> McGinn was also named as part of the [[PFA Scotland Team of the Year#Championship|2013–14 PFA Scotland Scottish Championship Team of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27080275 | title=Falkirk and Rangers dominate team of the year voting | publisher=[[BBC Sport]] | date=18 April 2014 | access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref>

===Dundee===
On 20 June 2014, McGinn was persuaded by [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] manager [[Paul Hartley]] to sign a two-year contract alongside former St Mirren teammate [[Paul McGowan (footballer)|Paul McGowan]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Double Paul Signing|url=http://dundeefc.co.uk/news/double-paul-signing|publisher=Dundee F.C.|date=20 June 2014|access-date=23 August 2014}}</ref> He made his debut on 2 August 2014, as Dundee beat [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]] 4–0 in the [[Scottish League Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dundee vs Peterhead|url=http://www.dundeefc.co.uk/fixtures-and-results/dundee-vs-peterhead|publisher=Dundee F.C.|last=Christie|first=James|date=2 August 2014|access-date=23 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923220925/http://www.dundeefc.co.uk/fixtures-and-results/dundee-vs-peterhead|archive-date=23 September 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Chesterfield===
On 22 June 2016, McGinn signed a two-year contract with English club [[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]] after his Dundee contract expired.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chesterfield-fc.co.uk/news/article/scottish-defender-signs-3149170.aspx|title=Scottish defender signs|publisher=Chesterfield FC|date=22 June 2016|access-date=22 June 2016|archive-date=24 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160624195733/http://www.chesterfield-fc.co.uk/news/article/scottish-defender-signs-3149170.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Chesterfield in a 3–1 [[EFL Cup]] loss against [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]] on 9 August 2016.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36949944|title=Rochdale 3-1 Chesterfield|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=9 August 2016|access-date=9 August 2016}}</ref> On 25 August 2017 he left the club, with his contract being cancelled by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite web|title=Defender Departs|url=https://www.chesterfield-fc.co.uk/news/2017/august/20170825-defender-departs/|publisher=Chesterfield F.C.|date=25 August 2017|access-date=26 August 2017|archive-date=25 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825225911/https://www.chesterfield-fc.co.uk/news/2017/august/20170825-defender-departs/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Partick Thistle===
McGinn returned to Scottish football on 31 August 2017, signing a one-year contract with [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41116091 |title=Partick Thistle: Paul McGinn joins Premiership outfit after Chesterfield exit |publisher=BBC Sport  |date=31 August 2017 |access-date=31 August 2017}}</ref> Thistle were relegated from the [[Scottish Premiership]], via the playoffs, in his only season with the club.

===St Mirren (second spell)===
McGinn returned to [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] in May 2018, signing a two-year contract. He agreed a deal with the club while the manager position was vacant; [[Alan Stubbs]] took over in June 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/1893-paul-mcginn-signs-with-saints |title=Paul McGinn signs with Saints |publisher=St Mirren FC |date=25 May 2018 |access-date=25 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180526041755/https://www.stmirren.com/news/club/all-news/1893-paul-mcginn-signs-with-saints |archive-date=26 May 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Hibernian===
McGinn signed an 18-month contract with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on 31 January 2020, moving from St Mirren for an undisclosed transfer fee.<ref name = mcginn>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51286784 |title=Paul McGinn: Hibs sign defender from St Mirren for undisclosed fee |publisher=BBC Sport |date=31 January 2020 |access-date=31 January 2020}}</ref> He was added to the [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] international squad in October 2020, after six players dropped out of the initial selection due to injuries and [[COVID-19]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54477749 |title=Scotland calls for Aberdeen's Andrew Considine and Hibernian's Paul McGinn |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 October 2020 |access-date=9 October 2020}}</ref> On the same day as his international selection, McGinn agreed an extended contract with Hibernian.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/paul-mcginn-and-hibs-celebrate-scotland-call-and-new-contract-2999029 |title=Paul McGinn and Hibs celebrate Scotland call-up and new contract |first=Moira |last=Gordon |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=9 October 2020 |access-date=9 October 2020}}</ref> McGinn scored his first goals for Hibs, and his first since April 2019, when he scored twice in a 2–2 draw with [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on 24 November.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/scotland/article/paul-mcginn-ends-goal-drought-to-twice-foil-lively-st-johnstone-dx93phs92 |title=Paul McGinn ends goal drought to twice foil lively St Johnstone |first=Alison |last=McConnell |newspaper=[[The Times]] |date=25 November 2020 |access-date=25 November 2020}}</ref>

On 18 September 2021, McGinn scored against his former club [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] during a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58525350|title=Hibernian 2–2 St Mirren|publisher=BBC|first=Matthew|last=Reed|date=18 September 2021|access-date=18 September 2021}}</ref> His appearances for Hibs during the 2021–22 season triggered a one-year extension to his contract, but he was allowed to leave by mutual consent soon afterwards.<ref name = well>{{cite web |title=Paul McGinn: Motherwell sign right-back 20 days after Hibernian contract extension |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61903616 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=22 June 2022 |access-date=22 June 2022}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
After leaving Hibs, McGinn signed a one-year contract with [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref name = well/>

On 24 May 2024, McGinn extended his contract with Motherwell until the summer of 2025.<ref>{{cite web |title=2023/24 END OF SEASON SQUAD UPDATE |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2024/05/24/2023-24-end-of-season-squad-update/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=24 May 2024 |date=24 May 2024}}</ref> On 9 May 2025, Motherwell announced that McGinn had extended his contract until the end of the 2025/26 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Paul McGinn remains for 2025/26 season |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2025/05/09/paul-mcginn-remains-for-2025-26-season/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=9 May 2025 |date=9 May 2025}}</ref> On 1 January 2026, McGinn again extended his contract with Motherwell, this time until the summer of 2027.<ref>{{cite web |title=McGinn extends his stay at Fir Park |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/01/01/mcginn-extends-his-stay-at-fir-park/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=2 January 2026 |date=1 January 2026}}</ref>

==International career==

In October 2020, McGinn received his first national team call-up from [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]], but he failed to make an appearance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edinburghlive.co.uk/sport/football/stephen-mcginn-paul-scotland-hibs-19080131|title=Hibs' Stephen McGinn reveals 'immense pride' at brother Paul's Scotland call up|work=edinburghlive.co.uk|date=9 October 2020|access-date=6 September 2021}}</ref>

On 6 September 2021, McGinn was called up for Scotland for a second time following three players' withdrawal from the squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denbighshirefreepress.co.uk/sport/national/19560969.hibs-defender-paul-mcginn-gets-scotland-call-up-trio-withdraw-squad/|title=Hibs defender Paul McGinn gets Scotland call-up after trio withdraw from squad|website=denbighshirefreepress.co.uk|date=6 September 2021|access-date=6 September 2021}}</ref> On 7 September, McGinn came off the bench to make his international debut against [[Austria national football team|Austria]] in [[Vienna]], where Scotland won 1–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58386792|title=Austria 0–1 Scotland|publisher=BBC|first=Martin|last=Watt|date=7 September 2021|access-date=7 September 2021}}</ref> His brother John was already on the field, and they became only the third siblings to play together for the national team since the end of [[World War II]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/who-were-the-last-brothers-to-play-for-scotland-before-paul-and-john-mcginn-hibs-and-rangers-players-63-year-record-broken-by-caldwell-siblings-3375560%3famp|title=Who were the last brothers to play for Scotland before Paul and John McGinn? Hibs and Rangers players' 63-year record broken by Caldwell siblings|work=The Scotsman |date=8 September 2021|access-date=10 September 2021}}</ref> It was also the first occasion that he and Scotland captain [[Andy Robertson]] had played together since their time in the fourth tier of Scottish football with Queen's Park eight years earlier.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/andrew-robertson-and-paul-mcginns-last-game-together-before-steering-scotland-to-crucial-1-0-win-over-austria-in-qatar-2022-world-cup-qualifier-3375159|title=Andrew Robertson and Paul McGinn's last game together before steering Scotland to crucial 1-0 win over Austria in Qatar 2022 World Cup qualifier|work=The Scotsman |date=8 September 2021|access-date=10 September 2021}}</ref>

'''Regan Evans Charles-Cook''' (born 14 February 1997) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[winger (association football)|winger]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]. Born in England, he plays for the [[Grenada national football team|Grenada national team]].

==Club career==
===Charlton Athletic===
Following a move from [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in 2013, Charles-Cook made his professional debut for [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] on 11 August 2015, playing 90 minutes at right back in a 4–1 [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] victory over [[Dagenham & Redbridge F.C.|Dagenham & Redbridge]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33769182 |title=Charlton Athletic 4–1 Dagenham & Redbridge |publisher=BBC Sport |date=11 August 2015 |access-date=5 January 2017}}</ref>

On 4 February 2017, Charles-Cook joined [[National League (division)|National League]] side [[Solihull Moors F.C.|Solihull Moors]] on loan for the remainder of the campaign.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Charlton Athletic midfielder Regan Charles-Cook joins Solihull Moors on loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38867449 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=4 February 2017 |accessdate=21 September 2017}}</ref> A week later, during his debut for Solihull, Charles-Cook scored twice against [[Sutton United F.C.|Sutton United]] in their 3–0 victory.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Solihull Moors 3-0 Sutton United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38865490 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=11 February 2017 |accessdate=21 September 2017}}</ref> On 17 April 2017, Charles-Cook sealed Solihull Moors' 3–1 away victory against [[Macclesfield Town F.C.|Macclesfield Town]], netting the third goal in the 93rd minute.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Macclesfield Town 1-3 Solihull Moors |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39550236 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=17 April 2017 |accessdate=21 September 2017}}</ref> Charles-Cook returned to Charlton following the conclusion of the campaign, in which he scored four times in thirteen games.

Following an impressive loan spell with Solihull, Charles-Cook returned to Charlton for the 2017–18 pre-season. He scored his first goal for Charlton in a 2–1 [[EFL Cup]] win against [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]] on 8 August 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40785775|title=Exeter 1-2 Charlton|publisher=BBC|date=8 August 2017|accessdate=14 August 2017}}</ref>

On 1 September 2017, Charles-Cook joined [[Woking F.C.|Woking]] on loan until January 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Midfielder joins from Charlton Athletic |url=https://www.wokingfc.co.uk/news/article/5938/midfielder-joins-from-charlton-athletic/ |publisher=Woking Official Site |date=1 September 2017 |accessdate=1 September 2017}}</ref> A day later, Charles-Cook made his Woking debut during their 3–1 away victory against Macclesfield Town, replacing [[Jason Banton]] in the 60th minute.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Macclesfield Town 1-3 Woking |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41058499 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 September 2017 |accessdate=4 September 2017}}</ref> On 16 September 2017, Charles-Cook scored both goals in Woking's 2–0 home victory over local rivals, Sutton United.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Woking 2-0 Sutton United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41210163 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=16 September 2017 |accessdate=21 September 2017}}</ref> In January 2018, Charles-Cook returned to Charlton after sustaining a long-term ankle injury whilst at Woking. On 8 March 2018, Charles-Cook rejoined Woking on loan until 28 April 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Charles-Cook returns to Woking on loan |url=https://www.cafc.co.uk/news/view/5aa150034ad27/charles-cook-returns-to-woking-on-loan |publisher=Charlton Athletic Official Site |date=8 March 2018 |accessdate=8 March 2018}}</ref> A day later, he marked his return, assisting Charlie Carter for his tenth goal of the season in Woking's 3–1 home defeat against [[F.C. Halifax Town]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Woking 1-3 FC Halifax Town |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43267357 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=10 March 2018 |accessdate=20 March 2018}}</ref>

===Gillingham===
Charles-Cook reportedly signed a new one-year contract with Charlton at the end of the [[2017–18 Charlton Athletic F.C. season|2017-18 season]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44168640|title=Ahmed Kashi: Charlton Athletic in contract talks with Algerian midfielder|date=18 May 2018|accessdate=18 May 2018|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> however shortly afterwards he signed for [[Gillingham F.C.|Gillingham]] on 30 May 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44303656|title=Regan Charles-Cook: Gillingham sign Charlton midfielder|date=30 May 2018|accessdate=30 May 2018|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

===Ross County===
On 30 June 2020, Charles-Cook joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news/archive/club-news-charles-cook-joins-county/|title=Charles-Cook joins County|date=30 June 2020|accessdate=30 June 2020|publisher=Ross County|archive-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630121132/https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news/archive/club-news-charles-cook-joins-county/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He struggled in his first season, with him citing homesickness and not being able to visit his family due to [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 restrictions]] as factors, and was in and out of the team.<ref name="ross1">{{cite news |last=Fraser |first=Alistair |title=Winger Regan Charles-Cook now settled at Ross County after difficult start |url=https://www.ross-shirejournal.co.uk/sport/winger-now-settled-after-difficult-start-253455/ |access-date=31 January 2022 |issue=Ross-shire Journal |date=8 October 2021}}</ref> His second season saw him become a regular in the side under new manager [[Malky MacKay]],<ref name="ross1"/> with his improved form seeing him linked with moves to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Henderson |first1=Andrew |title=Regan Charles-Cook feels happy playing with Ross County as contract close to expiry |url=https://www.ross-shirejournal.co.uk/sport/charles-cook-feels-happy-playing-with-ross-county-as-contrac-264294/ |access-date=31 January 2022 |work=Ross-shire Journal |date=28 January 2022}}</ref> On 28 January 2022, he scored one of Ross County's goals in a 3–3 draw with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]], making him at the time the top goalscorer in the [[Scottish Premiership]] on 10 goals.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Skinner |first1=Andy |title=Regan Charles-Cook vows to give all for Ross County amid transfer speculation |url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/ross-county/3899667/regan-charles-cook-vows-to-give-all-for-ross-county-amidst-transfer-speculation/ |access-date=31 January 2022 |work=The Press & Journal |date=30 January 2022}}</ref>

===Eupen===
On 8 June 2022, Charles-Cook joined [[Belgian First Division A]] side [[K.A.S. Eupen|Eupen]] on a free transfer, signing a three-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.as-eupen.be/kas-eupen-engagiert-linksaussen-regan-charles-cook/|title=KAS Eupen engagiert Linksaußen Regan Charles-Cook|publisher=[[K.A.S. Eupen]]|date= 8 June 2022|accessdate=8 June 2022|language=German}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
On 22 August 2025, [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] announced that Charles-Cook had signed with the club on a two year deal, marking his return to the Scottish Premiership.<ref>{{cite web |title=Motherwell add Regan Charles-Cook to ranks |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2025/08/22/motherwell-add-regan-charles-cook-to-ranks/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |access-date=24 August 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
On 1 July 2021, Charles-Cook was called up to [[Grenada national football team|Grenada]]'s squad for the [[2021 CONCACAF Gold Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/ross-county/3282172/ross-county-proud-as-harry-paton-and-regan-charles-cook-score-gold-cup-call-ups/|title= Ross County proud as Harry Paton and Regan Charles-Cook score Gold Cup call-ups|publisher=Press and Journal|access-date=1 July 2021|date=1 July 2021}}</ref> He started all three matches as Grenada exited at the group stage, making his debut in the side's opening game of the tournament, a 4–0 defeat to [[Honduras national football team|Honduras]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Honduras vs. Grenada – Football Match Line-Ups – July 13, 2021 – ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/lineups/_/gameId/602714|access-date=15 July 2021|publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Charles-Cook was born in England and is of Jamaican and Grenadian descent. He is the brother of fellow professional footballers [[Anthony Cook (footballer)|Anthony Cook]], [[Roman Charles-Cook]] and [[Reice Charles-Cook]];<ref>{{cite web| url = http://fullcontactlaw.co.uk/player/regan-charles-cook/| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150826221702/http://fullcontactlaw.co.uk/player/regan-charles-cook| archive-date = 26 August 2015| title = Regan Charles-Cook}}</ref> they grew up with two other brothers in [[Beckenham]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61114228 Regan Charles-Cook: Ross County's Premiership top scorer on rise from rock bottom], Jamie Lyall, BBC Sport, 10 May 2022</ref> Charles-Cook's uncle, [[James Cook (boxer)|James Cook]], is a former British [[super middleweight]] [[boxing]] champion.<ref>{{Cite news |title=ClaretArmy Q&A with Anthony Cook |url=https://www.claretarmy.co.uk/claretarmy-qa-with-anthony-cook/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200326021534/https://www.claretarmy.co.uk/claretarmy-qa-with-anthony-cook/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=26 March 2020 |publisher=Claret Army |date=12 April 2013 |accessdate=26 March 2020}}</ref>

'''John "Johnny" Koutroumbis''' (born 6 March 1998) is an [[Australians|Australian]] professional [[Association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Defender (football)|right back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe}} club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].

==Club career==
===Newcastle Jets===
After initially signing with [[Newcastle Jets FC|Newcastle Jets]] as an injury replacement for [[Daniel Alessi]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.newcastlejets.com.au/article/news-jets-welcome-johnny-koutroumbis/10ug37kfv07ge1hozfjmy6t40c|title=Jets welcome Johnny Koutrombis|publisher=[[Newcastle Jets FC|Newcastle Jets]]|date=22 October 2016|access-date=2 February 2017|archive-date=22 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161022091515/http://www.newcastlejets.com.au/article/news-jets-welcome-johnny-koutroumbis/10ug37kfv07ge1hozfjmy6t40c|url-status=dead}}</ref> on 2 February 2017, Newcastle Jets signed Koutroumbis on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/4443075/johnnys-cash-jets-re-sign-rookie-koutroumbis/?cs=306|title=Rookie Johnny Koutroumbis earns new deal with Newcastle Jets|first=James|last=Gardiner|newspaper=[[The Newcastle Herald]]|date=2 February 2017}}</ref> He mutually terminated his contract with the club in July 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newcastlejetsfc.com.au/news/koutroumbis-donachie-and-otoole-depart-jets|title=Koutroumbis, Donachie and O'Toole depart Jets|website=[[Newcastle Jets FC|Newcastle Jets]]|date=16 July 2021}}</ref>

===Western Sydney Wanderers===
In July 2021, Koutroumbis joined [[Western Sydney Wanderers FC|Western Sydney Wanderers]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wswanderersfc.com.au/news/koutroumbis-red-black|title=Koutroumbis is Red & Black|website=[[Western Sydney Wanderers FC|Western Sydney Wanderers]]|date=26 July 2021}}</ref> After making 17 league appearances, his contract was mutually terminated in July 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wswanderersfc.com.au/news/koutroumbis-departs-the-wanderers|title=Koutroumbis departs the Wanderers|website=[[Western Sydney Wanderers FC|Western Sydney Wanderers]]|date=29 July 2022}}</ref>

===Perth Glory===

On 29 July 2022, Koutroumbis signed for [[Perth Glory FC|Perth Glory]] on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://perthglory.com.au/news/versatile-defender-koutroumbis-joins-glory-on-two-year-deal|title=Versatile defender Koutroumbis joins Glory on two-year deal|first=Gareth|last=Morgan|website=[[Perth Glory FC|Perth Glory]]|date=29 July 2022}}</ref> He made 40 appearances for the club, before departing at the end of the [[2023–24 Perth Glory FC season|2023–24 season]], upon the end of his contract, in order to pursue an overseas opportunity.<ref name="28MayGlorydepartures">{{cite web|url=https://perthglory.com.au/news/alm-player-departures-confirmed/|title=ALM player departures confirmed|first=Gareth|last=Morgan|website=[[Perth Glory FC|Perth Glory]]|date=28 May 2024}}</ref>

=== Motherwell ===
On 15 June 2024, it was announced that Koutroumbis would join [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]] on 1 July, signing a two-year contract.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=15 June 2024 |title=Motherwell sign Johnny Koutroumbis after Perth Glory exit |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c7229r0r84po |access-date=23 June 2024 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 3 April 2026, Motherwell announced that they had extended their contract with Koutroumbis until the summer of 2028.<ref>{{cite web |title=Contract Extension for Johnny Koutroumbis |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/04/03/contract-extension-for-johnny-koutroumbis/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=4 April 2026 |date=3 April 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Born in Australia, Koutroumbis is of [[Greek Australians|Greek descent]].<ref name=":1" />

In 2018, Koutrombis was temporarily sidelined after being diagnosed with [[Stage-1 cancer|stage 1]] [[thyroid cancer]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=https://neoskosmos.com/en/122832/the-greek-australians-looking-to-light-up-the-2018-19-a-league-and-w-league-seasons/|title=The Greek Australians looking to light up the 2018/19 A-League and W-League seasons - Neos Kosmos|first=Con|last=Stamocostas|date=19 October 2018|website=English Edition}}</ref>

'''Jamie Brandon''' (born 5 February 1998) is a Scottish footballer who plays as a [[right-back]], [[midfielder]] or [[Midfielder#Winger|right winger]] for Premiership club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref name = "Peterhead"/> Brandon has previously played for [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]], [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]], and [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]].

==Career==
===Heart of Midlothian===
Brandon began his football career with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] at the age of 6, before signing his first professional contract in May 2015.<ref name="six">{{Cite web |url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/13308527.Rangers_kid_signs_for_Ibrox_club___then_sets_sights_on_breaking_into_first_team/|title=Rangers kid signs for Ibrox club - then sets sights on breaking into first team |website=eveningtimes.co.uk |publisher=[[Evening Times]] |date=21 May 2015 |access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref> He was released by Rangers in May 2016,<ref name="Eight Academy Players To Leave">{{cite news | url=http://rangers.co.uk/news/academy-news/eight-academy-players-leave/| work=Rangers.co.uk|publisher=Rangers Football Club|first=Alice |last=Hedworth| title=Eight Academy Players To Leave| date=4 May 2016}}</ref> before joining [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]<ref name="FIVE JOIN U20S">{{cite news | url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/5200 | title=Five join U20s| date=13 June 2016| publisher=Heart of Midlothian Football Club|work=Heartsfc.co.uk}}</ref> alongside fellow youth [[Rory Currie]].<ref name="debut">{{Cite web |url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/jamie-brandon-making-my-debut-against-celtic-was-all-i-d-hoped-for-1-4453839 |title=Jamie Brandon: Making my debut against Celtic was all I'd hoped for |website=edinburghnews.scotsman.com |publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |date=23 May 2017 |access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref>

Brandon made his professional debut for Hearts on 21 May 2017,<ref name="unbeaten">{{Cite web |url=https://www.eveningexpress.co.uk/pipe/sport/celtic-beat-hearts-to-end-the-season-as-unbeaten-champions/ |title=Celtic beat Hearts to end the season as unbeaten champions |website=eveningexpress.co.uk |publisher=[[Evening Express (Scotland)|Evening Express]] |date=21 May 2017 |access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref> playing from the start in a 2–0 defeat against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] at [[Celtic Park]].<ref name="wing">{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39911911 |title=Champions Celtic beat Hearts to become the first team to complete a Scottish top-flight season unbeaten for 118 years. |website=bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=21 May 2017 |access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref> Having played in every pre-season friendly at the start of the [[2017–18 Heart of Midlothian F.C. season|2017–18]] season,<ref name="rise">{{Cite web |url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/15405009.Ex_Ibrox_kid_Jamie_Brandon_on_the_rise_at_Hearts/?ref=rss |title=Ex-Ibrox kid Jamie Brandon on the rise at Hearts |website=eveningtimes.co.uk |publisher=[[Evening Times]] |date=12 July 2017 |access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref> his next appearance<ref name="stats">{{Soccerbase season|93361|2017|name=Jamie Brandon Stats|access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref> was in the League Cup against [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]] on 29 July 2017.<ref name="Dunfermline">{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40760158 |title=Hearts were knocked out of the Scottish League Cup after drawing with second-tier Dunfermline Athletic, who progress from round one as Group B winners |website=bbc.co.uk/sport |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=29 July 2017 |access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref> He had been due to appear as a substitute in the previous game versus [[Peterhead F.C.|Peterhead]], however was not allowed to enter the field of play due to an error on the teamsheet.<ref name="Peterhead">{{Cite web |url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/jamie-brandon-determined-to-survive-hectic-start-at-hearts-1-4524632 |title=Jamie Brandon determined to survive hectic start at Hearts |website=edinburghnews.scotsman.com |publisher=[[Edinburgh Evening News]] |date=8 August 2017 |access-date=8 August 2017 |archive-date=8 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808235206/http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/jamie-brandon-determined-to-survive-hectic-start-at-hearts-1-4524632 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 10 January 2022, Brandon was loaned to [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Greenock Morton F.C.|Greenock Morton]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Brandon's Morton move {{!}} Heart Of Midlothian Football Club|url=https://www.heartsfc.co.uk/news/article/brandons-morton-move|access-date=2022-01-10|website=www.heartsfc.co.uk}}</ref>

===Livingston===
On 10 May 2022, Brandon signed a pre-contract agreement to join [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on a free transfer upon the expiration of his Hearts contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://livingstonfc.co.uk/jamie-brandon-signs-pre-contract-with-the-lions/|title=Jamie Brandon signs pre-contract with the Lions!|website=livingstonfc.co.uk|date=10 May 2022}}</ref>

===International===
Brandon made his debut for the [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21 team]] in March 2019.<ref name=mex19>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/scotland-u21s-0-mexico-u22s-14173946|title=Scotland U21s 0 Mexico U22s 0 as Mikey Johnston misses last-gasp penalty - 3 talking points|work=Daily Record|date=22 March 2019|accessdate=23 March 2019 }}</ref>
