==Club career==
Born in [[Warsaw]],<ref name = "90m">{{90minut|22380}}</ref> Stryjek began playing football for his school at the age of 6.<ref name = "Echo"/> He signed for [[Polonia Warsaw]] at the age of 11. He moved to English club [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] in 2013, following a trial with the club.<ref name = "Echo"/>

He spent a loan spell with [[Boston United F.C.|Boston United]] in 2015, making 10 league and 2 cup appearances for them.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bostonunited.co.uk/teams/24809/player/max-stryjek-1455436/24504|title=Profile|accessdate=2 September 2017|publisher=Boston United F.C.}}</ref> In February 2016 he signed a new contract with Sunderland, lasting until 2019,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/sunderlands-young-goalkeeper-max-stryjek-10847600|title=Sunderland's young goalkeeper Max Stryjek extends his stay on Wearside|date=5 February 2016|accessdate=2 September 2017|author=James Hunter|publisher=Chronicle Live}}</ref> and in July 2017 he made his senior debut for the club, in a friendly game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.shieldsgazette.com/sport/football/sunderland-afc/opportunity-knocks-for-max-stryjek-as-sunderland-look-to-replace-vito-mannone-1-8657189|title=Opportunity knocks for Max Stryjek as Sunderland look to replace Vito Mannone|date=19 July 2017|accessdate=2 September 2017|author=Richard Mennear|publisher=Shields Gazette}}</ref> He moved on loan to [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]] on transfer deadline day, 31 August 2017.<ref name = "Echo">{{cite web|url=http://www.sunderlandecho.com/sport/football/sunderland-afc/sunderland-goalkeeper-max-stryjek-reacts-to-his-deadline-day-move-to-accrington-stanley-1-8730904|title=Sunderland goalkeeper Max Stryjek reacts to his deadline day move to Accrington Stanley|date=31 August 2017|accessdate=2 September 2017|author=Richard Mennear|publisher=Sunderland Echo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41111954|title=Accrington Stanley: Sunderland's Max Stryjek and Derby's Farrend Rawson join|date=31 August 2017|accessdate=2 September 2017|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He was injured 9 minutes into his professional debut, on 2 September 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/max-stryjek-injury-stanley-sunderland-13564831|title=Max Stryjek facing weeks on the sidelines after injury blow in Accrington Stanley debut|date=2 September 2017|accessdate=2 September 2017|author=Craig Johns|publisher=Chronicle Live}}</ref>

On 21 September, Stryjek joined National League side [[Eastleigh F.C.|Eastleigh]] on a one-month loan to replace the recently retired [[Graham Stack (footballer)|Graham Stack]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Stryjek joins Eastleigh on loan |url=https://www.safc.com/news/team-news/2018/september/stryjek-joins-eastleigh-on-loan |accessdate=21 September 2018 |publisher=[[Sunderland A.F.C.]] |date=21 September 2018}}</ref> On 11 June 2019, Sunderland announced that Stryjek was to leave the club when his contract expired at the end of that month.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.safc.com:443/news/team-news/2019/june/201920-retained-list|title=SAFC confirm retained list|date=11 June 2019|website=Sunderland Association Football Club}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48599307|title=Sunderland: Wales defender Adam Matthews among four players released|date=11 June 2019|publisher=BBC Sport|accessdate=12 June 2019}}</ref>

On 1 July 2019, Stryjek returned to [[Eastleigh F.C.|Eastleigh]], this time on a one-year deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eastleighnews.co.uk/2019/07/max-stryjek-returns-to-eastleigh/|title=Max Stryjek returns to Eastleigh|last=James|first=Kieran|date=1 July 2019|website=Eastleigh News|access-date=1 July 2019}}</ref> He returned home to [[Poland]] as the [[2019-20 National League|season was terminated]] and he was released due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 outbreak]].<ref name ="onet"/> After a successful trial<ref name ="onet"/> he signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] on 20 July 2020 on a three-year deal.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53472237|title=Livingston sign goalkeeper Max Stryjek|work=BBC Sport|date=20 July 2020}}</ref>

On 18 August 2022, he signed for [[EFL League One]] side [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Max Stryjek signs! |url=https://www.wwfc.com/news/2022/august/18/max-stryjek-signs/ |publisher=[[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]] |language=en |date=18 August 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62599775|title=Goalkeeper Stryjek leaves Livingston for Wycombe|work=BBC Sport |date=18 August 2022 }}</ref> On 24 February 2024, Styjek was red-carded in Wycombe's 1–0 defeat at [[Stevenage F.C.|Stevenage]].<ref name="BBC-24Feb2023">{{cite news |title=Stevenage 1–0 Wycombe Wanderers |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68324241 |access-date=13 May 2024 |work=BBC Sport |date=24 February 2024}}</ref> It was his 82nd and last appearance for the Chairboys.<ref name="BBC-02May2024"/>

On 13 April 2024, he signed on an emergency loan for [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.crewealex.net/news/2024/april/keeper-stryjek-joins-on-emergency-loan/|title=Keeper Stryjek joins on Emergency Loan|website=www.crewealex.net}}</ref> While on loan at Crewe, Wycombe announced on 2 May 2024 that Stryjek would be released by the club when his contract expired in June 2024.<ref name="BBC-02May2024">{{cite news |title=Goalkeeper Stryjek released by Wycombe |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c72pvy8d49xo |access-date=2 May 2024 |work=BBC Sport |date=2 May 2024}}</ref> Stryjek kept his first clean sheet for Crewe in their [[2024 English Football League play-offs|League Two play-off]] semi-final at Doncaster on 10 May, helping the side to a 2–2 aggregate draw, then saving twice in the penalty shoot-out that Crewe won 4–3.<ref name="BBC-10May2024">{{cite news |title=Doncaster Rovers 0–2 Crewe Alexandra |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/clw0p0epqj9t#Report |access-date=11 May 2024 |work=BBC Sport |date=10 May 2024}}</ref>

Stryjek's stay in the United Kingdom came to an end after over eleven years; on 19 June 2024, the defending Polish [[Ekstraklasa]] champions [[Jagiellonia Białystok]] announced the signing of Stryjek on a two-year contract, with an extension option, effective from 1 July.<ref>{{cite web |title=Maksymilian Stryjek zawodnikiem Jagiellonii Białystok |url=https://www.jagiellonia.pl/aktualnosci/maksymilian-stryjek-zawodnikiem-jagiellonii-biaystok |publisher=[[Jagiellonia Białystok]] |access-date=19 June 2024 |language=pl |date=19 June 2024}}</ref> His first match for [[Jagiellonia Białystok II]] was on 10 August 2024 in a 2–3 loss against [[Wisła II Płock]], and he debuted for Jagiellonia's main team in a 3–0 loss against [[Ajax Amsterdam]] in the [[UEFA Europa League]] on 29 August 2024.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Maksymilian Stryjek (season 2024–25) |url=http://www.90minut.pl/wystepy.php?id=22380&id_sezon=105 |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=www.90minut.pl |language=pl}}</ref>

He debuted in the [[Ekstraklasa]] on 1 September 2024 in a 1–0 home victory over [[Widzew Łódź]], keeping a clean sheet.<ref name=":0" />

On 4 July 2025, Stryjek returned to Scotland to join [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Boroń |first1=Jakub |title=Jagiellonia pożegnała kolejnego piłkarza. Przeniesie się za granicę |url=https://www.goal.pl/transfery/jagiellonia-pozegnala-kolejnego-pilkarza-przeniesie-sie-za-granice/ |website=goal.pl |access-date=4 July 2025 |language=pl |date=4 July 2025}}</ref>

Polak trafił z V ligi do Premiership i staje się gwiazdą}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.90minut.pl/news/278/news2780549-Reprezentacja-mlodziezowa-Kadra-na-mistrzostwa-Europy.html|title = Reprezentacja młodzieżowa: Kadra na mistrzostwa Europy}}</ref>

'''Callum David Hendry''' (born 8 December 1997) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].

Born in England, he is the son of former [[Scotland national football team|Scotland international]] defender [[Colin Hendry]], and began his career with his father's former club [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]], during which time he spent time on loan at non-league [[Clitheroe F.C.|Clitheroe]]. After being released by Blackburn in 2017 without making an appearance, Hendry then moved to Scotland, signing for [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]], and spent time on loan at [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]], [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], and [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]]. After five years with St Johnstone, he returned to England to sign for [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]]. After two years, he moved to [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|Milton Keynes Dons]]. Hendry moved back to Scotland in August 2025, when he signed for Motherwell.

==Career==

{{quote box |width=30% |align=right |quote=When I was young and I had injury troubles and wasn't able to play I did at times wonder if it was worth it. With his father formerly playing for the club, Hendry joined the youth system at [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]]. He progressed through [[Blackburn Rovers F.C. Under-23s and Academy|the club's academy]], but took a year off from football at the age of 12 following the death of his mother.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/rugby-union/colin-hendry-hails-warrior-son-callum-he-emerges-st-johnstone-265016 |title=Colin Hendry hails 'warrior' son Callum as he emerges with St Johnstone |work=[[The Scotsman]] |publisher=[[JPIMedia]] |issn=0307-5850 |date=18 August 2018 |access-date=18 June 2022}}</ref> He was sent out on loan to [[Northern Premier League]] [[2015–16 Northern Premier League#Division One North|Division One North]] team [[Clitheroe F.C.|Clitheroe]] in September 2015.<ref name="Herald"/> Hendry was offered to the club by Blackburn's academy manager Eric Kinder in order to "test Callum as a footballer in the men's game".<ref>{{cite web |last=Jackson |first=Andrew |url=https://www.clitheroefc.co.uk/news/two-new-faces-come-onboard-at-shawbridge-1485159.html |title=Two new faces come onboard at Shawbridge |work=[[Clitheroe F.C.]] |publisher=[[Pitchero]] |date=4 September 2015 |access-date=21 December 2017}}</ref>

He made his debut for ''The Blues'' in a 3–1 victory over [[Kendal Town F.C.|Kendal Town]], scoring twice.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/13712424.blackburn-rovers-youngster-callum-hendry-enjoys-dream-debut-clitheroe/ |title=Blackburn Rovers youngster Callum Hendry enjoys dream debut for Clitheroe |work=[[Lancashire Telegraph]] |publisher=[[Newsquest]] |issn=1746-0522 |date=10 September 2015 |access-date=18 June 2022}}</ref> His loan spell was extended for a further month on 10 October but,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/13837721.blackburn-rovers-academy-striker-callum-hendry-extends-clitheroe-loan-spell/ |title=Blackburn Rovers Academy striker Callum Hendry extends Clitheroe loan spell |work=[[Lancashire Telegraph]] |publisher=[[Newsquest]] |issn=1746-0522 |date=10 October 2015 |access-date=18 June 2022}}</ref> having scored six times for the club during his loan spell, Hendry suffered ruptured ligaments in his knee during a 2–0 victory over [[Mossley A.F.C.|Mossley]], and was ruled out for over six months.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/13926191.blackburn-rovers-loanee-striker-callum-hendry-faces-lengthy-spell-sidelines/ |title=Blackburn Rovers loanee striker Callum Hendry faces lengthy spell on sidelines |work=[[Lancashire Telegraph]] |publisher=[[Newsquest]] |issn=1746-0522 |date=30 October 2015 |access-date=18 June 2022}}</ref> He had previously suffered a similar injury at the age of 15.<ref name="Herald"/> After returning to Blackburn, Hendry was released by the club at the end of the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Sharpe |first=Rich |url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/15295134.rovers-release-six-first-team-players-looking-secure-future-connor-mahoney/ |title=Rovers release six first-team players but are looking to secure the future of Connor Mahoney |work=[[Lancashire Telegraph]] |publisher=[[Newsquest]] |issn=1746-0522 |date=19 May 2015 |access-date=18 June 2022}}</ref> He later praised his father for his influence in keeping him in football after his release from Blackburn and through his injury issues.<ref>{{cite web |last=Temple |first=Alan |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/1203976/st-johnstone-callum-hendry-dad-colin/ |title=St Johnstone star Callum Hendry admits he was ready to quit football before dad Colin's intervention |date=18 March 2020 |access-date=19 June 2022 |work=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]] |publisher=[[DC Thomson]]}}</ref>

===St Johnstone===
====2017–2020: professional debut, Brechin City loan====
Following his release, Hendry joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] on a one-year contract,<ref name="DDN"/><ref name="FondFarewell">{{cite web |last=Gallagher |first=Matthew |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/fond-farewell-callum-hendry-reflects-27312034 |title=FOND FAREWELL: Callum Hendry reflects on his special journey from trialist to first team star |date=24 June 2022 |access-date=25 June 2022 |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=[[Reach plc]] |issn=0956-8069}}</ref> after being recommended to assistant manager [[Callum Davidson]] by former teammate [[Brian O'Neil (footballer, born 1972)|Brian O'Neil]];<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/472371/colin-hendrys-son-callum-can-make-name-st-johnstone/ |title=Colin Hendry's son Callum can make his name at St Johnstone |date=20 July 2017 |access-date=18 June 2022 |work=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]] |publisher=[[DC Thomson]]}}</ref> he had been training with the team prior to his release, and it was intended for him to be used as an over-age player in the Under-20 team, but "exceeded expectations" upon his arrival.<ref>{{cite web |last=Marshall |first=Alan |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/st-johnstone-striker-callum-hendry-11000208 |title=St Johnstone striker Callum Hendry tipped to beat injuries and hit the big time – just like dad Colin |date=3 April 2019 |access-date=19 June 2022 |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=[[Reach plc]] |issn=0956-8069}}</ref> He made his début for the club as a substitute in place of [[Steven MacLean (footballer)|Steven MacLean]] during a 4–1 victory over [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on 12 August 2017.<ref name="2017-18"/> His first goal for the club came on 18 August 2018, scoring in a 4–2 win in the [[2018–19 Scottish League Cup#Second round|second round]] of the [[Scottish League Cup|League Cup]] against [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]].<ref name="FondFarewell"/>

He moved on loan to [[Brechin City F.C.|Brechin City]] in August 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45377414 |title=Ross Callachan: Midfielder joins St Johnstone from Hearts |date=31 August 2018 |access-date=31 August 2018 |work=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref> Though he only scored one goal in his time at the [[Scottish League One|League One]] club, manager [[Darren Dods]] was full of praise when reflecting on the loan in 2020, saying that he "could see the talent" of Hendry and that he had the right attitude and mentality to succeed.<ref>{{cite web |last=Nicolson |first=Eric |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/1318896/the-goals-didnt-flow-at-brechin-but-darren-dods-could-see-callum-hendry-was-a-future-st-johnstone-star/ |title=The goals didn't flow at Brechin but Darren Dods could see Callum Hendry was a future St Johnstone star |date=14 May 2020 |access-date=18 June 2022 |work=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]] |publisher=[[DC Thomson]]}}</ref> After returning to St Johnstone, he scored his first league goal on 3 April 2019 in a 2–0 win against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], his first start of the [[2018–19 St Johnstone F.C. season|2018–19 season]], and only his second start for the club.<ref>{{cite web |last=Haggerty |first=Anthony |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/st-johnstone-2-dundee-0-14231726 |title=St Johnstone 2 Dundee 0 as Callum Hendry grabs first career league goal |date=3 April 2019 |access-date=19 June 2022 |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=[[Reach plc]] |issn=0956-8069}}</ref>

In January 2020 he signed a new contract with St Johnstone, keeping him at the club until 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51333746 |title=St Johnstone: Matt Butcher & Isaiah Jones sign as Callum Hendry extends contract |date=31 January 2020 |access-date=31 January 2020 |work=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref> Hendry scored nine goals in the [[2019–20 St Johnstone F.C. season|2019–20 season]], directly adding 13 points to St Johnstone's points tally in the league,<ref>{{cite web |last=Bannerman |first=Gordon |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/callum-hendry-steps-out-from-his-dads-shadow-gb8xxz6dm |title=Callum Hendry steps out from his dad's shadow |date=9 March 2020 |access-date=19 June 2022 |work=[[The Times]] |issn=0140-0460 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> the last of which came on 7 March against [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]], and was the club's last without fans in attendance at [[McDiarmid Park]] until July 2021 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Gallagher |first=Matthew |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/green-light-st-johnstone-fans-24490638 |title=Green light for St Johnstone fans to make emotional McDiarmid Park return |date=8 July 2021 |access-date=19 June 2022 |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=[[Reach plc]] |issn=0956-8069}}</ref>

====2020–2022: out of favour, Aberdeen and Kilmarnock loans, departure====
Having fallen behind fellow strikers [[Chris Kane (footballer, born 1994)|Chris Kane]], [[Guy Melamed (footballer, born 1992)|Guy Melamed]], and [[Stevie May]] in the pecking order,<ref>{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Aidan |url=https://www.thenational.scot/sport/19056357.st-johnstone-striker-callum-hendry-completes-loan-switch-aberdeen/ |title=St Johnstone striker Callum Hendry completes loan switch to Aberdeen |date=1 February 2021 |access-date=20 June 2022 |work=[[The National (Scotland)|The National]] |publisher=[[Newsquest]] |issn=2057-231X}}</ref> Hendry was allowed to depart on loan to [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on 1 February 2021,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bannerman |first1=Gordon |last2=Hamilton |first2=Sean |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/1939363/st-johnstone-callum-hendry-aberdeen-loan-move-matty-kennedy/ |title=St Johnstone striker Callum Hendry seals Aberdeen loan move – with help from former Saint Matty Kennedy |date=1 February 2021 |access-date=25 June 2022 |work=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]] |publisher=[[DC Thomson]]}}</ref> brought in by manager [[Derek McInnes]] as a late deadline day replacement for the outgoing [[Sam Cosgrove]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Burns |first=Scott |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/derek-mcinnes-hits-out-aberdeens-23485193 |title=Derek McInnes hits out at Aberdeen's transfer tiz as boss left frustrated by late deadline day deals |date=11 February 2021 |access-date=19 June 2022 |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=[[Reach plc]] |issn=0956-8069}}</ref> He impressed on his début despite a 2–0 defeat to Livingston.<ref>{{cite web |last=Reid |first=John |url=https://www.nottheoldfirm.com/news/derek-mcinnes-impressed-with-callum-hendry-on-a-bad-night-for-aberdeen/ |title=Derek McInnes impressed with Callum Hendry on a bad night for Aberdeen |date=3 February 2021 |access-date=19 June 2022 |work=Not The Old Firm}}</ref> Hendry scored his first goal for the club on 21 February after coming on as a first-half substitute for the injured [[Fraser Hornby]];<ref>{{cite web |last=Watt |first=Martin |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56050896 |title=Aberdeen 1–0 Kilmarnock: Derek McInnes says Dons 'have more in us' |date=21 February 2021 |access-date=19 June 2022 |work=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref> it was Aberdeen's first goal in 574 minutes of football.<ref>{{cite web |last=Burns |first=Scott |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/colin-hendrys-aberdeen-premonition-braveheart-23540705 |title=Colin Hendry's Aberdeen premonition as Braveheart knew son Callum would end 573 minutes of agony |date=22 February 2021 |access-date=19 June 2022 |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=[[Reach plc]] |issn=0956-8069}}</ref> He was also the scorer of Aberdeen's next goal, an 84th winner in the [[2020–21 Scottish Cup#Third round|third round]] of the [[Scottish Cup]] against [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] on 3 April.<ref>{{cite web |last=Swan |first=Craig |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/callum-hendry-earns-glowing-aberdeen-23847466 |title=Callum Hendry earns glowing Aberdeen praise after heroic winner as Stephen Glass handed silverware shot |date=3 April 2021 |access-date=19 June 2022 |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=[[Reach plc]] |issn=0956-8069}}</ref> He left Aberdeen at the conclusion of his loan, scoring four goals in 14 appearances.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bannerman |first=Gordon |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/2225062/callum-hendry-st-johnstone-return-summer-aberdeen/ |title=Callum Hendry set for summer St Johnstone return after 'no contact' from Aberdeen |date=14 May 2021 |access-date=25 June 2022 |work=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]] |publisher=[[DC Thomson]]}}</ref> While away from ''Saints'', he missed out on their successes in the [[2021 Scottish Cup Final|Scottish Cup Final]] and the [[2021 Scottish League Cup Final (February)|Scottish League Cup Final]].<ref name="FondFarewell"/>

At the beginning of the [[2021–22 St Johnstone F.C. season|2021–22 season]], Hendry failed to score in eight appearances,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nicolson |first=Eric |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/2628021/callum-hendry-ended-up-trying-too-hard-to-score-goals-for-st-johnstone-says-callum-davidson/ |title=Callum Hendry ended up 'trying too hard' to score goals for St Johnstone, says Callum Davidson |date=30 September 2021 |access-date=18 June 2022 |work=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]] |publisher=[[DC Thomson]]}}</ref> but made his [[UEFA|European]] début in the [[UEFA Europa League]] [[2021–22 UEFA Europa League qualifying phase and play-off round#Third qualifying round|third qualifying round]] defeat against Turkish club [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]],<ref>{{cite web |last=Gallagher |first=Matthew |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/st-johnstone-show-fight-no-24772174 |title=St Johnstone will show fight and no fear against LASK, says Callum Hendry |date=16 August 2021 |access-date=20 June 2022 |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=[[Reach plc]] |issn=0956-8069}}</ref> an occasion he described as "surreal".<ref name="FondFarewell"/> On 29 September he moved on loan to [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/2626885/st-johnstone-striker-callum-hendry-joins-kilmarnock-on-loan/ |title=St Johnstone striker Callum Hendry joins Kilmarnock on loan |first=Eric |last=Nicolson |date=29 September 2021 |access-date=29 September 2021 |work=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]] |publisher=[[DC Thomson]]}}</ref> Having scored five goals in 13 appearances for the [[Ayrshire]]-based side,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Highet |first=Lochlin |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/callum-hendry-brands-kilmarnock-fantastic-26033806 |title=Callum Hendry brands Kilmarnock 'fantastic' as he thanks club upon departure |date=24 January 2022 |access-date=18 June 2022 |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=[[Reach plc]] |issn=0956-8069}}</ref> including a goal on his début against [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Highet |first=Lochlin |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/kilmarnock-1-raith-3-ayrshire-25123916 |title=Kilmarnock 1 Raith 3 as Ayrshire side fail to climb to top of Championship |date=2 October 2021 |access-date=25 June 2022 |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=[[Reach plc]] |issn=0956-8069}}</ref> With his parent club bottom of the table,<ref>{{cite web |agency=[[PA Media]] |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/st-johnstone-recall-callum-hendry-from-kilmarnock-loan-1643021166000 |title=St Johnstone recall Callum Hendry from Kilmarnock loan |work=[[FourFourTwo]] |publisher=[[Future plc]] |issn=1355-0276 |date=24 January 2022 |access-date=25 June 2022}}</ref> Hendry was recalled by St Johnstone in January 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/2937561/callum-hendry-kilmarnock-st-johnstone-dundee/ |title=Callum Hendry recalled by St Johnstone ahead of crunch Dundee showdown |first=Alan |last=Temple |date=24 January 2022 |access-date=24 January 2022 |work=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]] |publisher=[[DC Thomson]]}}</ref> Hendry credited manager [[Tommy Wright (footballer, born 1963)|Tommy Wright]] for helping rediscover his form and confidence while at ''Killie''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Highet |first=Lochlin |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/ayrshire/kilmarnock-striker-callum-hendry-admits-25118512 |title=Kilmarnock striker Callum Hendry admits Tommy Wright's tough love is what he needs to reignite form |date=1 October 2021 |access-date=20 June 2022 |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=[[Reach plc]] |issn=0956-8069}}</ref>

Upon his return to ''Saints'', he scored the opening goal in a 2–1 win against Livingston as St Johnstone ended a 12 game winless run.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Petrie |first=Andrew |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60121353 |title=Livingston 1–2 St Johnstone: Ali Crawford strikes at death to end winless run |date=1 February 2022 |access-date=18 June 2022 |work=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref> On 19 March, Hendry scored both goals to help St Johnstone come from a goal down to win 2–1 against Motherwell, with the winning goal coming in stoppage time, moving the team four points clear of Dundee at the bottom of the table.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12570512/st-johnstone-2-1-motherwell-callum-hendry-nets-added-time-winner-in-comeback-win |title=St Johnstone 2–1 Motherwell: Callum Hendry nets |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/callum-hendry-hits-added-time-winner-as-st-johnstone-beat-motherwell |title=Callum Hendry hits added-time winner as St Johnstone beat Motherwell |date=9 March 2022 |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12580863/st-johnstone-1-0-livingston-callum-hendrys-early-penalty-earns-saints-valuable-win-over-livi |title=St Johnstone 1–0 Livingston: Callum Hendry's early penalty earns Saints valuable win over Livi |date=2 April 2022 |access-date=20 June 2022 |work=[[Sky Sports]]}}</ref>

His run of form coincided with the final few months of his contract, though he said he was focused on helping St Johnstone survive and scoring; "that is what matters to me. The contract is the last thing on my mind right now".<ref>{{cite web |last=Gallagher |first=Matthew |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/callum-hendry-current-focus-scoring-26620781 |title=Callum Hendry: Current focus is on scoring goals and league safety not contract situation |date=2 April 2022 |access-date=20 June 2022 |work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]] |publisher=[[Reach plc]] |issn=0956-8069}}</ref> On 11 May, Hendry scored the only goal in a 1–0 win against Aberdeen, securing St Johnstone's place in the [[2021–22 Scottish |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/callum-hendry-strike-confirms-st-johnstones-play-off-place-and-relegates-dundee |title=Hendry goal confirms St Johnstone's play-off spot and relegates Dundee |date=11 relegation 6–2 on aggregate against Championship team [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Paton |first=Ewan |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/20160265.st-johnstone-4-inverness-0-6-2-agg-premiership-safety-confirmed-play-off-rout/ |title=St Johnstone 4 Inverness 0 (6–2 agg): Premiership safety |title=Callum Hendry confirms St Johnstone departure as striker prepares for next chapter |date=17 June 2022 |access-date=18 June 2022 |work=[[Yahoo! Sports]]}}</ref> and the goals scored in his final few months ensured he left as a fans' favourite, his name sung to the tune of [[Lady Gaga]]'s song ''[[Paparazzi (Lady Gaga song)|Paparazzi]]'' by ''Saints'' supporters.<ref name="FondFarewell"/>

===Salford City===
On 17 June 2022, Hendry agreed to join [[EFL League Two]] club [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]] on a two-year deal following his departure from St Johnstone on 1 July.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61844892 |title=Salford sign Hendry after St Johnstone exit |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=17 June 2022 |access-date=17 June 2022}}</ref> [[Neil Wood]], his new manager at Salford, described his acquisition as a "great addition to our squad, young and hungry to achieve success".<ref>{{cite web |agency=[[PA Media]] |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/callum-hendry-joins-salford-after-leaving-st-johnstone-1655475917000 |title=Callum Hendry joins Salford after leaving St Johnstone |work=[[FourFourTwo]] |publisher=[[Future plc]] |issn=1355-0276 |date=17 June 2022 |access-date=18 June 2022}}</ref> He was awarded the [[EFL League Two Player of the Month]] award for March 2023 having scored four goals and assisted a further two in Salford's play-off push.<ref name="Mar23 POTM">{{cite web|url=https://www.efl.com/news/2023/april/sky-bet-efl-march-manager-and-player-of-the-month-winners/|title=Sky Bet EFL March Manager and Player of the Month winners!|website=www.efl.com|date=7 April 2023|accessdate=9 April 2023}}</ref>

On 19 August 2023, Hendry scored a hat-trick in a 4–3 victory over [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]], the first player to achieve such a feat in the league that season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66482653 |title=Tranmere Rovers 3–4 Salford City: Callum Hendry's second-half hat-trick is enough to give Salford a thrilling win at Tranmere in League Two |date=19 August 2023 |access-date=19 March 2024 |work=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref> At the end of the season, Hendry signed a new one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cn0w392p3d7o |title=Hendry signs new one-year deal with Salford City |date=26 April 2024 |access-date=4 May 2024 |work=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref>

===Milton Keynes Dons===
On 12 July 2024, Hendry joined League Two club [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|Milton Keynes Dons]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cye08dyypg8o|title=Callum Hendry: MK Dons sign striker from Salford City|date=12 July 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 10 August 2024 in a 2–1 home defeat to [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/clynln40gp5t |title=Milton Keynes Dons 1–2 Bradford City |publisher=[[BBC]] |date=10 August 2024 |access-date=10 August 2024 }}</ref> Hendry scored his first goal for the club on 24 August 2024 in a 3–0 home win over [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c0l86z4p231t?page=2 |title=Milton Keynes Dons vs Carlisle United |publisher=[[BBC]] |date=24 August 2024 |access-date=26 August 2024 }}</ref>

===Motherwell===
Hendry transferred to [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] in August 2025 for an undisclosed transfer fee, signing a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c70xlyz8pd5o |title=Hendry brings 'energy & strong finishing' to Motherwell |website=BBC Sport |date=18 August 2025 |accessdate=18 August 2025}}</ref>

'''Lukas Fadinger''' (born 27 September 2000) is an Austrian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].

==Career==
===Sturm Graz===
On 11 June 2019 [[SK Sturm Graz]] announced, that Fadinger had been loaned out to [[SV Lafnitz]] for the 2019–20 season.<ref>[https://www.sksturm.at/de/news/kampfmannschaft/2019/lukas-fadinger-wird-verliehen/ LUKAS FADINGER WIRD VERLIEHEN], sksturm.at, 11 June 2019</ref>

===TSV Hartberg===
On 11 September 2020 he signed with [[TSV Hartberg]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[TSV Hartberg]]|url=https://www.tsv-hartberg-fussball.at/zwei-neuzugaenge-kurz-vor-saisonstart/|title=Zwei Neuzugänge kurz vor Saisonstart|date=11 September 2020|language=German}}</ref>

===Rheindorf Altach===
Before the 2023–24 season, Fadinger signed a two-year contract with [[SC Rheindorf Altach|Rheindorf Altach]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Rheindorf Altach|url=https://www.scra.at/news/detail/lukas-fadinger-verstaerkt-scra-mittelfeld|title=Lukas Fadinger verstärkt SCRA-Mittelfeld|trans-title=Lukas Fadinger strengthens SCRA midfield|access-date=11 December 2023|language=de}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
Fadinger signed a two-year contract with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] in May 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cwy75nj7lkko |title=Michael Wimmer says son's face 'was beaming with joy' after Motherwell exit |website=BBC Sport |quote=Wimmer was speaking as Motherwell announced the signing of Austrian midfielder Lukas Fadinger after the 24-year-old left Rheindorf Altach in his country's top flight. Fadinger, who has signed a two-year contract, told the Premiership club's website that negotiations had been ongoing "for a couple of months". |date=27 May 2025 |accessdate=27 May 2025}}</ref> On 19 May 2026, Motherwell announced that Fadinger had signed a one-year contract extension that will see him remain at the club until 2028.<ref>{{cite web |title=Contract extension for Lukas Fadinger |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/05/19/contract-extension-for-lukas-fadinger/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=19 May 2026 |date=19 May 2026}}</ref>

'''Robbie Deas''' (born 27 February 2000) is a Scottish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for {{Scottish football updater|Kilmarno}} club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].

==Club career==
===Celtic===
Deas signed his first professional contract with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2018. He scored the winning goal in stoppage time as [[Celtic F.C. Under-20s and Academy|Celtic youths]] beat [[Rangers F.C. Under-20s and Academy|Rangers]] 3–2 to lift the [[Glasgow Cup]] in May 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.footballscotland.co.uk/spfl/scottish-premiership/celtic-robbie-deas-goal-rangers-16206502|title=Watch Celtic kid Robbie Deas' last-gasp strike to win Glasgow Cup|last=Doyle|first=Chris|date=1 May 2019|website=footballscotland|access-date=17 October 2019}}</ref>

====Loan moves to Cowdenbeath and Alloa Athletic====
On 23 August 2018, Deas joined [[Scottish League Two]] club [[Cowdenbeath F.C.|Cowdenbeath]] on loan for the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tbrfootball.com/celtic-half-term-loan-report-ross-doohan-and-robbie-deas-lead-the-way-injury-pain-for-regan-hendry/|title=Celtic half-term loan report: Ross Doohan and Robbie Deas lead the way, injury pain for Regan Hendry|last=Nash|first=Mathew|date=25 December 2018|website=The Boot Room|language=en-US|access-date=17 October 2019}}</ref> On 9 October 2018, he was named in the SPFL team of the week after a  narrow 1–0 victory over [[Stirling Albion F.C.|Stirling Albion]] at [[Central Park, Cowdenbeath|Central Park]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spfl.co.uk/news/team-of-the-week-45089|title=Team of the Week {{!}} SPFL|website=spfl.co.uk|access-date=17 October 2019}}</ref>

On 2 August 2019, Deas moved on loan to [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] for the [[2019-20 Alloa Athletic season|2019–20]] season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thecelticstar.com/season-long-loans-agreed-for-young-celts-robbie-deas-and-daniel-church/|title=Season Long Loans agreed for young Celts Robbie Deas and Daniel Church|date=9 August 2019|accessdate=17 October 2019}}</ref>

===Inverness CT===
Deas left Celtic after the [[2019–20 Scottish Premiership|2019–20 season]] and signed a three-year contract with [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.inverness-courier.co.uk/sport/ex-celtic-defender-is-looking-up-with-caley-thistle-208380/ |title=Former Celtic defender Robbie Deas looking for promotion with Inverness Caley Thistle |newspaper=Inverness Courier |first=Will |last=Clark |date=7 August 2020 |accessdate=4 October 2020}}</ref> He played for Inverness in the [[2023 Scottish Cup final]], which they lost 3–1 to Celtic.<ref name = killie/>

===Kilmarnock===
Despite interest from [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]] earlier in the year,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Robbie Deas a Livingston transfer target as Lions eye summer move for Inverness defender |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/robbie-deas-livingston-transfer-target-29274950|website=dailyrecord.co.uk|date=22 February 2023}}</ref> it was announced that Deas had signed a two-year contract with [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on 5 June 2023.<ref name = killie>{{cite web |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/kilmarnock-seal-first-summer-signing-as-defender-robbie-deas-joins-from-inverness-ct/ |title=Kilmarnock seal first summer signing as defender Robbie Deas joins from Inverness CT |website=STV News |first=James |last=Delaney |date=5 June 2023 |accessdate=5 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Fitzsimmons |first=Andrew |date=2023-06-05 |title=Deas strengthens the defence |url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/deas-strengthens-the-defence/ |access-date=2023-06-05 |website=Kilmarnock FC}}</ref>

==International career==
Deas has represented Scotland at the [[Scotland national under-17 football team|under-17]], [[Scotland national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Scotland national under-21 football team|under-21]] levels.<ref>{{cite web|title=Robbie Deas Player profile|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/players/?pid=224131&lid=9|publisher=Scottish Football Association|accessdate=25 October 2019}}</ref><ref name=sw>{{soccerway|robbie-deas/460410|accessdate=17 October 2019}}</ref>

Deas received his first call-up to the Scottish under-21 squad on 25 May 2021, alongside Inverness teammates [[Roddy MacGregor]], [[Daniel MacKay]] and [[Cameron Harper (footballer)|Cameron Harper]], ahead of two friendlies against [[Northern Ireland national under-21 football team|Northern Ireland]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scot Gemmill names Under-21 squad for friendly double header {{!}} News {{!}} Scottish FA|url=https://www.scottishfa.co.uk/news/scot-gemmill-names-under-21-squad-for-friendly-double-header/?rid=14258|access-date=2021-05-25|website=www.scottishfa.co.uk}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Deas is the nephew of former footballer [[Paul Deas]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Robbie Deas was nearly a St Johnstone player|date=23 May 2022 |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/st-johnstone/3319314/robbie-deas-st-johnstone-ict-play-off/|publisher=The Courier|accessdate=23 May 2022}}</ref>

'''Dylan James Christopher Levitt''' (born 17 November 2000) is a Welsh professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe}} club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].

Levitt is a graduate of the [[Manchester United F.C. Reserves and Academy|Manchester United youth system]]. He made his senior debut in a [[UEFA Europa League]] match in November 2019, which was his only first-team appearance for [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. He spent time on loan at [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]], Croatian club [[NK Istra 1961|Istra 1961]] and Scottish club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]. He left Manchester United in July 2022 and joined Dundee United on a permanent deal. Levitt moved to Hibernian a year later.

Levitt represented Wales at several youth levels, before making his senior international debut in a [[UEFA Nations League]] game against [[Finland national football team|Finland]] in September 2020. He was selected for the Wales squads that played in [[UEFA Euro 2020]] and the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]].

==Club career==
===Manchester United===
[[File:Dylan_Levitt.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Levitt with [[Manchester United F.C. Reserves and Academy|Manchester United U18]] in 2017.]]

Levitt joined the [[Manchester United F.C. Reserves and Academy|Manchester United youth system]] at the age of eight and signed his first professional contract with the club in April 2018.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sands |first1=Katie |title=Dylan Levitt, the outstanding Man Utd teenager just handed his Wales debut by Ryan Giggs |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/dylan-levitt-man-utd-wales-16346194 |work=WalesOnline |publisher=Media Wales |date=3 September 2020 |access-date=1 June 2021}}</ref> In November 2019, he signed a new contract with the club until June 2022.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dylan Levitt signs new contract with Manchester United |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/dylan-levitt-man-utd-contract-17227972 |work=Manchester Evening News |date=8 November 2019 |access-date=1 June 2021}}</ref> He made his senior debut with United in a [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]] match against [[FC Astana|Astana]] on 28 November 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-astana-v-man-united-europa-league-28-november-2019 |first=Gemma|last=Thompson|title=FC Astana 2 Manchester United 1|publisher=Manchester United |date=28 November 2019 |access-date=28 November 2019}}</ref>

On 8 September 2020, Levitt was sent on a season-long loan to [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Dylan Levitt: Charlton Athletic sign Manchester United midfielder on loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54080226 |work= BBC Sport |date=8 September 2020 |access-date=1 June 2021}}</ref> On 8 January 2021, it was reported that Levitt's loan at Charlton Athletic had been cut short after he made only five first-team appearances at the [[EFL League One|League One]] club.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dylan Levitt: Wales midfielder recalled from Charlton by Manchester United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55594996 |work=BBC Sport |date=8 January 2021 |access-date=1 June 2021}}</ref>

On 15 February 2021, Levitt joined [[Croatian First Football League|Prva HNL]] side [[NK Istra 1961|Istra 1961]] on loan for the remainder of the [[2020–21 NK Istra 1961 season|2020–21 season]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56075031 |title=Dylan Levitt: Manchester United loan Wales midfielder to Croatian club Istra |work=BBC Sport |date=15 February 2021 |accessdate=1 June 2021}}</ref> On 14 April, he was unexpectedly given a chance by coach [[Danijel Jumić]] in the [[2020–21 Croatian Football Cup|Croatian Cup]] semi-final against [[HNK Rijeka|Rijeka]], being named in the starting lineup. He played until 64th minute when he was replaced by [[Dino Halilović]], as Istra managed to pull off an upset 3[[2020–21 NK Istra 1961 season|–]]2 win and qualify for the [[2021 Croatian Football Cup Final|final]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Matteoni|first=Robert|date=14 April 2021|title=Video: Istra srušila Riječane i ušla u povijesno finale Kupa, branitelj naslova eliminiran nakon drame|url=https://sportske.jutarnji.hr/sn/nogomet/hnl/video-istra-srusila-rijecane-i-usla-u-povijesno-finale-kupa-branitelj-naslova-eliminiran-nakon-drame-15065398|url-status=live|access-date=14 April 2021|website=Sportske novosti|language=hr-hr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414184315/https://sportske.jutarnji.hr/sn/nogomet/hnl/video-istra-srusila-rijecane-i-usla-u-povijesno-finale-kupa-branitelj-naslova-eliminiran-nakon-drame-15065398 |archive-date=14 April 2021 }}</ref>

===Dundee United===
On 20 August 2021, Levitt joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite news |first=Steven |last=Railston |title=Manchester United's Dylan Levitt completes loan transfer to Dundee United |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/dylan-levitt-man-united-loan-21362921 |work=Manchester Evening News |date=20 August 2021 |access-date=20 August 2021 }}</ref> After scoring six goals in 29 league and cup appearances for the Tangerines, including an extra-time winner against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in the fourth round of the [[2021–22 Scottish Cup]],<ref>{{cite news |first=Andrew |last=Southwick |title=Kilmarnock 1-2 Dundee United (AET): Dylan Levitt extra-time winner for visitors |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60005929 |website=BBC Sport |date=22 January 2022 |accessdate=17 May 2022 }}</ref> and three in the final five league matches to help Dundee United qualify for European football, Levitt was voted the fans' player of the year.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dundee United Player of the Year Awards 2021/22 |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/7319/DUNDEE-UNITED-PLAYER-OF-THE-YEAR-AWARDS-202122.html |website=dundeeunitedfc.co.uk |publisher=Dundee United FC |date=16 May 2022 |accessdate=17 May 2022 }}</ref>

Levitt then joined Dundee United on a two-year deal in July 2022,<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 July 2022 |title=Dylan Levitt Joins Dundee United |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/7365/DYLAN-LEVITT-JOINS-DUNDEE-UNITED.html |access-date=8 July 2022 |website=DundeeUnitedFC.co.uk |publisher=Dundee United}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Levitt completes permanent move|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-midfielder-dylan-levitt-rejoins-dundee-united-on-permanent-deal|website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=8 July 2022 |access-date=8 July 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Dundee Utd: Steven Fletcher & Dylan Levitt pen two-year deals at Premiership club |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62080878 |website=BBC Sport |date=7 July 2022 |access-date=7 July 2022}}</ref> and later extended this contract by one year. United were relegated from the Premiership after the 2022–23 season, and in July 2023 the club accepted an offer of around £300,000 for him from [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hibs/hibs-complete-signing-of-dylan-levitt-fee-paid-contract-length-lee-johnson-comments-4208541 |title=Hibs complete signing of Dylan Levitt - fee paid, contract length, Lee Johnson comments |first=Patrick |last=McPartlin |newspaper=Edinburgh Evening News |date=5 July 2023 |accessdate=5 July 2023}}</ref><ref name = hibs/>

===Hibernian===
Levitt signed a three-year contract with [[Scottish Premiership]]  club [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] on 5 July 2023.<ref name = hibs>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66111836 |title=Dylan Levitt: Hibernian sign Wales international from Dundee United |website=BBC Sport |date=5 July 2023 |accessdate=5 July 2023}}</ref>

===Leyton Orient===
In February 2026 Levitt joined [[EFL League One]] club [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]] on a 18 month contract.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cm24mg6r0xmo levitt joins Orient]</ref>

===Motherwell===
On 1 September 2026, Scottish Premiership club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] announced the signing of Levitt from Leyton Orient for an undisclosed fee, to a two-year contract with the club holding the option of an additional year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dylan Levitt is a Motherwell player |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/09/01/dylan-levitt-is-a-motherwell-player/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk/ |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=1 September 2026 |date=1 September 2026}}</ref>

'''Tyreece Romayo John-Jules''' (born 14 February 2001) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].

He has previously played for [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] and [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] before spending time on loan with [[Lincoln City F.C.|Lincoln City]], [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]], [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]], [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]], [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] and [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]]. After his release from Arsenal he played for [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]] and Scottish club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].

==Early life==
John-Jules was born in [[Westminster]], Greater London.<ref name="Profile">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/academy/players/tyreece-john-jules |title=Tyreece John-Jules |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |accessdate=31 August 2020}}</ref> He began his football career with [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] before joining [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] at the age of 8.<ref name=fox />

==Club career==
===Arsenal===
John-Jules made his debut for [[Arsenal F.C. Under-23s and Academy|Arsenal under-23s]] against Arsenal's [[North London derby]] rivals [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C. Under-23s and Academy|Tottenham Hotspur]] and scored in the match.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.football.london/arsenal-fc/tyreece-john-jules-arsenal-goal-15351221 |title=Who is Tyreece John-Jules? Arsenal's teenage striker who scored against Al Nasr in Dubai friendly |website=Football.London |date=26 March 2019 |access-date=16 January 2020}}</ref> He was part of the Arsenal under-18s team that reached the final of the [[2017–18 FA Youth Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2018/apr/27/chelsea-arsenal-fa-youth-cup-final-first-leg-270418 |title=Chelsea-Arsenal: FA Cup Youth Final first leg |date=27 April 2018 |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>

John-Jules signed professional terms for Arsenal in 2018.<ref name="Profile"/> In 2019, head coach [[Unai Emery]] selected him for the club's pre-season tour of the United States.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Willacy |first=Gavin |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/jul/31/charlton-young-players-lookman-konsa-grant-gomez |title=Charlton's academy keeps producing young players who make the grade |newspaper=The Guardian |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref> He renewed his contract with the club in August 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tyreece John-Jules signs new contract|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/tyreece-john-jules-signs-new-contract|access-date=26 March 2021|website=www.arsenal.com|language=en}}</ref> Later in the year, he started to train with the first-team squad at the request of [[Freddie Ljungberg]], Arsenal's under-23 manager who was then the acting first-team coach.<ref name="fox">{{Cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/football/premier-league/best-young-players-2020-manchester-united-real-madrid-barcelona-latest-news-transfers-lionel-messi/news-story/eee10d0021a4e8f57bd00bcef5dc6af1 |title=Best young players 2020 |last=Boon |first=Jon |date=31 December 2019 |website=Fox Sports |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>

John-Jules was loaned to [[Lincoln City F.C.|Lincoln City]] in January 2020.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/tyreece-john-jules-joins-lincoln-city-loan |title=Tyreece John-Jules joins Lincoln City on loan |publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51067520 |title=Lincoln City sign four players including Max Melbourne and Tayo Edun |work=BBC Sport |date=10 January 2020 }}</ref> The move was made by Arsenal head coach [[Mikel Arteta]] in order for John-Jules to get first-team football in his preferred role as a striker.<ref name="fl">{{Cite web |url=https://www.football.london/arsenal-fc/players/john-jules-makes-lincoln-debut-17558641 |title=John-Jules makes Lincoln debut |website=Football.London |date=13 January 2020 |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref> He made his Lincoln City debut against [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]].<ref name="fl" /> Lincoln City manager [[Michael Appleton]] praised John-Jules and said he could see him starting in Arsenal's first team in the future.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Whiley |first=Mark |url=https://www.lincolnshirelive.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/an-arsenal-number-nine-future-3722324 |title='An Arsenal number nine of the future' – Michael Appleton on new Lincoln City striker John-Jules |access-date=16 January 2020 |website=Lincolnshire Live}}</ref> He scored his first Football League goal against [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] in his next match.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51073021 |title=Lincoln City 1–0 Blackpool |date=18 January 2020 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=22 January 2020}}</ref> He was injured and ruled out for the rest of the season in March 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.lincolnshirelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/lincoln-city-facing-striker-shortage-3917174 |title=City facing striker shortage as extent of John-Jules' injury is confirmed |last=Whiley |first=Mark |date=5 March 2020 |website=Lincolnshire Live}}</ref> He subsequently returned to his parent club.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.lincolnshirelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/arsenal-lincoln-city-relationship-last-3916926 |title=Arsenal and Imps have a relationship which will 'last for many years' |last=Whiley |first=Mark |date=5 March 2020 |website=Lincolnshire Live}}</ref>

After his return to Arsenal, on 29 August 2020 John-Jules was an unused substitute in the [[2020 FA Community Shield]], in which Arsenal clinched a 5–4 penalty shootout victory over [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] after the match ended 1–1.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Association|first=The Football|title=Arsenal 1–1 Liverpool (5–4 on penalties)|url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2020/aug/29/arsenal-liverpool-mens-fa-community-shield-match-report-290820|access-date=26 March 2021|website=www.thefa.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 8 September 2020, John-Jules was loaned to [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]] for the 2020–21 season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54079042|title=Doncaster sign Arsenal's John-Jules|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> He scored his first goal for Doncaster in a 3–1 win against [[Charlton Athletic]] on 19 September 2020,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54127656 |title=Charlton 1–3 Doncaster |date=19 September 2020 |publisher=BBC|accessdate=20 September 2020}}</ref> for which he won the Goal of the Month for League One.<ref name="LOGotM">{{cite news|url=https://www.doncasterroversfc.co.uk/news/2020/october/john-jules-wins-sky-bet-league-one-september-goal-of-the-month/|title=John-Jules wins Sky Bet League One September Goal of the Month|publisher=Doncaster Rovers F.C.|date=16 October 2020|access-date=12 February 2021}}</ref>

John-Jules joined [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] on a season-long loan on 29 July 2021.<ref>[https://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/news/post/seasiders-bring-in-tyreece-john-jules "Seasiders Bring in Tyreece John Jules"] – Blackpool F.C., 29 July 2021</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58012192|title=Blackpool sign John-Jules from Arsenal|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> He returned from the loan on 17 January 2022.<ref>[https://www.blackpoolgazette.co.uk/sport/football/blackpool-fc/tyreece-john-jules-returns-to-arsenal-early-after-unsuccessful-loan-spell-with-blackpool-3531105 "Tyreece John-Jules returns to Arsenal early after unsuccessful loan spell with Blackpool"] – ''[[Blackpool Gazette]]'', 17 January 2022</ref>

On 25 January 2022, John-Jules joined [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] on loan for the remainder of the season to team up with manager [[Darren Moore]] once again.<ref>{{cite web |title=Owls sign Arsenal forward John-Jules|url=https://www.swfc.co.uk/news/2022/january/owls-sign-arsenal-forward-john-jules/|publisher=Sheffield Wednesday FC |access-date=25 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60130164|title=Arsenal striker John-Jules joins Owls|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> He made his debut on 29 January, coming off the bench against [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.swfc.co.uk/news/2022/january/report-wednesday-1-0-ipswich/|title=Report: Wednesday 1-0 Ipswich|publisher=Sheffeld Wednesday F.C. |date=29 January 2022 |access-date=29 January 2022}}</ref>

On 22 June 2022, John-Jules joined Ipswich Town on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.itfc.co.uk/news/2022/june/tyreece-john-jules-joins-on-loan/ | publisher = [[Ipswich Town F.C.]] | title = Tyreece John-Jules joins on loan | access-date = 22 June 2022 | date = 22 June 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/61901691|title=Ipswich sign Arsenal's John-Jules on loan|work=BBC Sport }}</ref>

On 25 August 2023, John-Jules joined [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] on loan until January 2024.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.dcfc.co.uk/news/2023/08/derby-sign-arsenal-striker-john-jules-on-loan | publisher = [[Derby County F.C.]] | title = Derby sign Arsenal striker John-Jules on loan | access-date = 25 August 2023 | date = 25 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66627204|title=Derby sign Gunners striker John-Jules on loan|work=BBC Sport |date=26 August 2023 }}</ref> After making his debut against [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]] on 26 August 2023, he picked up a thigh injury during the [[international break]] which ruled him out of the game at home to [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] on 16 September 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.derbytelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/derby-county-injury-latest-warne-8757559|title=Paul Warne reveals fresh Derby County injury blow|work=Derbyshire Live |via=www.derbytelegraph.co.uk|date=16 September 2023|access-date=19 September 2023}}</ref> John-Jules was out for two months with this injury, missing fifteen matches.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.derbytelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/derby-injury-news-bristol-rovers-8915991|title=Elder, Washington, Mendez-Laing - Derby County injury latest ahead of Bristol Rovers|work=Derbyshire Live |via=www.derbytelegraph.co.uk|date=21 November 2023|access-date=1 December 2023}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Derby in his return appearance from injury, with his first touch after being a 76th-minute substitute against [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] on 28 November 2023, scoring a minute later in the 1–0 victory.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67482040|title=Port Vale 0–1 Derby County|work=BBC Sport |date=28 November 2023|access-date=1 December 2023}}</ref> Derby head coach [[Paul Warne]] was keen to extend John-Jules loan beyond its middle of January 2024 expiry, with Arsenal and Derby being in talks to do so.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.derbytelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/derby-arsenal-tyreece-john-jules-9007791|title=Derby County in Arsenal talks after Tyreece John-Jules wish revealed|work=Derbyshire Live |via=www.derbytelegraph.co.uk|date=2 January 2024|access-date=8 January 2024}}</ref> John-Jules started his first game for Derby on 6 January 2024, at [[Fleetwood Town F.C.|Fleetwood Town]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dcfc.co.uk/news/2024/01/team-news-fleetwood-town-vs-derby-county-january-2024|title=Team News: Fleetwood Town vs Derby County|via=www.dcfc.co.uk|date=6 January 2024|access-date=8 January 2024}}</ref> Later that month his loan was extended until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68024433|title=Derby renew John-Jules loan for rest of the season|work=BBC Sport |date=19 January 2024|access-date=19 January 2024}}</ref> On 23 January 2024, he left the field against [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] in pain from a "serious" injury; later in the week it was confirmed that he would out for foreseeable future with a severe [[hamstring]] tear which may require surgery, and that the spate of injuries during his loan spells was taking a toll on him [[Mental health in association football|mentally]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.derbytelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/derby-county-tyreece-john-jules-9059736|title=Paul Warne issues emotional update as striker left 'destroyed' by injury blow|work=Derbyshire Live |via=www.derbytelegraph.co.uk|date=26 January 2024|access-date=26 January 2024}}</ref> On 8 February 2024, Warne confirmed that John-Jules had surgery on the injury, which ruled him out for the rest of the season. He also stated that John-Jules had returned to Arsenal for recovery and rehabilitation from said surgery.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68240852|title=Tyreece John-Jules: Derby County's on-loan Arsenal striker has season ended by injury|work=BBC Sport |date=8 February 2024|access-date=8 February 2024}}</ref> John-Jules returned to training at Derby in April with a chance of a possible return to action before the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.derbytelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/derby-tyreece-john-jules-arsenal-9232018|title=Paul Warne issues Tyreece John-Jules update after Derby County get Arsenal go-ahead|work=Derbyshire Live |via=www.derbytelegraph.co.uk|date=18 April 2024|access-date=18 April 2024}}</ref> He did not feature in any further games for Derby, however; he made a total of twelve appearances for Derby, scoring one goal, as they secured promotion to the Championship.<ref name=2324promotion>{{cite news|title=Breaking: Derby County promoted as duo seal it for Paul Warne's side|url=https://www.derbytelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/breaking-derby-county-promoted-duo-9250843|publisher=Derby Telegraph|date=27 April 2024|accessdate=28 April 2024}}</ref>

He was released by Arsenal at the end of the 2023–24 season following the expiration of his contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/22-players-depart-arsenal-end-contacts |title= 22 players to depart Arsenal at end of contacts  |publisher=Arsenal FC |date=3 June 2024 |accessdate=3 June 2024}}</ref>

===Crawley Town===
On 18 October 2024, John-Jules joined League One club [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]] on a deal for the remainder of the [[2024–25 Crawley Town F.C. season|2024–25 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.crawleytownfc.com/news/2024/october/18/reds-sign-tyreece-john-jules/|title=REDS SIGN TYREECE JOHN-JULES|website=www.crawleytownfc.com|date=18 October 2024|accessdate=18 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c93yzdlg0n3o|title=Tyreece John-Jules: Crawley sign former Arsenal striker|date=18 October 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 12 May 2025, Crawley announced he would be leaving the club in June when his contract expired.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 May 2025 |title=Crawley Town released and retained list: Reds in negotiations with six key players as former Arsenal man leaves |url=https://www.sussexexpress.co.uk/sport/football/crawley-town-released-and-retained-list-reds-in-negotiations-with-six-key-players-as-former-arsenal-man-leaves-5125092 |access-date=12 May 2025 |website=SussexWorld |language=en}}</ref>

===Kilmarnock===
He signed for Scottish club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in October 2025 on a short-term deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kilmarnockfc.co.uk/news/tyreece-john-jules-signs-for-kilmarnock/|title=Tyreece John-Jules signs for Kilmarnock|first=Lochlin|last=Highet|date=24 October 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
John-Jules has represented England at [[England national under-16 football team|under-16]], [[England national under-17 football team|under-17]], [[England national under-18 football team|under-18]] and [[England national under-18 football team|under-19]] level.<ref name="Profile" /><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://dailycannon.com/2018/01/daily-cannon-exclusive-interview-tyreece-john-jules/ |title=Daily Cannon Exclusive: Interview with Tyreece John-Jules |date=21 January 2018 |website=Daily Cannon |access-date=12 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="Soccerway">{{soccerway|453134|Tyreece John-Jules}}</ref> In May 2018, John-Jules was a member of the side that hosted the [[2018 UEFA European Under-17 Championship]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2018/may/03/england-u17s-squad-named-for-u17-euro-finals-030518 |title=England U17s squad revealed for U17 Euro finals on home turf |date=3 May 2018 |access-date=4 March 2020 |publisher=The Football Association}}</ref> The hosts were eliminated by the [[Netherlands national under-17 football team|Netherlands]] at the semi-final stage on a penalty shootout with John-Jules scoring his spot kick.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/under17/match/2024318--england-vs-netherlands/ |title=England 0–0 Netherlands |date=17 May 2018 |access-date=4 March 2020 |publisher=UEFA}}</ref>

On 7 September 2021, John-Jules made his England U21 debut during the 2–0 [[2023 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification]] win over [[Kosovo national under-21 football team|Kosovo U21s]] at [[Stadium MK]].<ref>{{cite news|title=England U21 2-0 Kosovo U21|work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58460993|date=7 September 2021|access-date=7 September 2021}}</ref>

He is also eligible to both represent the [[Dominica national football team|Dominica national team]], as both his paternal grandparents are from Dominica,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://cultbox.co.uk/interviews/exclusives/danny-john-jules-death-in-paradise-interview |title=Danny John-Jules: Death in Paradise interview |website=Cultbox |date=17 October 2011 |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=FIFA Statutes |url=https://resources.fifa.com/mm/document/affederation/generic/02/78/29/07/fifastatutsweben_neutral.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160509164416/http://resources.fifa.com/mm/Document/AFFederation/Generic/02/78/29/07/FIFAStatutswebEN_Neutral.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=9 May 2016 |publisher=FIFA |access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref> and [[Barbados national football team|Barbados]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.tiktok.com/@tbgpod/video/7237362509152390426 |title=John-Jules's England Desire |website=TikTok |date=29 June 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
John-Jules is the nephew of actor [[Danny John-Jules]], best known for playing [[Cat (Red Dwarf)|Cat]] in the sci-fi comedy series ''[[Red Dwarf]]''.<ref name=fox /><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://dailycannon.com/2019/08/arsenal-reward-tyreece-john-jules-with-new-deal/ |title=Arsenal reward Tyreece John-Jules with new deal |date=5 August 2019 |website=Daily Cannon |access-date=12 January 2020}}</ref>

'''Emmanuel Longelo Mbule''' (born 27 December 2000) is an English professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left back]] for <!--do not remove template--> {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe}} club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]. Longelo began his career with [[West Ham United]] and played first-team football in the [[EFL Cup]] and the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] before joining Birmingham City, initially [[loan (association football)|on loan]], in 2022. He spent the 2024–25 season on loan at [[Cambridge United]].

==Club career==
===West Ham United===
Longelo started playing [[Sunday league football]] as a nine-year old for Euro Dagenham. He joined [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]]'s under-10 side playing as a [[midfielder]] and scored five goals on his debut, against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Due to his pace he was moved to play as a striker. Playing for [[West Ham United F.C. Under-23s and Academy|West Ham's under-23]] team, Longelo played as a [[left-back]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.whufc.com/news/articles/2020/march/31-march/academy-spotlight-emmanuel-longelo |title=Academy Spotlight: Emmanuel Longelo |publisher=West Ham United F.C. |date=31 March 2020 |access-date=1 October 2022}}</ref> On 21 September 2020, Longelo made his debut for West Ham in a 5–1 [[EFL Cup]] win against [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.whufc.com/news/articles/2020/september/24-september/emmanuel-longelo-west-ham-united-debut-dream-come-true|title=Emmanuel Longelo: West Ham United debut is a dream come true|publisher=West Ham United F.C.|date=24 September 2020|accessdate=24 September 2020}}</ref>

===Birmingham City===
He joined [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] on a season-long loan on 30 August 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Manny Longelo joins Birmingham City on loan |url=https://www.whufc.com/news/manny-longelo-joins-birmingham-city-loan |publisher=West Ham United F.C. |access-date=30 August 2022 |date=30 August 2022}}</ref> After recovering from injuries suffered earlier in the season,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/birmingham-city-whufc-manny-longelo-24963552 |title=What West Ham expect from Manny Longelo at Birmingham City |first=Brian |last=Dick |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=1 October 2022 |access-date=1 October 2022}}</ref> he made his debut on 1 October, starting at left [[wing-back (association football)|wing-back]] in a 1–1 draw away to [[EFL Championship|Championship]] leaders [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-sheffutd-player-ratings-25154623 |title=Birmingham City player ratings vs Sheffield United: Troy Deeney pounces to give Blues a point |first=Brian |last=Dick |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=1 October 2022 |access-date=1 October 2022}}</ref> In a 2–0 win over [[Queens Park Rangers]] on 28 October, he "received the ball on the left, twisted and turned past [[Ethan Laird]] and then found the bottom-right corner with a low curling finish"<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12732580/birmingham-2-0-qpr-auston-trusty-and-manny-longelo-goals-prevent-rangers-re-taking-championship-top-spot |title=Birmingham 2–0 QPR: Auston Trusty and Manny Longelo goals prevent Rangers re-taking Championship top spot |first=Dan |last=Long |website=Sky Sports |date=28 October 2022 |access-date=29 October 2022}}</ref> to score his first senior goal, and later gave away a [[penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] which was saved by [[John Ruddy]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-qpr-player-ratings-25383643 |title=Birmingham City player ratings vs QPR: Ruddy stands firm as Trusty and Longelo fire Blues |first=Brian |last=Dick |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=28 October 2022 |access-date=29 October 2022}}</ref>

Longelo signed a three-and-a-half-year contract with Birmingham City on 31 January 2023. The fee, officially undisclosed, was reported by ''[[football.london]]'' as £400,000.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64478779 |title=Emmanuel Longelo: West Ham wing-back completes Birmingham City move |website=BBC Sport |date=31 January 2023 |access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.football.london/west-ham-united-fc/west-ham-transfer-birmingham-city-26124498 |title=West Ham confirm transfer decision as defender completes £400,000 Birmingham City switch |first=Jonty |last=Colman |website=football.london |date=31 January 2023 |access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref> He lost his place for a time, but came back into the team at the end of the season, which he finished with 23 league appearances.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/manny-longelo-makes-birmingham-city-26532069 |title=Manny Longelo makes Birmingham City promise after being dropped by John Eustace |first=Alex |last=Dicken |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=22 March 2023 |access-date=22 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-citys-absent-trio-set-26715118 |title=Birmingham City's absent trio set a challenge during run-in |first=Joseph |last=Chapman |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=18 April 2023 |access-date=22 August 2024}}</ref><ref name="sb2223" /> He began the 2023–24 season as a regular in the matchday squad,<ref name="Soccerway">{{cite web |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/players/mbule-longelo-emmanuel/457357/ |title=M. Emmanuel |website=Soccerway |publisher=Perform Group |access-date=22 August 2024}}</ref> and he and [[Cody Drameh]] had a run in the starting eleven when both [[full back (association football)|full back]], [[Ethan Laird]] and [[Lee Buchanan (footballer)|Lee Buchanan]], were injured at the same time.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-west-brom-highlights-27862032 |title=Krystian Bielik was right about Birmingham City as John Eustace finds two solutions in crisis |first=Alex |last=Dicken |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=7 October 2023 |access-date=22 August 2024}}</ref> When Laird regained fitness, it was Longelo who lost the starting place,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-transfer-wayne-rooney-28089820 |title=Birmingham City have glaring transfer need as Wayne Rooney faces defining period |first=Alex |last=Dicken |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=12 November 2023 |access-date=22 August 2024}}</ref> and after [[Wayne Rooney]] was replaced as manager in January 2024, he did not play in the league again.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/burke-hogan-aiwu-birmingham-city-28568381 |title=Oliver Burke, Scott Hogan and Co have a brutal new reality at Birmingham City |first=Alex |last=Dicken |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=14 February 2024 |access-date=22 August 2024}}</ref><ref name="sb2324" />

====Loan to Cambridge United====
Longelo was not given a [[squad number]] by Birmingham at the start of the [[2024–25 EFL League One|2024–25 League One season]], and after a proposed move to [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] fell through,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/birmingham-city-transfers-longelo-bacuna-29751923 |title=Birmingham City reveal latest on Manny Longelo and Juninho Bacuna transfer sagas |first=Alex |last=Dicken |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=16 August 2024 |access-date=22 August 2024}}</ref> he joined Birmingham's divisional rivals [[Cambridge United F.C.|Cambridge United]] on 22 August 2024 on loan for the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cambridgeunited.com/news/emmanuel-longelo-arrives-us |title=Emmanuel Longelo arrives at the U's |publisher=Cambridge United F.C. |date=22 August 2024 |access-date=22 August 2024}}</ref> He made 19 appearances, scoring twice, in all competitions.<ref name="sb2425" />

===Motherwell===
On 10 July 2025, Longelo moved to [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] for an undisclosed fee, signing a two year deal through 2027, with the option of a further year to extend the contract through 2028.<ref>{{cite web |title=Left-back Longelo Signs |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2025/07/10/left-back-emmanuel-longelo-signs/ |website=Motherwell FC |publisher=Motherwell FC |access-date=10 July 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Longelo was born in [[Barking, London|Barking]], London, and is of [[DR Congo|Congolese]] descent. His older brother, [[Rosaire Longelo|Rosaire]], played alongside him at West Ham before joining [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1137689/2019/08/14/from-forward-to-left-back-academy-star-longelo-is-one-to-watch-out-for-at-west-ham/ |title=From forward to left back, academy star Longelo is one West Ham fans should watch out for |first=Roshane |last=Thomas |website=The Athletic |date=14 August 2019 |access-date=22 September 2020 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>
