'''Joshua James Rawlins''' (born 23 April 2004) is an Australian professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Fullback (association football)|right back]] for {{Scottish football updater|DundeeUn}} club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].

== Early life ==
Born in [[Perth]], Rawlins played for Dianella Soccer Club during his childhood, before joining [[Perth Glory FC|Perth Glory]]'s development sector in 2015.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2022-05-04 |title=Australische aanwinst: Joshua Rawlins |url=https://www.fcutrecht.nl/nieuws/2022/mei/australische-aanwinst-joshua-rawlins/ |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=FC Utrecht |language=nl}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2022-05-05 |title=Rawlins Set To Complete Move To Dutch Top Flight |url=https://perthglory.com.au/news/rawlins-set-to-complete-move-to-dutch-top-flight |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=Perth Glory}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=AFC Champions League | AFC |url=https://www.the-afc.com/competitions/afc-champions-league/matches/2020/2043056}}</ref>

He attended Our Lady's Assumption Primary School in [[Dianella, Western Australia|Dianella]], and then continued his study path at [[Chisholm Catholic College, Perth|Chisholm Catholic College]] in [[Bedford, Western Australia|Bedford]].<ref name=":2" />

== Club career ==

=== Perth Glory ===
After coming through the youth ranks of [[Perth Glory FC|Perth Glory]] and playing both in the [[A-League Youth]] and the [[National Premier Leagues Western Australia|National Premier Leagues]] with their youth sides, Rawlins made his professional debut on 18 November 2020, starting the match against [[Shanghai Shenhua F.C.|Shanghai Shenhua]] in the [[2020 AFC Champions League group stage|group stage]] of the [[2020 AFC Champions League]], which Perth eventually lost 1-2. In the occasion, he became the youngest player to ever feature in an ACL game, at 16 years, six months and 26 days.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-11-19 |title=Shanghai Shenhua's Choi hails '100 percent' effort in AFC Champions League win |url=https://www.the-afc.com/en/club/afc_champions_league/news/shanghai_shenhua%E2%80%99s_choi_hails_%E2%80%98100_percent%E2%80%99_effort_in_afc_champions_league_win%0D.html |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=The AFC}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last1=Christenson |first1=Marcus |last2=Kemp |first2=Emma |date=2021-10-07 |title=Next Generation 2021: 60 of the best young talents in world football |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2021/oct/07/next-generation-2021-60-of-the-best-young-talents-in-world-football |access-date=2022-06-06 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> He would go on playing three more matches in the continental tournament, two of which as a starter, as his side finished last in their group and failed to progress to the next round.<ref name=":3" />

On 20 January 2021, Rawlins made his debut in the [[2020-2021 A-League|A-League]], starting the match against [[Adelaide United FC|Adelaide United]] as his team eventually gained a 5-3 win: at 16 years and 272 days, he became the youngest ever player to feature in the starting XI for a league match.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Nick |date=2021-01-20 |title=A-League 2021: Perth Glory dominant in season-opening 5-3 win over Adelaide United |url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/perth-glory/a-league-2021-perth-glory-dominant-in-season-opening-5-3-win-over-adelaide-united-ng-b881774617z |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=The West Australian |language=en}}</ref> Under the manager [[Richard Garcia]], he went on to collect eleven more appearances during the campaign (seven of which as a starter), as Perth finished the regular season at the bottom of the league table.<ref name=":3" />

Finally, on 24 November 2021, the full-back debuted in the [[FFA Cup]], coming in as a substitute for [[Tyler Vecchio]] at the 66th minute of the play-off match against [[Melbourne Victory FC|Melbourne Victory]], with the visitors eventually winning the match at [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-outs]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-11-24 |title=FFA Cup Report: Glory 1 (3) - 1 (4) Victory |url=https://melbournevictory.com.au/news/ffa-cup-report-glory-13-14-victory |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=Melbourne Victory}}</ref> During the [[2021-22 A-League|2021-2022 season]], Rawlins established himself more as a regular starter in the team, collecting a total amount of 23 appearances between the league and the [[2022 Australia Cup|national cup]], although Perth Glory finished last in the A-League and got left out of the final play-offs for the second year in a row.{{Citation needed|date=June 2024}}

=== Utrecht ===
On 4 May 2022, it was officially announced that Rawlins would join [[FC Utrecht|Utrecht]] on 1 July for an undisclosed fee, signing a four-year contract with the Dutch club and becoming their fifth ever Australian player in the process, after [[Tommy Oar]], [[Adam Sarota]], [[Michael Zullo]] and [[Daniel Arzani]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

On 11 June 2024, Utrecht announced that Rawlins had terminated his contract with the club by mutual consent.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 June 2024 |title=Joshua Rawlins keert niet meer terug bij FC Utrecht |url=https://www.fcutrecht.nl/nieuws/2024/juni/joshua-rawlins-keert-niet-meer-terug-bij-fc-utrecht |access-date=13 June 2024 |website=FC Utrecht |language=nl}}</ref>

==== Loan to Perth Glory ====
On 29 January 2024, Perth announced the re-signing of Rawlins on loan.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morgan |first=Gareth |date=2024-01-29 |title=Rising star Rawlins returns to Glory on loan |url=https://perthglory.com.au/news/rising-star-rawlins-returns-to-glory-on-loan |access-date=2024-01-29 |website=Perth Glory}}</ref> In May 2024, the club confirmed that Rawlins had returned to his parent club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morgan |first=Gareth |date=2024-05-28 |title=ALM player departures confirmed |url=https://perthglory.com.au/news/alm-player-departures-confirmed/ |access-date=2024-05-28 |website=Perth Glory |language=en-AU}}</ref>

=== Melbourne Victory ===
On 28 June 2024, it was officially announced that Rawlins had signed for [[Melbourne Victory FC|Melbourne Victory]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=sachapisani |date=2024-06-28 |title=Victory recruit Aussie young gun from Eredivisie club: 'Incredibly bright future' |url=https://aleagues.com.au/news/a-league-melbourne-victory-transfer-news-josh-rawlins/ |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=A-Leagues |language=en-AU}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=tlusk |date=2024-06-28 |title=Melbourne Victory signs Josh Rawlins |url=https://melbournevictory.com.au/news/melbourne-victory-signs-josh-rawlins/ |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=Melbourne Victory |language=en-AU}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
In May 2026, Rawlins signed a contract with Scottish side [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], joining former [[A-League Men]] players [[Jesse Randall]] and [[Lachlan Rose]].<ref>https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/9369/JOSHUA-RAWLINS-SET-TO-BECOME-DUNDEE-UNITEDS-THIRD-ADDITION-OF-THE-SUMMER-TRANSFER-WINDOW.html</ref>

== International career ==
Rawlins was born in Australia to a half Malaysian mother.<ref name="Majoriti.com.my 2023">{{cite web | title=Risau Corbin Ong bersara? Prospek FC Utrecht dikhabarkan ada pertalian darah dengan Malaysia, calon pengganti terbaik | website=Majoriti.com.my | date=2023-05-28 | url=https://majoriti.com.my/sukan/2023/05/28/risau-corbin-ong-bersara-prospek-fc-utrecht-dikhabarkan-ada-pertalian-darah-dengan-malaysia-calon-pengganti-terbaik | language=ms | access-date=2023-06-05}}</ref> He has represented Australia at several youth international levels.

He was the [[Captain (association football)|captain]] of the national selection at the [[2019 AFF U-15 Championship]], where his side failed to progress to the knock-out stage.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aseanfootball.org/v3/wp-content/uploads/match_result/u16/2019/M5.pdf|title=AFF Championship Match Summary Cambodia U15 v Australia U15|publisher=AFF|date=28 July 2019|access-date=24 September 2021}}</ref>

In the same year, he was also included in the [[Australia national under-17 soccer team|squad]] that took part in the [[2019 FIFA U-17 World Cup|FIFA Under-17 World Cup]] in [[Brazil]]:<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-10-02 |title=Trevor Morgan names Australia's Brazil-bound boys |url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/trevor-morgan-names-australias-brazil-bound-boys |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=Socceroos |language=en}}</ref> being the youngest player of the bunch, Rawlins played all the three matches in the group stage of the competition, as the ''Joeys'' managed to progress to the knock-out phase as one of the best third-placed teams, before eventually getting eliminated by [[France national under-17 football team|France]] in the round of 16.

In May 2022, Rawlins was called-up to the [[Australia men's national under-23 soccer team|under-23 national team]] to take part in the [[2022 AFC U-23 Asian Cup|AFC U-23 Asian Cup]] in [[Uzbekistan]], once again being the youngest member in the squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-18 |title=CONFIRMED: Squad named for Australia's U23 Asian Cup quest |url=https://www.footballaustralia.com.au/news/confirmed-squad-named-australias-u23-asian-cup-quest |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=Football Australia |language=en}}</ref> He subsequently made his debut for the ''Olyroos'' on June 4, starting their second group stage fixture against [[Iraq national under-23 football team|Iraq]]: in the occasion, he assisted [[Alou Kuol]]'s opening goal, as the match eventually ended in a 1-1 draw.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-04 |title=Group B: Iraq, Australia play to a thrilling draw |url=https://www.the-afc.com/en/national/afc_u23_asian_cup/news/group_b_iraq_v_australia__1.html |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=The AFC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ward |first=Roy |date=2022-06-04 |title='Don't ask me how I've done it': Young Socceroo Alou Kuol scores scorpion goal |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/soccer/don-t-ask-me-how-i-ve-done-it-young-socceroo-alou-kuol-scores-scorpion-goal-20220605-p5ar4s.html |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=The Sydney Morning Herald |language=en}}</ref> After losing to eventual champions [[Saudi Arabia national under-23 football team|Saudi Arabia]] in the semi-finals,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-15 |title=Saudi Arabia turn on the style against Australia to book final ticket |url=https://www.the-afc.com/en/national/afc_u23_asian_cup/news/semi-final_australia_v_saudi_arabia_3.html |access-date=2022-07-07 |website=The AFC |language=en}}</ref> Australia also lost the third place match against [[Japan national under-23 football team|Japan]] and finished fourth overall in the continental tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-18 |title=Japan power past Australia to take third spot |url=https://www.the-afc.com/en/national/afc_u23_asian_cup/news/third_place_playoff_japan_v_australia_1.html |access-date=2022-07-07 |website=The AFC |language=en}}</ref>

== Style of play ==
Rawlings primarily plays as a [[right back]], though he has demonstrated that he can play in any position across the backline, as well as a [[defensive mid]]fielder. He's been described as an athletic footballer, who has his strengths in his passing and dribbling skills, as well as in the defensive phase.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" />

In 2021, the [[United Kingdom|British]] newspaper ''[[The Guardian]]'' included him in their annual list of the most promising talents in world football, alongside his fellow countryman [[Mohamed Toure (footballer, born 2004)|Mohamed Toure]].<ref name=":3" />

'''Lachlan Rose''' (born 10 May 1999) is an Australian professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] or [[Winger (association football)|right winger]] for {{Scottish football updater|DundeeUn}} club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].

==Early life==
Rose was born on 10 May 1999. Born in [[Sydney]], Australia.

==Club career==
New [[A-League]] club [[Macarthur FC|Macarthur]] announced the signing of Rose for their inaugural [[2020–21 A-League]] season in November 2020.<ref>[https://www.macarthurfc.com.au/news/macarthur-fc-announce-lachlan-rose-inaugural-season Macarthur FC Announce Lachlan Rose for Inaugural Season], Macarthur FC official website, 26 November 2020, access date 30 December 2020</ref> He debuted for the club starting in their first ever A-League game against [[Western Sydney Wanderers]] on 30 December 2020, having a goal ruled offside.<ref>[https://www.a-league.com.au/news/live-western-sydney-wanderers-v-macarthur-fc-match-report-goals-video-highlights-updates Macarthur record famous win over Wanderers in inaugural A-League match], A-League official website, 30 December 2020</ref> In March 2021, after playing in eight out of a possible ten league matches, Macarthur extended Rose's contract for another two years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.macarthurfc.com.au/news/signing-news-macarthur-fc-lach-rose|title=SIGNING NEWS: Macarthur FC Lach-in Rose|website=[[Macarthur FC]]|date=4 March 2021}}</ref> He underwent ankle surgery while playing for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/8157736/rose-tells-macarthur-to-bring-cup-final-mindset/|title=Rose tells Macarthur to bring cup final mindset|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[The Canberra Times]]|date=13 April 2023|access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref>

After scoring seven of the club's 36 goals during the [[2021–22 Macarthur FC season|season]], Rose was crowned as the Macarthur Medal Winner for 2022.<ref name=MacarthurMedal />

On 21 July 2024, Rose joined fellow [[A-League Men]] side [[Newcastle Jets FC|Newcastle Jets]] on a two-year deal following a free transfer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://newcastlejetsfc.com.au/news/newcastle-jets-sign-lachlan-rose/|title=Newcastle Jets sign Lachlan Rose|website=[[Newcastle Jets FC|Newcastle Jets]]|date=21 July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/8703165/lachy-rose-steps-up-for-newcastle-jets-after-stammas-exit/|title=Rosy outlook: Jets recruit has big shoes to fill after striker's exit|first=James|last=Gardiner|newspaper=[[Newcastle Herald]]|date=22 July 2024|quote= Stamatelopoulos' move coincides with the arrival of Rose on a two-year deal.}}</ref> He was regarded as a fan favorite while playing for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/9218748/lachlan-rose-jets-stars-final-push-for-a-league-silverware/|title=Jets striker keen to depart Newcastle on a high before overseas move|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[Newcastle Herald]]|date=9 April 2026|access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref>

Following an impressive 2 seasons, it was announced on the 17th of March 2026 that he had signed a pre-contract agreement with [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on a 2 year deal with the Scottish side holding an option to extend his contract for another year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LACHLAN ROSE AGREES PRE-CONTRACT WITH DUNDEE UNITED |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/9333/LACHLAN-ROSE-AGREES-PRE-CONTRACT-WITH-DUNDEE-UNITED.html |access-date=2026-04-12 |website=Dundee United Football Club |language=en}}</ref>

Cup|2024 Fiji/Vanuatu]]|}} {{Medal|Competition|[[OFC U-16 Championship]]}} {{Medal|W|[[2018 OFC U-16 Championship|2018 Tonga/Solomon Islands]]|}} }} '''Alexander Noah Paulsen''' (born 4 July 2002) is a New Zealand professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|keeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe}} club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], on loan from English {{English football updater|AFCBourn}} club [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]], and the [[New Zealand men's national football team|New Zealand national team]]. Born in Auckland, Paulsen joined the academy of [[Wellington Phoenix FC|Wellington Phoenic FC]] in 2018 and signed his first professional contract in September 2021. After establishing himself as the club’s first-choice goalkeeper, he signed for Bournemouth in June 2024.{{cite news|url=https://www.afcb.co.uk/news/2024/June/4/cherries-complete-signing-of-goalkeeper-paulsen|website=[[AFC Bournemouth]]|date=4 June 2024|access-date=10 February 2025|title=Cherries complete signing of goalkeeper Paulsen}} He was subsequently loaned to sister club [[Auckland FC]] for their inaugural [[A-League Men]] season and won the Premiership with them, before joining [[Lechia Gdańsk]] on loan for the 2025–26 campaign. In July 2026, Paulsen was loaned to Scottish side [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].{{cite news |title=Paulsen joins Motherwell on season-long loan |url=https://www.afcb.co.uk/news/2026/july/13/paulsen-joins-motherwell-on-season-long-loan/ |access-date=13 July 2026 |publisher=AFC Bournemouth |date=13 July 2026}} Paulsen represented [[New Zealand men's national under-23 football team|New Zealand]] at the [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics|2020]] and [[Football at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024]] Olympics.{{cite web | url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12356355/football-at-olympics-tokyo-2020-which-premier-league-stars-are-heading-to-the-games | title=Football at Olympics Tokyo 2020: Which Premier League stars are heading to the Games? | publisher=SkySports | date=15 July 2021 | access-date=17 July 2021 | author=Ben Grounds}}{{cite web | url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/nz-teams/117115849/fifa-under17-world-cup-new-zealand-stay-alive-thanks-to-alex-paulsens-saves | title=Fifa Under-17 World Cup: New Zealand stay alive thanks to Alex Paulsen's saves | publisher=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] | date=2 November 2019 | access-date=18 July 2021 | author=Andrew Voerman}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/143021?newsfeedId=1275622|website=[[New Zealand Football]]|date=10 July 2024|access-date=12 August 2024|title=Men's Football Team Announced for Paris 2024}} He also featured in the New Zealand squad at the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].{{Cite web |title=New Zealand Squad Named for FIFA World Cup 2026 |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/nzfootball |access-date=2026-07-13 |website=www.nzfootball.co.nz}} ==Early life== Paulsen was born in [[Auckland]] to a South African father and Namibian mother.{{Cite web|url=https://aleagues.com.au/news/who-is-alex-paulsen-wellington-phoenix-a-league/|title=Meet the 21yo goalkeeper taking the A-Leagues by storm: 'There will be clubs after him'|date=28 November 2023}}{{cite web | url=https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/mens/u17worldcup/brazil2019/news/paulsen-bounces-back-new-zealand-canada-u17wc | title=Paulsen Bounces Back at First Opportunity | publisher=FIFA | date=2 November 2019 | access-date=18 July 2021}} He played [[futsal]] throughout his childhood, and only committed to playing football as a goalkeeper at the age of 13 after beginning as an outfielder.{{Cite web|url=https://wellingtonphoenix.com/news/match-programme-feature-alex-paulsen/|title=Match Programme Feature - Alex Paulsen|date=4 December 2023}} Paulsen initially played in the youth ranks of [[Eastern Suburbs AFC|Eastern Suburbs]] and then [[Onehunga Sports]] under the tutelage of noted youth development coach [[Hiroshi Miyazawa (footballer)|Hiroshi Miyazawa]]. In 2018, aged 15, Paulsen moved to Wellington to join the [[Wellington Phoenix FC|Wellington Phoenix]] academy through their affiliation with Onehunga Sports, following in the footsteps of fellow graduates [[Sarpreet Singh]] and [[Max Mata]]. ==Club career== ===Wellington Phoenix=== ====Early career==== After progressing through the Wellington Phoenix age-grade sides, Paulsen was regularly named as a substitute for [[Wellington Phoenix FC Reserves|Wellington Phoenix Reserves]] throughout the [[2018–19 New Zealand Football Championship|2018–19]] and [[2019–20 New Zealand Football Championship|2019–20]] [[New Zealand Football Championship]] seasons, but did not make an appearance. During this time, Paulsen played for Wellington Phoenix affiliate clubs [[Wellington United]] and [[Lower Hutt City AFC|Lower Hutt City]] in the [[Central League (New Zealand)|Central League]]. On 14 November 2020, Paulsen finally made his reserves debut, starting in a 1–0 loss to [[Team Wellington]] in the opening game of the [[2020–21 New Zealand Football Championship|2020–21]] season. Paulsen remained a consistent starter throughout the season, and despite the team finishing last, Paulsen was named the league's Most Valuable Player.{{Cite web |last=Ellie |date=2021-03-21 |title=Team Wellington crowned 2020/21 ISPS Handa Men's Premiership champions {{!}} ISPS Handa |url=https://ispsgolf.com/team-wellington-crowned-2020-21-isps-handa-mens-premiership-champions/ |access-date=2024-06-19 |language=en-AU}} His performances for the reserves culminated in his first professional contract, signing for the senior team on a three-year deal alongside fellow reserve standout [[Ben Old]].{{Cite web|url=https://wellingtonphoenix.com/news/wellington-phoenix-sign-academy-players-ben-old-and-alex-paulsen/|title=Wellington Phoenix Sign Academy Players Ben Old and Alex Paulsen|date=13 September 2021}} Paulsen entered the [[2021–22 A-League Men]] season as second-choice goalkeeper behind club captain [[Oliver Sail]]. On 19 December 2021, following an injury to Sail, Paulsen made his A-League debut as a substitute in a 2–1 loss against [[Sydney FC]].{{cite news |last1=Rollo |first1=Phillip |title='Not up to standard': Wellington Phoenix lose third A-League Men game in a row |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/a-league/127326106/not-up-to-standard-wellington-phoenix-lose-third-aleague-men-game-in-a-row |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=19 December 2021 |language=en}} Paulsen would remain starter in Sail's absence; in an [[2021 FFA Cup|FFA Cup]] quarterfinal match against [[Melbourne City FC|Melbourne City]] on 5 January 2022, Paulsen made three saves in a 0–0 (4–3) [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] win to secure the Phoenix's maiden semifinal appearance in the competition.{{cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/a-league/127420779/alex-paulsen-saves-the-day-to-send-wellington-phoenix-into-ffa-cup-final-four|title=Alex Paulsen saves the day to Paulsen made three competition appearances, and was presented the Golden Glove award. In the final against the [[Solomon Islands national under-17 football team|Solomon Islands]], Paulsen saved two penalties – one in regular time, one in the penalty shootout – as New Zealand prevailed to win their eighth title, qualifying for the [[2019 FIFA U-17 World Cup]] in the process.{{Cite web |date=2018-09-24 |title=Sport: NZ seal seventh OFC U16 title |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/367135/sport-nz-seal-seventh-ofc-u16-title |access-date=2024-06-19 |website=[[RNZ]] |language=en-nz}} Paulsen played in all three of New Zealand's games in the [[2019 FIFA U-17 World Cup]], being eliminated in the group stage. Despite making a high-profile error in a 3–0 loss to [[Brazil national under-17 football team|Brazil]], Paulsen recovered to keep a clean sheet in a 1–0 win over [[Canada men's national under-17 soccer team|Canada]].{{Cite web | title=Keeper calm and carrying on: How Alex Paulsen bounced back from unfortunate error {{!}} Stuff.co.nz | url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/a-league/301039178/keeper-calm-and-carrying-on-how-alex-paulsen-bounced-back-from-unfortunate-error | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240114065230/https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/a-league/301039178/keeper-calm-and-carrying-on-how-alex-paulsen-bounced-back-from-unfortunate-error | access-date=2026-07-09 | archive-date=2024-01-14}} Aged just 17, Paulsen was called up by [[Des Buckingham]] to the [[New Zealand men's national under-23 football team|New Zealand under-23]] squad for the [[2019 OFC Men's Olympic Qualifying Tournament]]. Paulsen made one appearance, as a late substitute in a 6–1 win over [[Samoa national under-23 football team|Samoa]], as New Zealand won the title and qualified for the [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020 Summer Olympics]].{{cite web | url=https://www.oceaniafootball.com/new-zealand-u-23-secure-olympic-qualification/ | title=New Zealand U-23 secure Olympic qualification|website=Oceaniafootball.com | date=5 October 2019 }} [[Danny Hay]] named Paulsen as a traveling reserve for the tournament, with [[Michael Woud]] and [[Jamie Searle]] preferred in the main squad; Paulsen did not make an appearance as New Zealand reached the quarter-finals. In September 2022, Paulsen was first called up to the [[New Zealand men's national football team|senior national team]] for a two-game friendly series against [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]], but did not play in either match.{{Cite web |title=New Zealand Football |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/nzfootball |access-date=2024-06-19 |website=Nzfootball.co.nz}} He was later called up for friendlies against [[Greece national football team|Greece]] and [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Ireland]] in November 2023, and then in March 2024 for two [[2024 FIFA Series|FIFA Series]] matches against [[Egypt national football team|Egypt]] and [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]], but again did not play ahead of incumbent [[Max Crocombe]].{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-11-06 |title=Paulsen one of three Nix called up to the All Whites |url=https://wellingtonphoenix.com/news/paulsen-one-of-three-nix-called-up-to-the-all-whites/ |access-date=2024-06-19 |website=Wellington Phoenix |language=en-AU}} On 18 June 2024, Paulsen finally made his senior international debut, keeping a clean sheet against the [[Solomon Islands national football team|Solomon Islands]] in a 3−0 [[2024 OFC Men's Nations Cup]] win. Crocombe started all subsequent tournament games as New Zealand eventually claimed the trophy.{{cite web | url=https://www.oceaniafootball.com/competition-list/ofc-mens-nations-cup-2024-group-a-2700242489/new-zealand-solomon-islands-2701555571/ | title=Match|website=Oceaniafootball.com }}{{cite web | url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/football/all-whites/all-whites-v-vanuatu-live-updates-from-the-oceania-nations-cup-final/SVBR3KJDBZFKJNF2RPBEA6EMVA/ | title=All Whites claim Nations Cup|website=Nzherald.co.nz | date=30 June 2024 }} Paulsen was recalled to the All Whites for the inaugural New Zealand [[FIFA Series]], featuring matches against [[Finland national football team|Finland]] and [[Chile national football team|Chile]]. He played the full 90 minutes against Chile in a 4–1 victory, which marked New Zealand's first win against a [[CONMEBOL]] opponent and ended their eight-game winless run.{{Cite web |last=Burgess '''Joseph Brennen Hugill''' (born 19 October 2003) is an English [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|centre-forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]].

==Early life ==
Born in [[Durham, England|Durham]], England, Hugill started his career with [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], where he spent a year, before joining rivals [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]].<ref name=sky>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11667/12109040/joe-hugill-is-hype-around-manchester-united-teenager-real|title=Joe Hugill: Is hype around Manchester United teenager justified?|date=21 October 2020|accessdate=3 August 2021|website=skysports.com}}</ref><ref name=athletic>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2360124/2021/02/05/joe-hugill-manchester-united/|title=Four goals against Liverpool mean Joe Hugill is already on Solskjaer's radar|first=Laurie|last=Whitwell|date=5 February 2021|access-date=3 August 2021|website=theathletic.com}} {{subscription required}}</ref><ref name=vavel>{{cite web|url=https://www.vavel.com/en/football/2021/07/28/manchester-united/1079957-joe-hugill-signsnew-deal-at-old-trafford-who-is-the-17-year-old-solskjaer-is-so-excitedabout.html|title=Joe Hugill signs new deal at Old Trafford: Who is the 17-year-old Solskjaer is so excited about?|first=Ryan|last=Batty|date=28 July 2021|accessdate=3 August 2021|website=vavel.com}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Manchester United===
Hugill signed with [[Premier League]] side [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] on 1 July 2020, with the Manchester club reportedly having fought off competition from [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], among others, for his signature.<ref name=sky/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/manchester-united-joe-hugill-news-20963141|title=Manchester United starlet Joe Hugill could benefit from summer transfer decision|first=Richard|last=Fay|date=4 July 2021|accessdate=3 August 2021|website=manchestereveningnews.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.90min.com/posts/joe-hugill-things-to-know-man-utd-starlet|title=Who is Joe Hugill? Things to know about the Man Utd starlet|first=Tom|last=Gott|date=31 January 2021|accessdate=3 August 2021|website=90min.com}}</ref> His career in Manchester started brightly, with his most notable performance coming against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] U23, where he scored four goals in a 6–3 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/liverpool-manchester-united-diallo-highlights-19732660|title=Liverpool U23s 3-6 Manchester United U23s highlights after Hugill scores four and Diallo nets brace|first=Marcus|last=Banks|date=30 January 2021|accessdate=3 August 2021|website=manchestereveningnews.co.uk}}</ref><ref name=athletic/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/sunderland-phillips-hugill-manchester-united-19794288|title=Kevin Phillips blasts Sunderland's decision to sell Joe Hugill to Manchester United|first=Matty|last=Hewitt|date=8 February 2021|accessdate=3 August 2021|website=chroniclelive.co.uk}}</ref> In doing so, he became only the second player in Manchester United history to score four in one game against Liverpool, after [[Steve Jones (footballer, born 1960)|Steve Jones]] in a reserve game in 1977.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/why-joe-hugill-entered-the-record-books-with-four-goal-haul-v-liverpool|title=Why Hugill has Entered the Record Books|first=Adam|last=Marshall|date=3 February 2021|accessdate=3 August 2021|website=manutd.com}}</ref>

Hugill was called up to train with the Manchester United first team for [[2021–22 Manchester United F.C. season|2021–22]] pre-season preparation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/former-sunderland-youngster-joe-hugill-20975963|title=Former Sunderland youngster Joe Hugill pictured training with Manchester United first team|first=Matty|last=Hewitt|date=5 July 2021|accessdate=3 August 2021|website=chroniclelive.co.uk}}</ref> He featured in friendly games against [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] and [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thepeoplesperson.com/2021/08/02/joe-hugill-whats-next-for-the-youngster-at-man-united-233765/|title=Joe Hugill: What's next for the youngster at Man United|first=Joe|last=Taylor|date=2 August 2021|accessdate=3 August 2021|website=thepeoplesperson.com}}</ref>

He signed a new contract in July 2021.<ref name=vavel/>

On 1 February 2023, Hugill was one of three Manchester United youngsters to join [[National League (division)|National League]] club [[Altrincham F.C.|Altrincham]] on loan for the remainder of the season, alongside [[Sonny Aljofree]] and [[Maxi Oyedele]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://altrinchamfc.com/blogs/news/goal-machine-joe-among-united-trio-joining-alty-on-loan|title=Goal machine Joe among United trio joining Alty on loan|website=altrinchamfc.com|date=1 February 2023|accessdate=1 February 2023}}</ref> This marked the start of a new scheme that would see the youngsters continue to train and play for Manchester United's academy teams, while also earning senior experience playing for their loan club.<ref>{{cite news |title=United trio head out in innovative loan scheme |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/altrincham-sign-man-utd-academy-players-sonny-aljofree-joe-hugill-maxi-oyedele-on-loan |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=1 February 2023 |accessdate=1 February 2023 }}</ref>

On 12 January 2024, he joined [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Burton Albion F.C.|Burton Albion]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.burtonalbionfc.co.uk/news/2024/january/1001-signing/|title=BREWERS FIGHT OFF COMPETITION TO CAPTURE STRIKER JOE HUGILL ON LOAN FROM MANCHESTER UNITED|website=www.burtonalbionfc.co.uk|date=12 January 2024|accessdate=16 January 2024}}</ref> He made his debut three days later, scoring his side's equaliser within minutes of his introduction from the bench in an eventual 3–2 defeat to [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67908904|title=Derby County 3–2 Burton Albion|publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 January 2024|accessdate=16 January 2024}}</ref>

He joined League One club [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] on loan at the start of the 2024–25 season, returning to Manchester United on 8 January 2025.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hugill Returns From Wigan Loan |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/joe-hugill-returns-to-manchester-united-after-wigan-athletic-loan-8-january-2025#:~:text=Joe%20Hugill%20has%20returned%20to,at%20Altrincham%20and%20Burton%20Albion. |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |access-date=8 January 2025 |date=8 January 2025}}</ref>

On 17 January 2025, Hugill joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] bottom side [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.carlisleunited.co.uk/news/joe-hugill-joins-united-loan|title=JOE HUGILL JOINS UNITED ON LOAN|website=www.carlisleunited.co.uk|date=17 January 2025|accessdate=17 January 2025}}</ref>

On 19 July 2025, Hugill joined [[Barnet F.C.|Barnet]] on a season-long loan.<ref>https://barnetfc.com/joe-hugill-joins-on-loan</ref> He was recalled by Manchester United on 14 January 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HUGILL RECALLED - Barnet Football Club |url=https://barnetfc.com/hugill-recalled |access-date=2026-01-14 |website=barnetfc.com |language=en-GB}}</ref>

===Kilmarnock===

'''William Ferry''' (born 7 December 2000) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|full-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|DundeeUn}} club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]. Born in England, he is a senior international for Ireland.

==Club career==
Born in [[Bury, Greater Manchester|Bury]],<ref name="sw" /> Ferry spent his early career with [[Bury F.C.|Bury]] and [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]], turning professional in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 January 2021 |title=Ferry pens two-year contract extension |url=https://www.southamptonfc.com/news/2020-01-10/will-ferry-contract-extension-southampton-football-club-june-2022 |access-date=26 September 2021 |publisher=Southampton F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kinsella |first=Rudi |date=27 April 2021 |title=Player profile #2 – Will Ferry — one of Ireland and Southampton's most highly rated talents |url=https://www.irishpost.com/sport/will-ferry-player-profile-210758 |access-date=26 September 2021 |website=The Irish Post}}</ref> He signed a new two-year contract with Southampton in August 2021 and immediately moved on loan to [[Crawley Town F.C.|Crawley Town]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |date=3 August 2021 |title=Will Ferry: Crawley Town sign Southampton full-back on loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58080203 |access-date=26 September 2021 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Crocker |first=Tom |date=3 August 2021 |title=Crawley loan for Will Ferry after signing new Saints deal |url=https://www.dailyecho.co.uk/sport/19488864.crawley-loan-will-ferry-signing-new-saints-deal/ |access-date=26 September 2021 |website=Daily Echo}}</ref>

In August 2022 he signed for [[Cheltenham Town F.C.|Cheltenham Town]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62479438|title=Cheltenham sign Southampton wing-back Ferry|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> Following relegation at the end of the [[2023–24 Cheltenham Town F.C. season|2023–24 season]], Ferry was offered a new contract to remain with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ctfc.com/news/2024/april/202324-retained-and-released-list/|title=2023/24 retained and released list|website=www.ctfc.com|date=30 April 2024|accessdate=6 June 2024}}</ref>

On 6 June 2024, Ferry agreed to join [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on a three-year deal from the expiration of his contract with Cheltenham Town.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/8424/WILL-FERRY-BECOMES-UNITEDS-FIRST-SUMMER-SIGNING.html|title=WILL FERRY BECOMES UNITED's FIRST SUMMER SIGNING|website=www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk|date=6 June 2024|accessdate=6 June 2024}}</ref> He scored his first professional goal for United on 22 March 2026 in a 2–0 win against Celtic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5456795/jim-goodwin-celtic-dundee-united-verdict-miracle/|title=Jim Goodwin delivers 'deserved' Celtic verdict as Dundee United boss eyes 'miracle'|date=22 March 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Ferry is a former [[Republic of Ireland national under-18 football team|Republic of Ireland under-18]], [[Republic of Ireland national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Republic of Ireland national under-21 football team|under-21]] international.<ref name="auto" /> On 6 October 2025, he received his first senior [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] call-up, replacing the injured [[Callum O'Dowda]] in the squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification|2026 FIFA World Cup qualifiers]] against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] and [[Armenia national football team|Armenia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2025/1006/1537167-ferry-earns-first-ireland-call-szmodics-and-odowd-out/|title=Ferry earns first Ireland call, Szmodics & O'Dowda out|date=6 October 2025|via=www.rte.ie}}</ref> On 16 May 2026, Ferry made his senior [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] debut, replacing [[Tayo Adaramola]] from the bench in a 5–0 win over [[Grenada national football team|Grenada]] in a friendly.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hallgrímsson names 21-player squad for Grenada international friendly |url=https://www.fai.ie/latest/hallgrimsson-names-21-player-squad-grenada-international-friendly/|access-date=5 May 2026 |publisher=FAI|date=5 May 2026}}</ref>

'''Zidane Aamar Iqbal''' ({{langx|Ar| زیدان عمار اقبال}}; born 27 April 2003) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]. Born in England, he plays for the [[Iraq national football team|Iraq national team]].

Iqbal joined [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]'s youth system aged nine. He made his first-team debut, and his only senior appearance for United, in a [[UEFA Champions League]] match in December 2021. He signed for [[FC Utrecht|Utrecht]] in 2023, and moved to Dundee United in 2026.

Iqbal represented Iraq at [[Iraq national under-23 football team|under-23]] level, before making his senior international debut in January 2022. He represented Iraq at the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Manchester]] to a Pakistani father and an Iraqi mother, Iqbal played for local side Sale United from the age of four before joining [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at the age of nine.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/zidane-iqbal-manchester-united-wiki-22406508 |title=Who is Zidane Iqbal? ===Utrecht===
On 23 June 2023, Iqbal announced that he would be leaving Manchester United to join a new club, subject to registration and international clearance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/zidane-iqbal-posts-emotional-message-to-club-and-fans-as-man-utd-academy-graduate-departs|title=Iqbal's emotional post as he departs United|first=Adam|last=Bostock|date=23 June 2023|accessdate=26 June 2023|website=ManUtd.com|publisher=Manchester United}}</ref> His move to [[FC Utrecht|Utrecht]] was announced and finalised on 26 June, on a four-year contract for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cyxp2jvz1lvo |title=Iqbal leaves Man Utd to join FC Utrecht |website=BBC Sport |date=26 June 2023 |access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref>

=== Dundee United ===
After three years in the Netherlands, he moved to Scotland, signing for [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on a two-year deal with the club having the option of extending for another year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zidane checks in on deadline day |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/9500/Zidane-checks-in-on-deadline-day.html |date=3 September 2026 |access-date=3 September 2026 |website=Dundee United Football Club |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Iraq World Cup midfielder Iqbal joins Dundee United from Utrecht |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cg491z1q13vo |website=BBC Sport |date=3 September 2026 |access-date=3 September 2026}}</ref> Iqbal scored his debut goal for the club in a 3-2 home win against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].

==International career==
Iqbal was eligible to represent [[England national football team|England]], [[Iraq national football team|Iraq]], and [[Pakistan national football team|Pakistan]] at international level.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60104894 |title=Zidane Iqbal: Manchester United youngster called up by Iraq |work=BBC Sport |date=23 January 2022 |accessdate=22 February 2022 |archive-date=22 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220222095259/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60104894 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Youth===
In May 2021, he received an Iraqi passport, and has represented Iraq at youth international level.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://shafaq.com/ar/%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%80%D8%A7%D8%B6%D8%A9/%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%A8-%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%B4%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B1-%D9%8A%D9%88%D9%86%D8%A7%D9%8A%D8%AA%D8%AF-%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%86-%D9%82%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%AA%D8%B3%D9%84%D9%85-%D8%AC%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B2-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%81%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%82%D9%8A|title=لاعب مانشستر يونايتد "زيدان إقبال" يتسلم الجواز العراقي|trans-title=Manchester United player Zidane Iqbal receives Iraqi passport|date=20 May 2021|accessdate=4 August 2021|website=shafaq.com|language=Arabic|archive-date=8 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211208203849/https://shafaq.com/ar/%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%80%D8%A7%D8%B6%D8%A9/%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%A8-%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%B4%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B1-%D9%8A%D9%88%D9%86%D8%A7%D9%8A%D8%AA%D8%AF-%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%86-%D9%82%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%AA%D8%B3%D9%84%D9%85-%D8%AC%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B2-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%81%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%82%D9%8A|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="MEN">{{cite web|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/zidane-iqbal-manchester-united-beckham-21021488|title=Manchester United video suggests Zidane Iqbal may be the next David Beckham in the making|first=Daniel|last=Feliciano|date=10 July 2021|accessdate=4 August 2021|website=manchestereveningnews.co.uk|archive-date=20 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220520033650/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/zidane-iqbal-manchester-united-beckham-21021488|url-status=live}}</ref> In June 2021, he was called up to the [[Iraq national under-20 football team|Iraq under-20 team]] for the [[2021 Arab Cup U-20]]. However, Manchester United refused to let him travel, due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ina.iq/127701--.html|title=مانشستر يونايتد يرفض التحاق زيدان بمنتخب الشباب|trans-title=Manchester United refuse Zidane to join the youth team|date=10 June 2021|accessdate=4 August 2021|website=ina.iq|language=Arabic|archive-date=8 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211208212849/https://www.ina.iq/127701--.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In September 2021, Iqbal received his first call up to the [[Iraq national under-23 football team|Iraq under-23 team]] for a training camp in the United Arab Emirates. He made his debut on 4 September, against the [[United Arab Emirates national under-23 football team|UAE under-23 team]], making the starting line-up. In October 2021, Iqbal was named as part of the 23-man Iraq under-23 squad for the [[2021 WAFF U-23 Championship]] in Saudi Arabia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ifa.iq/23-%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%8B-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%A6%D9%85%D8%A9-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%AA%D8%AE%D8%A8%D9%86%D8%A7-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%88%D9%84%D9%85%D8%A8%D9%8A-%D9%84%D8%A8%D8%B7%D9%88-7575/|title=3 لاعباً في قائمة منتخبنا الأولمبي لبطولة غرب آسيا|trans-title=Iraqi Olympic team squad|date=1 October 2021|accessdate=2 October 2021|website=Iraq FA|language=Arabic|archive-date=2 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220702135531/https://ifa.iq/23-%d9%84%d8%a7%d8%b9%d8%a8%d8%a7%d9%8b-%d9%81%d9%8a-%d9%82%d8%a7%d8%a6%d9%85%d8%a9-%d9%85%d9%86%d8%aa%d8%ae%d8%a8%d9%86%d8%a7-%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%a3%d9%88%d9%84%d9%85%d8%a8%d9%8a-%d9%84%d8%a8%d8%b7%d9%88-7575/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 8 October, Iqbal scored his first goal for the under-23 team as the captain of his side.<ref>{{Cite web|date=9 October 2021|title=Zidane Iqbal captains Iraq under-23s and scores|url=https://www.unitedinfocus.com/academy/zidane-iqbal-captains-iraq-under-23s-and-scores/|access-date=8 November 2021|website=United In Focus|archive-date=11 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211111050521/https://www.unitedinfocus.com/academy/zidane-iqbal-captains-iraq-under-23s-and-scores/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Senior===
In January 2022, Iqbal was called up to the [[Iraq national football team|Iraq national team]] for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (AFC)|2022 FIFA World Cup qualifiers]] against [[Iran national football team|Iran]] and [[Lebanon national football team|Lebanon]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Zidane Iqbal: Iraq set to hand Manchester United teenager international debut away in Iran |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11667/12519326/zidane-iqbal-iraq-set-to-hand-manchester-united-teenager-international-debut-away-in-iran |website=Sky Sports |date=20 January 2022 |access-date=24 January 2022 |archive-date=28 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128072334/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11667/12519326/zidane-iqbal-iraq-set-to-hand-manchester-united-teenager-international-debut-away-in-iran |url-status=live }}</ref> He made his debut in a 1–0 loss to Iran on 27 January 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zidane Iqbal becomes 32nd international player in Manchester United squad |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/zidane-iqbal-manchester-united-internationals-22899229 |website=Manchester Evening News |date=27 January 2022 |access-date=27 January 2022 |archive-date=4 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220204024309/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/zidane-iqbal-manchester-united-internationals-22899229 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 26 March 2024, Iqbal scored his first international goal during the [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – AFC second round|2026 FIFA World Cup qualification]] match against [[Philippines national football team|Philippines]] in a 5–0 away win.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Web |first=G. C. |date=2024-03-26 |title=Philippines 0-5 Iraq - Philippine Football Federation |url=https://pff.org.ph/philippines-0-5-iraq/ |access-date=2025-08-19 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Iqbal was included in Iraq's 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cy526nrz39eo |title=Al-Hamadi and Iqbal named in Iraq's World Cup squad |website=BBC Sport |date=1 June 2026 |access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Iqbal is a versatile midfielder who mostly plays in the centre.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zidane Iqbal Positions |url=https://www.footballcritic.com/zidane-iqbal/player-positions/375195 |access-date=2022-10-15 |website=FootballCritic |language=en |archive-date=15 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015034427/https://www.footballcritic.com/zidane-iqbal/player-positions/375195 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Personal life==
As one of a small number of [[British Asians in association football]], Iqbal was part of an [[The Football Association|FA]] content series to support South Asian Heritage Month in 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2021/jul/27/fa-supports-south-asian-heritage-month-20210727|title=A New Content Series will be Released to Support South Asian Heritage Month|date=27 July 2021|accessdate=4 August 2021|website=thefa.com|archive-date=14 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214042050/https://www.thefa.com/news/2021/jul/27/fa-supports-south-asian-heritage-month-20210727|url-status=live}}</ref>

Iqbal is [[Muslims|Muslim]], and cites [[Mesut Özil]] as an inspiration for him.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/zidane-iqbal-interview-with-the-fa-to-mark-south-asian-heritage-month|title=Iqbal Enjoying the 'Rollercoaster Ride'|first=Matthew|last=Holt|date=3 August 2021|accessdate=4 August 2021|website=manutd.com|archive-date=4 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210804155031/https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/zidane-iqbal-interview-with-the-fa-to-mark-south-asian-heritage-month|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/zidane-iqbal-man-united-academy-21218237|title=Manchester United academy star Zidane Iqbal names his football idol|first=Liam|last=Wood|date=3 August 2021|accessdate=4 August 2021|website=manchestereveningnews.co.uk|archive-date=21 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220521194714/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/zidane-iqbal-man-united-academy-21218237|url-status=live}}</ref> Iqbal has stated in interviews that he is fluent in [[English language|English]] and can speak some [[Punjabi language|Punjabi]] and [[Arabic]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 March 2023 |title="They Were All Swinging Their Shoes" 🥴 {{!}} Zidane Iqbal {{!}} Spotlight Questions 💬 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IcrVh7d3X2U=3m41s |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230520232803/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IcrVh7d3X2U=3m41s |archive-date=20 May 2023 |access-date=20 May 2023 |website=YouTube |quote=Event occurs at 3:41}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mitten |first=Andy |title=Zidane Iqbal on identity, Iraq and his new start: ‘I needed to leave Manchester United to grow’ |url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/football/2025/10/12/zidane-iqbal-on-identity-iraq-and-his-new-start-i-needed-to-leave-manchester-united-to-grow/ |access-date=2026-10-07 |website=The National |language=en}}</ref>

'''Dylan Riley Williams''' (born 13 September 2003) is an English [[Association football|football]]er who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|left-back]] for {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe}} side [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref>{{Soccerway|dylan-willis/644837}}</ref>

==Club career==
Williams made his debut for [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] in a 2–0 FA Cup loss to [[Chorley F.C.|Chorley]] on 9 January 2021. He was one of fourteen players from [[Derby County F.C. Reserves and Academy|Derby County's academy]] to make their debut in the game, after the entirety of Derby's first team squad and coaching team were forced to isolate due to a [[COVID-19]] outbreak.<ref>{{cite news|title=Chorley 2–0 Derby County|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55574408|accessdate=10 August 2021|work=British Broadcasting Corporation|date=9 January 2021}}</ref> He made his second appearance, appearing alongside members of Derby County's first team, in a 3–3 Carabao Cup draw against [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]] on 10 August 2021.<ref>{{cite news|title=Derby County 3–3 Salford City|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58065959|accessdate=10 August 2021|work=British Broadcasting Corporation|date=10 August 2021}}</ref>

On 22 January 2022, he signed a professional contract with [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Dylan Williams|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/teams/academy/dylan-williams|accessdate=22 January 2022|work=Chelsea FC|date=28 January 2022}}</ref>

On 3 July 2024, Williams joined [[Burton Albion F.C.|Burton Albion]] on a season-long loan, with an obligation to buy if certain conditions are met.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dylan Williams bound for Burton |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/dylan-williams-bound-for-burton |access-date=4 July 2024 |publisher=Chelsea FC |date=4 July 2024}}</ref>

On 2 May 2025, it was announced that Williams would join Burton Albion permanently in the coming summer transfer window.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.burtonalbionfc.co.uk/news/2025/may/02/dylan-williams-completes-burton-albion-transfer-from-chelsea/ |access-date=2025-05-05 |website=www.burtonalbionfc.co.uk}}</ref>

On 20 July 2026, [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] announced the signing of Williams from [[Burton Albion F.C.|Burton Albion]] for an undisclosed fee, on a contract until the summer of 2028 with the option for an additional year.<ref>{{cite web |title=DYLAN WILLIAMS JOINS FROM BURTON ALBION |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/07/20/dylan-williams-joins-from-burton-albion/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=20 July 2026 |date=20 July 2026}}</ref>

'''Ibrahim Muhammad Said''' (born 15{{nbsp}}June 2002) is a Nigerian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].

==Club career==
===Early years===
A product of Dabo Babes Academy in Nigeria, Said gained international recognition following his strong performances at the [[2019 FIFA U-17 World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hat-trick hero Ibrahim Said vows Golden Eaglets will be world champions again – Score Nigeria |url=https://scorenigeria.com.ng/hat-trick-hero-ibrahim-said-vows-golden-eaglets-will-be-world-champions-again/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Viborg===
Despite receiving offers from other clubs, including [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] and [[İstanbul Başakşehir F.K.|İstanbul Başakşehir]],<ref name="TB290920">{{cite news |last1=Dehn |first1=Anders |date=29 September 2020 |title=Spilleren bekræfter selv: Viborg henter "den nye Victor Moses" |url=https://www.tipsbladet.dk/nyhed/1-division/spilleren-bekraefter-selv-viborg-henter-den-nye-victor-moses |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211027031931/https://www.tipsbladet.dk/nyhed/1-division/spilleren-bekraefter-selv-viborg-henter-den-nye-victor-moses |archive-date=27 October 2021 |access-date=29 September 2024 |work=Tipsbladet.dk |language=da}}</ref> and reportedly from English clubs [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Marshment |first1=James |date=15 December 2019 |title=EXCLUSIVE: Man City lead Liverpool, Chelsea for Nigeria sensation Said |url=https://www.teamtalk.com/news/exclusive-man-city-lead-liverpool-chelsea-for-nigeria-sensation |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221103130615/https://www.teamtalk.com/news/exclusive-man-city-lead-liverpool-chelsea-for-nigeria-sensation |archive-date=3 November 2022 |access-date=29 September 2024 |work=TEAMtalk}}</ref> Said ultimately moved to Denmark. The 18-year-old, described by Nigerian media as the next [[Victor Moses]],<ref name="TB290920" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Emmanuel |first1=Ifeanyi |date=30 October 2019 |title=Five Interesting Facts About Nigeria U17 Hat-trick Hero Dubbed The 'New Victor Moses' |url=https://www.allnigeriasoccer.com/read_news.php?nid=34171 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191031165142/https://www.allnigeriasoccer.com/read_news.php?nid=34171 |archive-date=31 October 2019 |access-date=29 September 2024 |work=All Nigeria Soccer}}</ref> signed a four-year contract with [[Danish 1st Division]] club [[Viborg FF]] on 21 October 2021.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kristensen |first1=Danni |date=21 October 2020 |title=Viborg FF handler igen – nigeriansk talent på kontrakt frem til 2024 |url=https://viborg-folkeblad.dk/sport/viborg-ff-handler-igen-nigeriansk-talent-paa-kontrakt-frem-til-2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240929152750/https://viborg-folkeblad.dk/sport/viborg-ff-handler-igen-nigeriansk-talent-paa-kontrakt-frem-til-2024 |archive-date=29 September 2024 |access-date=29 September 2024 |work=Viborg Folkeblad |language=da}}</ref>

After a few matches with Viborg's under-19 team, Said made his official debut in the [[Danish 1st Division]] on 16 April 2021, in a 4–0 win against [[Esbjerg fB]]. He started on the bench before replacing [[Davit Skhirtladze]] in the 86th minute.<ref>{{cite web |title=Viborg vs. Esbjerg 4–0: Summary |url=https://nr.soccerway.com/matches/2021/04/16/denmark/1st-division/viborg-ff/esbjerg-fb/3481835/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211025212531/https://nr.soccerway.com/matches/2021/04/16/denmark/1st-division/viborg-ff/esbjerg-fb/3481835/ |archive-date=25 October 2021 |access-date=29 September 2024 |website=Soccerway |publisher=Perform Group}}</ref> Said made three appearances that season, scoring one goal and helping Viborg secure promotion to the [[Danish Superliga]] for the 2021–22 season.<ref name="SW" /> His debut in the [[Danish Superliga]] came against [[FC Nordsjælland|Nordsjælland]] on 18 July 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nordsjælland vs. Viborg 1–2: Summary |url=https://nr.soccerway.com/matches/2021/07/18/denmark/superliga/fc-nordsjalland/viborg-ff/3510669/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230101153638/https://nr.soccerway.com/matches/2021/07/18/denmark/superliga/fc-nordsjalland/viborg-ff/3510669/ |archive-date=1 January 2023 |access-date=29 September 2024 |website=Soccerway |publisher=Perform Group}}</ref>

Starting in the [[2022–23 Danish Superliga|2022–23 season]], Said made regular appearances for Viborg. On 28 July 2022, in a [[2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League qualifying phase and play-off round (Main Path)|2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League]] qualifying match against [[FK Sūduva]], he scored in the opening minute as the only goal in a 1–0 victory for Viborg.<ref>{{cite web |date=28 July 2022 |title=History: Viborg 1-0 Sūduva {{!}} UEFA Conference League 2022/23 |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaconferenceleague/match/2035145/ |access-date=11 July 2025 |publisher=[[UEFA]]}}</ref> One month later, both he and his Viborg teammate [[Alassana Jatta]] were unable to travel to England for the club's Europa Conference League play-off against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] due to post-[[Brexit]] entry rules for non-EU citizens.<ref>{{cite news |date=17 August 2022 |title=Viborg lose two African players for West Ham playoff due to UK entry rules |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/aug/17/viborg-lose-two-african-players-for-west-ham-playoff-due-to-visa-problems |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230614012213/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/aug/17/viborg-lose-two-african-players-for-west-ham-playoff-due-to-visa-problems |archive-date=14 June 2023 |access-date=29 September 2024 |work=The Guardian}}</ref> Said finished the season with six goals from 41 appearances.<ref name="SB-2022">{{soccerbase season| id=140715| season=2022| name=Ibrahim Said| access-date=11 July 2025}}</ref>

The [[2023–24 Danish Superliga|following season]] saw fewer appearances for Said overall, and only three goals.<ref name="SB-2023">{{soccerbase season| id=140715| season=2023| name=Ibrahim Said| access-date=11 July 2025}}</ref> Viborg head coach [[Jakob Poulsen]] did not include Said in a Superliga match versus [[Silkeborg IF|Silkeborg]] on 4 August 2024 due to a violation of team rules, though Poulsen declined to elaborate further.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kristensen |first=Danni |date=6 August 2024 |title=Offensivspiller var udeladt af kamptruppen i Silkeborg: Havde overtrådt interne regler |trans-title=Offensive player was left out of the match squad in Silkeborg: Had violated internal rules |url=https://viborg-folkeblad.dk/viborgff/offensivspiller-var-udeladt-af-kamptruppen-i-silkeborg-havde-overtraadt-interne-regler |access-date=7 July 2025 |work=Viborg Folkeblad |language=da}}</ref> By March 2025, Said was dropped from Viborg's lineup without explanation by the club.<ref>{{cite web |last=Grønborg |first=Matias |date=2 March 2025 |title=Viborg er uden Isak Jensen og Said |trans-title=Viborg is without Isak Jensen and Said |url=https://bold.dk/fodbold/klubber/viborg/nyheder/viborg-er-uden-isak-jensen-og-said |access-date=7 July 2025 |publisher=bold.dk |language=da}}</ref> His final appearance for Viborg came on 24 February, in a 4–1 loss to Silkeborg.<ref>{{cite web |date=24 February 2025 |title=Viborg FF vs Silkeborg IF (1-4), 3F Superliga 2025 |url=https://bold.dk/fodbold/kamp/viborg-ff-vs-silkeborg-if/3f-superliga/16174419/kampinfo |access-date=11 July 2025 |publisher=bold.dk |language=da}}</ref> He finished the season with 16 appearances, unable to score any goals.<ref name="SB-2024">{{soccerbase season| id=140715| season=2024| name=Ibrahim Said| access-date=11 July 2025}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
As Viborg began preparations for the [[2025–26 Viborg FF season|2025–26 season]], Said was not included in the lineup for a friendly match versus [[FC Fredericia]] as he was allowed to pursue interest from other clubs.<ref>{{cite web |last=Christensen |first=Tobias Bundgaard |date=5 July 2025 |title=Udeladt af kamptrup: Viborg FF-spiller kigger efter ny klub |trans-title=Left out of match squad: Viborg FF player is looking for a new club |url=https://viborg-folkeblad.dk/viborgff/udeladt-af-kamptrup-viborg-ff-spiller-kigger-efter-ny-klub |access-date=11 July 2025 |work=Viborg Folkeblad |language=da}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Grønberg |first=Matias |date=5 July 2025 |title=Ibrahim Said afsøger mulighed for klubskifte |trans-title=Ibrahim Said is exploring the possibility of changing clubs |url=https://bold.dk/fodbold/klubber/viborg/nyheder/ibrahim-said-afsoger-mulighed-for-klubskifte |access-date=11 July 2025 |publisher=bold.dk |language=da}}</ref> On 11 July 2025, his Said solgt til Motherwell FC |trans-title=Ibrahim Said sold to Motherwell FC |url=https://vff.dk/nyhed/sport/15109-ibrahim-said-solgt-til-motherwell-fc |access-date=11 July 2025 |publisher=Viborg FF |language=da}}</ref> He joined on a two-year contract, with an option for an additional year.<ref>{{cite web |date=11 July 2025 |title=Well sign 'exciting & versatile' winger Said F.C.|Celtic]] 2–0.<ref>{{cite news |title=Scottish Premiership: Nancy's Celtic slump to fifth defeat as Said inspires Motherwell |newspaper=The Guardian |date=30 December 2025 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/dec/30/scottish-premiership-motherwell-celtic-rangers-st-mirren |access-date=2 January 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
In [[2019 FIFA U-17 World Cup|2019]], he participated in the [[FIFA U-17 World Cup]] for [[Nigeria national under-17 football team|Nigeria]], where he played all four matches, and made himself especially noticeable when he scored a [[hat-trick (association football)|hat-trick]] in the team's 3–2 victory over [[Ecuador national under-17 football team|Ecuador]].<ref name="VFF-profile" /><ref>{{cite news |date=29 October 2019 |title=Ibrahim Said's hat-trick gives Golden Eaglets victory over Ecuador |url=https://pmnewsnigeria.com/2019/10/29/ibrahim-saids-hat-trick-gives-golden-eaglets-victory-over-ecuador/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191030132909/https://pmnewsnigeria.com/2019/10/29/ibrahim-saids-hat-trick-gives-golden-eaglets-victory-over-ecuador/ |archive-date=30 October 2019 |access-date=29 September 2024 |newspaper=[[P.M. '''Thomas Lance Sparrow''' (born 6 December 2002) is a Welsh professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe}} club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] and the [[Wales national under-21 football team|Wales under-21 national team]].

==Club career==
===Stoke City===
Sparrow joined [[Stoke City F.C. Under-23s and Academy|Stoke City]] from [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C. Development Squad and Academy|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] as a 14-year old.<ref>{{cite web |title=Stoke City teenager on cusp of first team breakthrough in new position |url=https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/stoke-city-tom-sparrow-position-6955987 |website=Stoke Sentinel |date=15 April 2022 |access-date=26 May 2022}}</ref> In October 2021 Sparrow joined [[National League North]] side [[AFC Telford United]] on a one-month youth loan.<ref>{{cite web |title=MIDFIELDER SIGNS ON A YOUTH LOAN FROM STOKE CITY |url=https://www.telfordunited.com/news/midfielder-signs-on-a-youth-loan-from-stoke-city/ |website=AFC Telford United |date=15 October 2021 |access-date=26 May 2022}}</ref> Sparrow made his professional debut on 7 May 2022 in a 1–1 draw against [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sparrow's debut delight |url=https://www.stokecityfc.com/news/2022/may/07/sparrow-s-debut-delight/ |website=Stoke City |date=7 May 2022 |access-date=7 May 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Stoke City 1–1 Coventry City |work=BBC Sport |date=7 May 2022 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61280945 |access-date=26 May 2022}}</ref>

On 7 January 2023, Sparrow joined [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] on loan for the remainder of the [[2022–23 Scottish Championship|2022–23]] season, making his debut the same day in a 1–0 defeat away at [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sparrow heads out on loan |url=https://www.stokecityfc.com/news/2023/january/07/sparrow-heads-out-on-loan/ |website=Stoke City |date=7 January 2023 |access-date=7 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Ayr United 1-0 Hamilton Academical |work=BBC Sport |date=7 January 2023 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64132747 |access-date=7 January 2023}}</ref> He helped Hamilton win the [[Scottish Challenge Cup]] after they beat [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] 1–0 in the [[2023 Scottish Challenge Cup final|final]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Raith Rovers 0-1 Hamilton Academical |work=BBC Sport |date=25 March 2023 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65008695 |access-date=27 May 2023}}</ref> Sparrow made 17 appearances for Accies as they suffered relegation after losing on penalties to [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] in the playoffs.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hamilton Academical 2–1 Airdrieonians |work=BBC Sport |date=20 May 2023 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65579896 |access-date=27 May 2023}}</ref> On 5 September 2023, Sparrow joined [[National League North]] side [[Chester F.C.|Chester]] on a three-month loan.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tom Sparrow joins Chester on loan |url=https://www.stokecityfc.com/news/2023/september/05/tom-sparrow-joins-chester-on-loan/ |website=Stoke City |date=5 September 2023 |access-date=5 September 2023}}</ref> Sparrow made twelve appearances for Chester before returning to Stoke in January 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sparrow returns from loan spell |url=https://www.stokecityfc.com/news/2024/january/03/sparrow-returns-from-loan-spell/ |website=Stoke City |date=3 January 2024 |access-date=3 January 2024}}</ref> He was released by Stoke at the end of the [[2023–24 Stoke City F.C. season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Potters release contracts update |url=https://www.stokecityfc.com/news/2024/may/21/potters-release-contracts-update/ '''Martin Moormann''' (born 30 April 2001) is an Austrian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] for [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].

==Club career==
Moormann is a youth product of Sierndorf, [[SV Horn|Horn]] and AKA St. Pölten, before moving to [[SK Rapid Wien|Rapid Wien]] in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skrapid.at/de/startseite/news/news/aktuelles/2018/04/nachwuchs-nationalteamspieler-wechselt-nach-huetteldorf|title=Nachwuchs-Nationalteamspieler wechselt nach Hütteldorf!|website=SK Rapid}}</ref> He began his professional career with their reserves, before debuting for their senior team in a 3–0 [[Austrian Cup]] win over [[SKU Amstetten|Amstetten]] on 28 October 2021.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.90minuten.at/de/red/presseschau/sky/2021/dezember/martin-moormann-ueber-sein-erstes-derby---wir-haben-dann-moral-bewiesen-/|title=Martin Moormann über sein erstes Derby: "Wir haben dann Moral bewiesen" (90minuten.at)|website=www.90minuten.at}}</ref> He signed a professional contract with the club on 11 March 2022, keeping him at the club until June 2025.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.skrapid.at/de/startseite/news/news/aktuelles/2022/03/martin-moormann-bleibt-rapidler|title=Martin Moormann bleibt Rapidler|website=SK Rapid}}</ref>

On 3 July 2026, [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] announced the signing of Moormann, on a contract until the summer of 2028.<ref>{{cite web |title=Welcoming Martin Moormann to ML1 |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/07/03/welcoming-martin-moormann-to-ml1/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=3 July 2026 |date=3 July 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Moormann is a youth international for Austria, having represented the [[Austria national under-16 football team|Austria U15]]s, [[Austria national under-17 football team|U17]]s, [[Austria national under-18 football team|U18]]s, and [[Austria national under-21 football team|U21]]s.<ref name="auto1"/>

==Personal life==
Moormann is a fan of the English football club [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref name="auto"/>

'''Tawanda Jethro Maswanhise''' (born 20 November 2002) is a Zimbabwean [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] and the [[Zimbabwe national football team]].

==Club career==
Maswanhise started his career in the academy of [[EFL Championship]] side [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lcfc.com/news/2202810|title=Maswanhise: Sporting Heritage|website=Leicester City F.C.}}</ref>

On 6 January 2024, Maswanhise made his senior debut for Leicester as a 77th-minute substitute for [[Wanya Marçal]] during a 3–2 away win against [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] in the third round of the [[FA Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67894607|title=Millwall 2-3 Leicester City: Clinical Foxes reach FA Cup fourth round|publisher=BBC Sport|date=6 January 2024}}</ref> However, he was released by the club at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Leicester City retained list in full with nine players leaving and four offered new contracts |url=https://www.leicestermercury.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/leicester-city-retained-list-full-9333800 |publisher=Leicester Mercury |date=10 June 2024 |access-date=18 August 2024}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
On 18 August 2024, after going on trial with different clubs, Maswanhise joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]. He signed a short-term deal until January 2025.<ref>{{cite news |title=Maswanhise 'ready to make impact' |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c78l0kdgd2mo |publisher=BBC Sport |date=18 August 2024 |access-date=18 August 2024}}</ref> Later on the same day, he made his debut for the club as a 58th-minute substitute in a 1–0 win against [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] in the second round of the [[Scottish League Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Motherwell vs Kilmarnock: Scottish League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cwy7jdm82vjt |publisher=BBC Sport |date=18 August 2024 |access-date=19 August 2024}}</ref> On 14 August 2025, Motherwell announced that Maswanhise had extended his contract with the club, until the summer of 2027, with the option of an additional year. In his second season with the club, Maswanhise finished as the top scorer in the division.

==International career==
On 26 March 2024, Maswanhise made his senior [[Zimbabwe national football team|Zimbabwe]] debut in a 3–1 loss against [[Kenya national football team|Kenya]].

On 11 December 2025, Maswanhise was called by [[Zimbabwe national football team|Zimbabwe]] for their participation in the [[2025 Africa Cup of Nations]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The wait is over. Here is the final Warriors AFCON 2025 squad to represent Zimbabwe in Morocco. |url=https://x.com/online_zifa/status/1999089805595181155/photo/1 |website=x.com/online_zifa |publisher=Zimbabwe Football Association Twitter |access-date=11 December 2025 |date=11 December 2025}}</ref> On 29 December 2025, in their last group match against South Africa, he scored a goal in the 17th minute.

He withdrew from the Zimbabwean side to play in the Four nations tournament in end of March 2025 due to a small issue as per reports by his club, Motherwell.

==Personal life==

He is the son of Zimbabwean sprinter [[Jeffrey Maswanhise]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newsday.co.zw/2021/08/maswanhise-likely-to-snub-warriors/|title='Maswanhise likely to snub Warriors'|publisher=newsday.co.zw}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.herald.co.zw/foxes-starlets-father-makes-warriors-pledge/|title=Foxes starlet's father makes Warriors pledge|publisher=herald.co.zw}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newzimbabwe.com/maswanhise-continues-scoring-spree-at-leicester-city/|title=Maswanhise Continues Scoring Spree At Leicester City|publisher=newzimbabwe.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.soccer24.co.zw/2021/08/02/im-getting-a-lot-of-love-from-zim-leicester-city-star/|title=I’m getting a lot of love from Zim: Leicester City star|publisher=soccer24.co.zw}}</ref>
