'''Joseph Shaun Hodge''' (born 14 September 2002) is an Irish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=Gibson |first=Scott |date=2026-08-12 |title=Joe Hodge arrives for undisclosed fee |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/08/12/joe-hodge-arrives-for-undisclosed-fee/ |access-date=2026-08-12 |publisher=Motherwell FC |language=en}}</ref> Born in Manchester, England, Hodge made his senior [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] debut in June 2026.

==Club career==
===Manchester City===
Hodge started his career with [[Premier League]] side [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-40835366.html|title=After swapping City for Black Country, Wolves' Hodge eager to bare teeth |date=23 March 2022 |publisher=irishexaminer.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.otbsports.com/soccer/joe-hodge-shane-keegan-1082244|title=Joe Hodge would be a bigger loss to Ireland than Grealish or Declan Rice|publisher=otbsports.com}}</ref> Before the 2021 season, he was sent on loan to [[League of Ireland Premier Division]] club [[Derry City F.C.|Derry City]] but departed the club without making a competitive appearance due to injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/joe-hodge-looking-forward-with-no-regrets-over-manchester-city-exit-41481560.html|title=Joe Hodge looking forward with 'no regrets' over Manchester City exit|publisher=independent.ie}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.derryjournal.com/sport/football/man-citys-joe-hodge-confident-he-can-meet-physical-demands-league-ireland-3131014|title=Man City's Joe Hodge confident he can meet physical demands of League of Ireland|publisher=derryjournal.com}}</ref>

===Wolverhampton Wanderers===
In 2021, Hodge signed for English [[Premier League]] club [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://punditarena.com/football/ronan-calvert/ireland-underage-stars-premier-league-cup-final-wolves-joe-hodge/|title=Ireland underage stars gear up for Premier League Cup Final|date=13 May 2022 |publisher=punditarena.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/2022/07/30/premier-league-no-irish-need-apply-almost/|title=Premier League: No Irish need apply...almost |publisher=irishtimes.com}}</ref> He made his [[Premier League]] debut against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] on 8 October 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.balls.ie/football/stephen-kenny-joe-hodge-410336|title=Stephen Kenny Is Clearly A Huge Fan Of Ireland U17 Midfielder Joe Hodge|publisher=balls.ie}}</ref> On 1 February 2024, Hodge was loaned to [[EFL Championship]] club [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Joe Hodge completes loan switch from Wolves |url=https://www.qpr.co.uk/news/2024/february/01/joe-hodge-completes-loan-switch-from-wolves/ |access-date=2 February 2024 |publisher=Queens Park Rangers FC |date=1 February 2024}}</ref> On 28 August 2024, he was loaned out to [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] for the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.extratime.com/articles/34620/joe-hodge-joins-huddersfield-town-on-loan-from-wolves/|title=Joe Hodge joins Huddersfield Town on loan from Wolves|first=Extratime|last=Team|website=extratime.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wolves.co.uk/news/loan-watch/20240828-hodge-completes-new-loan-switch/|title=Hodge completes new loan switch|website=Wolverhampton Wanderers FC}}</ref>

===Tondela===
On 18 July 2025, Hodge joined newly promoted [[Primeira Liga]] club [[C.D. Tondela|Tondela]] on a four-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cdtondela.pt/noticia/4371|trans-title=JOE HODGE IS A GOLDEN-GREEN|title=JOE HODGE É AURIVERDE|language=Portuguese|website=cdtondela.pt|date=18 July 2025|accessdate=18 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wolves.co.uk/news/mens-first-team/20250718-hodge-completes-permanent-move/|title=Hodge completes permanent move|website=www.wolves.co.uk|date=18 July 2025|accessdate=18 July 2025}}</ref> He scored 1 goal in 29 appearances in all competitions during his first season with the club, as they were relegated to [[Liga Portugal 2]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe545195/joe-hodge/|title=Joe Hodge: Career, Stats & Clubs|website=worldfootball.net}}</ref> In August 2026, he was reportedly due to sign for an unnamed [[Scottish Premiership]] club, but the move was on the verge of collapse due to a compensation dispute between Tondela and Hodge's former club Wolverhampton Wanderers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.balls.ie/football/ireland-joe-hodge-transfer-dispute-660968|title=Ireland Star's Summer Move Reportedly In Jeopardy Due To Dispute With Former Club|first=Gary|last=Connaughton|date=4 August 2026|website=Balls.ie}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.footballtransfers.com/en/transfer-news/gb-sct-premier-league/2026/07/joe-hodge-to-scotland-transfer-could-collapse-due-to-wolves-clause|title=EXCLUSIVE: Wolves and Tondela holding up Joe Hodge move to Scottish Premiership|first=Ronan|last=Murphy|date=31 July 2026|website=FootballTransfers}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
On 12 August 2026, Hodge joined [[Scottish Premiership]] side [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] for an undisclosed fee on a two-year contract with the option of a third year.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/motherwell-sign-ireland-midfielder-joe-hodge-from-portuguese-side-tondela/a/159918845.html|title=Motherwell sign Ireland midfielder Joe Hodge from Portuguese side Tondela|date=12 August 2026|website=Irish Independent}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cx2m15lxpj0o|title=Motherwell news: Republic of Ireland midfielder Joe Hodge joins for undisclosed fee|date=12 August 2026|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==International career==
Hodge played at several youth levels for the [[Republic of Ireland]] and captained the [[Republic of Ireland national under-21 football team|Republic of Ireland U21]] side.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5jt2UwOCZOE|title=Joe Hodge named Ireland U21 captain |date=24 March 2023 |publisher=FAI TV}}</ref> On 5 June 2026, Hodge made his senior [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] debut, as a substitute in a 1–1 draw with [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada]] at the [[Saputo Stadium]] in [[Montreal]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.balls.ie/football/four-debuts-as-ireland-battle-back-to-earn-credible-draw-with-world-cup-co-hosts-canada-656618|title=Four Debuts As Ireland Battle Back To Earn Credible Draw With World Cup Co-Hosts Canada|first=Donny|last=Mahoney|date=6 June 2026|website=Balls.ie}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-41857920.html|title=Hallgrímsson salutes Ireland resolve as Ogbene leads fightback in draw with Canada|first=Joe|last=Callaghan|date=6 June 2026|website=Irish Examiner}}</ref>

'''Jordan Yamoah Amissah''' (born 2 August 2001) is a German professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{Scottish football updater|DundeeUn}} club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].

==Early life==
Of Ghanaian descent,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://footballghana.com/sheffield-united-goalkeeper-jordan-amissah-set-to-earn-black-stars-call-up-reports|title=Sheffield United goalkeeper Jordan Amissah set to earn Black Stars call up - Reports|website=Footballghana}}</ref> Amissah was born on 2 August 2001 in [[Germany]]. Growing up, he supported German side [[FC Schalke 04]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressandjournal.co.uk/fp/sport/football/ross-county/6722192/ross-county-analysis-goalkeeper-jordan-amissah/|title=Analysis: Have Ross County struck goalkeeping gold with German giants-schooled Jordan Amissah?|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[The Press and Journal]]|date=28 March 2026|access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Sheffield United===
Amissah is a youth product of the academies of the German clubs Holsterhausen Herne, [[VfL Bochum]], [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] and [[Borussia Dortmund]] before moving to England with the youth sides of [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ghanasummary.com/ghanasoccernet/17361/exclusive-young-ghanaian-goalkeeper-jordan-amissah-joins-sheffield-united|title=EXCLUSIVE: Young Ghanaian goalkeeper Jordan Amissah joins Sheffield United|website=GhanaSummary}}</ref> On 21 May 2021, he signed his first professional contract with Sheffield United.<ref name="auto"/> He began his senior career on loan with [[Guiseley A.F.C.|Guiseley]] in the [[National League North]] for the first half of the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://guiseleyafc.co.uk/amissah-makes-it-a-fab-four-for-guiseley/|title=Amissah Makes It A Fab Four For Guiseley|date=4 January 2025}}</ref> In January 2022 he was loaned to [[Spennymoor Town F.C.|Spennymoor Town]] for the second half of the National League North Season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spennymoortownfc.co.uk/jordan-amissah/|title=Jordan Amissah}}</ref> He made his professional debut with Sheffield United in a 1–1 [[EFL Championship]] tie with [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] on 26 August 2022, coming on as a substitute in the 78th minute after the starting goalkeeper [[Wes Foderingham]] fell ill.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thestar.co.uk/sport/football/sheffield-united/sheffield-united-suffer-wes-foderingham-injury-blow-as-goalkeeper-limps-off-at-luton-town-3821685|title=Sheffield United suffer Wes Foderingham injury blow as goalkeeper limps off at Luton Town|date=26 August 2022|website=www.thestar.co.uk}}</ref> In January 2023, Amissah joined [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Burton Albion F.C.|Burton Albion]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.burtonalbionfc.co.uk/news/2023/january/0601-amissah/|title=BURTON ALBION SIGN GOALKEEPER JORDAN AMISSAH ON LOAN FROM SHEFFIELD UNITED|website=www.burtonalbionfc.co.uk|date=6 January 2023|accessdate=6 January 2023}}</ref> Amissah made his debut for Burton Albion in the FA Cup in a 1–0 defeat to [[Grimsby Town F.C.|Grimsby Town]] on 7 January. A week later, he made his [[EFL League One|League One]] debut in a 4–0 defeat to [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]]. It wasn't until 3 May that he would make an appearance in goal, in a 1–0 victory over [[Cambridge United F.C.|Cambridge United]].

On 29 May 2024, Sheffield United announced he would be released in the summer when his contract expired.<ref>{{Cite web |last=FC |first=Sheffield United |date=29 May 2024 |title=Retained and released list |url=https://www.sufc.co.uk/news/2024/may/29/retained-list/ |access-date=29 May 2024 |website=Sheffield United FC}}</ref> He spent time in July 2024 on trial with [[Scottish Championship]] club [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], appearing on the bench in a friendly against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] played at the [[University of Glasgow]]’s sports complex in Garscube on 3 July.

===Ross County===
On 6 December 2024, Amissah signed for Scottish club [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] on a short-term deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 December 2024 |title=Ross County sign Jordan Amissah on short-term deal |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/clyggv8kllqo.amp |access-date=7 December 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-gb}}</ref> In January 2025, Amissah allegedly received a [[Racism in association football|racially abusive]] social media message after a match against Aberdeen.<ref>🖉{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c4gp56dy5p5o|title=Ross County investigate racial abuse of goalkeeper Jordan Amissah|date=3 January 2025|website=BBC News}}</ref> On 7 January 2025, he extended his deal until the end of the season.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/jordan-amissah-extends-stay-with-the-staggies|title=Jordan Amissah extends stay with the Staggies|website=www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk|date=7 January 2025|accessdate=7 January 2025}}</ref> 

On 25 March 2025, Amissah signed a two-year deal to remain with ''the Staggies'' until June 2027.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk/news-items/jordan-amissah-agrees-new-deal-until-2027|title=Jordan Amissah agrees new deal until 2027|website=www.rosscountyfootballclub.co.uk|date=25 March 2025|accessdate=30 June 2025}}</ref> He suffered relegation from the [[Scottish Premiership|top flight]] to the [[Scottish Championship|second tier]] while playing for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5530350/jordan-amissah-dundee-united-everything-need-know/|title=Everything you need to know about Dundee United arrival Jordan Amissah: Crossing fierce divide, baptism of fire and poignant promise|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[The Courier (newspaper)|The Courier]]|date=3 July 2026|access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref>

===Burton Albion===
On 30 June 2025, Amissah returned to League One side Burton Albion on an initial two-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.burtonalbionfc.co.uk/news/2025/june/30/jordan-amissah-signs-for-burton-albion/|title=JORDAN AMISSAH SIGNS FOR BURTON ALBION|website=www.burtonalbionfc.co.uk|date=30 June 2025|accessdate=30 June 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Despite being born and raised in Germany, Amissah said in 2023 that playing for Ghana was "non-negotiable".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mobile.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/SportsArchive/Playing-for-Ghana-is-non-negotiable-Germany-born-Ghanaian-Jordan-Amissah-1763846|title=Playing for Ghana is non negotiable - Germany born Ghanaian Jordan Amissah}}</ref> He is a Ghana youth international.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thestar.co.uk/sport/football/sheffield-united/sheffield-united-mans-pride-after-penalty-save-ahead-of-african-cup-of-nations-bow-4193728|title=Sheffield United man’s pride after shining on international stage ahead of tournament debut|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[The Star (Sheffield newspaper)|The Star]]|date=22 June 2023|access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref>

'''Jardell Kanga''' (born 13 December 2005) is a Swedish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as an [[attacking midfielder]] or [[winger (association football)|winger]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]

==Club career==
Kanga is a youth product of [[IF Brommapojkarna|Brommapojkarna]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ettanfotboll.se/division-ett/talangportratt-jardell-kanga/|title=Talangporträtt: Jardell Kanga|website=Ettanfotboll|access-date=28 September 2022|archive-date=1 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001165610/https://ettanfotboll.se/division-ett/talangportratt-jardell-kanga/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He began his senior career with them in 2021 in the [[Ettan Fotboll|Ettan]] and became their youngest ever debutant at 15 years old and 3 months, their youngest ever goalscorer, and helped them achieve promotion into the [[Superettan]] that season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fotbolldirekt.se/2021/08/23/avslojar-nya-intresset-for-bp-s-15-arige-jattetalang|title=AVSLÖJAR: Flera storklubbar spionerar på svenskt underbarn|website=Fotbolldirekt – Experten på svensk fotboll|date=23 August 2021 }}</ref> On 20 January 2022, he signed with German [[Bundesliga]] club [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], and was assigned to their under-19s.<ref>{{cite press release |title=Swedish talent Jardell Kanga strengthens U19 squad |url=https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/u19/swedish-talent-jardell-kanga-strengthens-u19-squad |website=Bayer 04 Leverkusen |access-date=26 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240226192443/https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/u19/swedish-talent-jardell-kanga-strengthens-u19-squad |archive-date=26 February 2024 |date=20 January 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref> In September 2022, he was named by English newspaper ''[[The Guardian]]'' as one of the best players born in 2005 worldwide.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2022/sep/28/next-generation-2022-60-of-the-best-young-talents-in-world-football|title=Next Generation 2022: 60 of the best young talents in world football|first1=Marcus|last1=Christenson|first2=Steven|last2=Bloor|first3=Garry|last3=Blight|date=28 September 2022|accessdate=28 September 2022|work=The Guardian}}</ref>

On 1 February 2024, Kanga joined [[De Graafschap]] in the Dutch second-tier [[Eerste Divisie]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=De Graafschap|url=https://www.degraafschap.nl/nieuws/de-graafschap-trekt-jardell-kanga-aan|title=De Graafschap trekt Jardell Kanga aan|trans-title=De Graafschap signs Jardell Kanga|date=1 February 2024|access-date=3 February 2024|language=nl}}</ref> He made his debut for the ''Superboeren'' on 9 February, replacing [[David Flakus Bosilj]] in the 74th minute of a 2–0 home loss to [[Willem II (football club)|Willem II]].<ref>{{cite web |title=De Graafschap vs. Willem II 0–2: Summary |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2024/02/09/netherlands/eerste-divisie/bv-de-graafschap/sbv-willem-ii-tilburg/4097451/ |website=Soccerway |publisher=Perform Group |access-date=26 February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Willem II verstiert feestje ter ere van 70 jaar De Graafschap |url=https://www.vi.nl/nieuws/willem-ii-verstiert-feestje-ter-ere-van-70-jaar-de-graafschap |access-date=26 February 2024 |work=Voetbal International |date=9 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240210030115/https://www.vi.nl/nieuws/willem-ii-verstiert-feestje-ter-ere-van-70-jaar-de-graafschap |archive-date=10 February 2024 |language=nl}}</ref>

On 13 July 2024, Kanga signed for Swedish side [[Hammarby Fotboll|Hammarby IF]] on a contract until December 2028.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hammarbyfotboll.se/nyheter/jardell-kanga-klar-foer-bajen|title=Jardell Kanga klar för Bajen|language=sv|publisher=Hammarby IF|date=13 July 2024|access-date=31 July 2024}}</ref>

On 2 April 2025, Kanga was loaned to [[Veikkausliiga]] club [[Ilves (football)|Ilves]] with an option-to-buy.<ref>[https://www.ilvesfootball.com/jardell-kanga-liittyy-ilveksen-riveihin-lainasopimuksella/ Jardell Kanga liittyy Ilveksen riveihin lainasopimuksella], ilvesfootball.com, 2 April 2025</ref> On 19 July, his transfer was made permanent for an undisclosed fee. Kanga and Ilves signed a contract until the end of 2027.<ref>[https://www.ilvesfootball.com/ilves-kaytti-osto-optionsa-jardell-kangalle-kauden-2027-loppuun-ulottuva-sopimus/ ILVES KÄYTTI OSTO-OPTIONSA – JARDELL KANGALLE KAUDEN 2027 LOPPUUN ULOTTUVA SOPIMUS], ilvesfootball.com, 19 July 2025</ref>

===Motherwell===
On 28 August 2026, Kanga joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on a three-year contract,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c1e57qdn218o|title=Motherwell buy Sweden U21 forward Kanga|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=August 28, 2026|access-date=August 28, 2026}}</ref> for an initial €400,000 transfer fee, which could reach €1 million due to bonuses.<ref>[https://www.is.fi/veikkausliiga/art-2000012238722.html Ilveksen tähtipelaajan lähtö varmistui – ruotsalaistieto: rahaa tulee iso potti], [[Ilta-Sanomat]], 25 August 2026</ref>

==International career==
Kanga is a youth international for Sweden having played for the [[Sweden men's national under-17 football team|Sweden U17]]s, and is their record goalscorer at that level.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jardell Kanga med svenskt målrekord i P17-EM |url=https://www.svenskfotboll.se/nyheter/landslag/2022/05/p05-jardell-kanga-rekord-p17-em/ |access-date=26 February 2024 |work=Svensk Fotboll |date=21 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509160708/https://www.svenskfotboll.se/nyheter/landslag/2022/05/p05-jardell-kanga-rekord-p17-em/ |archive-date=9 May 2023 |language=sv}}</ref> He represented the country at the [[2022 UEFA European Under-17 Championship]], where they were eliminated at the group stage.

==Personal life==
Born in Sweden, Kanga is of DR Congolese descent.<ref>{{cite news |title=Euro U-17 stars today, African superstars tomorrow? |url=https://www.goal.com/en/lists/euro-u-17-stars-today-african-superstars-tomorrow/blt7cb7226e6bc242b4 |access-date=26 February 2024 |work=GOAL |date=17 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220930011514/https://www.goal.com/en/lists/euro-u-17-stars-today-african-superstars-tomorrow/blt7cb7226e6bc242b4 |archive-date=30 September 2022}}</ref> He is the cousin of the Swedish footballer [[Josafat Mendes]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Parker |first1=Cindy |title=Jardell kanga längd |url=https://duffysblog.com/2022/05/24/jardell-kanga-langd/ |website=Duffy's Blog |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220928152600/https://duffysblog.com/2022/05/24/jardell-kanga-langd/ |archive-date=28 September 2022 |language=sv |date=24 May 2022 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Jake Max Girdwood-Reich''' ({{IPA|yi|raɪx|lang}} {{respell|rike}};<ref>https://www.instagram.com/reel/DO7XCmGCfrr/?igsh=MWkzYWk3ZmFjd2NpYw==</ref> born 26 May 2004) is an Australian professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a central defender for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]. A [[utility player|versatile]] player, Girdwood-Reich can also be deployed as a defensive midfielder.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/st-louis-city-acquire-jake-girdwood-reich-from-sydney-fc#:~:text=%22His%20ability%20to%20play%20as,will%20help%20him%20fit%20in.%22&text=Girdwood%2DReich%20arrives%20after%20tallying,45%20matches%20for%20Sydney%20FC. |title=St. Louis CITY acquire Jake Girdwood-Reich from Sydney FC |publisher=MLSsoccer staff |date=3 June 2024 |access-date=19 July 2024 }}</ref>

== Early life ==
Jake Max Girdwood-Reich was born on 26 May 2004<ref name="soccerway"/> in [[Clovelly, New South Wales]] .<ref>{{cite web |last1=Benjamin |first1=Jonathan |title=Girdwood-Reich nets Israeli's jersey |url=https://www.jwire.com.au/girdwood-reich-nets-israelis-jersey/ |publisher=J-Wire |access-date=15 November 2023 |language=en |date=20 November 2022}}</ref> He is of [[Jewish Australians|Jewish]] descent through his mother, with his maternal grandmother is a [[Holocaust survivor]], and [[Scottish Australians|Scottish]] descent through his father.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stljewishlight.org/news/news-local/st-louis-city-sc-signs-jewish-australian-midfielder/|title=St. Louis City SC signs Jewish Australian midfielder|first=Bill|last=Motchan|publisher=[[STL Jewish Light]]|date=6 June 2024}}</ref> His mother briefly worked with [[UNICEF]] in [[Sydney]], which eventually partnered with [[Sydney FC]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sydney FC's Unicef Partnership Given Thumbs Up |url=https://sydneyfc.com/news/sydney-fcs-unicef-partnership-given-thumbs |publisher=Sydney FC |access-date=15 November 2023 |date=28 February 2012}}</ref> Girdwood-Reich grew up a Sydney FC supporter and became a member when he was six years old.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sydney FC's Most Loyal Fan Turned Player? |url=https://sydneyfc.com/news/sydney-fcs-most-loyal-fan-turned-player |publisher=Sydney FC |access-date=15 November 2023 |date=15 July 2022}}</ref>

He is also a supporter of [[Premier League]] club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] through the influence of the Scottish family of his father. Girdwood-Reich attended Clovelly Public School and [[Endeavour Sports High School]], playing for both the school football teams and state school teams.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ambitious Youngster Girdwoood-Reich Making His Mark In The NPL |url=https://sydneyfc.com/news/ambitious-youngster-girdwood-reich-making-his-mark-npl |publisher=Sydney FC |access-date=15 November 2023 |date=12 July 2021}}</ref><ref name="ref1">{{cite web |last1=Benjamin |first1=Jonathan |title=Jake signs with Sydney FC |url=https://www.jwire.com.au/jake-signs-with-sydney-fc/ |website=J-Wire |access-date=15 November 2023 |language=en |date=12 June 2022}}</ref> Outside of school, he played junior football for [[Sydney Uni SFC|Sydney University]], [[Sydney Olympic FC|Sydney Olympic]] and Scottish club [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]].<ref name="ref1"/> Girdwood-Reich later played in the under-13s for [[APIA Leichhardt FC|APIA Leichhardt]] before signing for [[Sydney FC Youth]] at the age of 12.<ref name="ref1"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Jake earns contract extension with Sky Blues |url=https://www.australianjewishnews.com/jake-earns-contract-extension-with-sky-blues/ |website=Australian Jewish News |access-date=15 November 2023 |date=28 July 2023}}</ref> He also played [[futsal]] for Mascot Vipers and the NSW representative futsal team.<ref name="ref1"/><ref name="ref2">{{cite web |last1=Benjamin |first1=Jonathan |title=Two mates debut the A-League |url=https://www.jwire.com.au/two-mates-debut-the-a-league/ |website=J-Wire |access-date=15 November 2023 |language=en |date=3 November 2022}}</ref>

== Club career ==
===Sydney FC===
Girdwood-Reich made his professional debut in an [[Australia Cup]] Round of 32 match for Sydney against [[Central Coast Mariners FC|Central Coast Mariners]] on 31 July 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.australiacup.com.au/match/sydney-fc-v-central-coast-mariners-australia-cup-31-07-2022/2305007#!/lineups |title= Sydney FC v Central Coast Mariners – Australia Cup Match Centre|website=[[Australia Cup]]|date=31 July 2022}}</ref> He made his [[A-League Men]] debut for the club as a substitute on 29 October 2022 against [[Macarthur FC]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://keepup.com.au/fixtures/macarthur-fc-v-sydney-fc-a-league-men-29-10-2022/2co36xh3xyiow596zdjgsai38|title=Macarthur FC vs Sydney FC|website=KEEPUP|date=29 October 2022}}</ref>

Jake won the Sydney FC Rising Star Award at the 2022 Sky Blue Awards night shortly after being promoted to the A-League from the NPL squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=davidw |date=2022-06-10 |title=Sky Blue Ball Awards Winners Crowned |url=https://sydneyfc.com/news/sky-blue-ball-awards-crown-winners |access-date=2022-11-19 |website=Sydney FC}}</ref> 2024 was selected for the PFA Players A League Team of the Season.

===St. Louis City SC===
After a standout [[2023–24 A-League Men|2023–24 A-League]] season, Girdwood-Reich was sold to [[Major League Soccer]] expansion club [[St. Louis City SC]] for an undisclosed amount,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sydneyfc.com/news/sydney-fc-academy-graduate-sold-for-record-transfer-fee/|title=Sydney FC Academy Graduate Sold For Record Transfer Fee|website=[[Sydney FC]]|date=4 June 2024}}</ref> believed to exceed the $1.3 million<ref>{{cite news |last1=Monterverde |first1=Marco |title=Sydney FC secures million-dollar transfer amount for young star heading to Major League Soccer |url=https://www.news.com.au/sport/football/sydney-fc-secures-milliondollar-transfer-amount-for-young-star-heading-to-major-league-soccer/news-story/1faea5d6d7cd5221059487853055e7cf |access-date=5 June 2024 |publisher=news.com.au |date=4 June 2024}}</ref> record set by [[Adrian Mierzejewski]].

====Loan to Auckland FC====
On 16 September 2025, Girdwood-Reich joined [[Auckland FC]] on loan for the 2025–26 season as an injury replacement for [[Nando Pijnaker]], reuniting with head coach [[Steve Corica]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/jake-girdwood-reich-reunited-with-steve-corica-at-auckland-fc/ |title=Jake Girdwood-Reich reunited with Steve Corica at Auckland FC |website=Auckland FC |date=16 September 2025 |access-date=6 November 2025}}</ref> He made his Auckland FC debut in a 0–0 draw in round 1 against [[Melbourne Victory FC|Melbourne Victory]] at [[AAMI Park]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/rd-1-post-match-report-melbourne-victory-00-auckland-fc-0/ |title=Post-Match Report: Melbourne Victory 0–0 Auckland FC |website=Auckland FC |date=16 September 2025 |access-date=6 November 2025}}</ref>

On 20 February 2026, Girdwood-Reich featured in his third [[New Zealand Derby (football)|New Zealand derby]]. After scooping the ball high following a clearance, he inadvertently pressured the [[Wellington Phoenix FC|Wellington Phoenix]] goalkeeper [[Josh Oluwayemi]] into heading the ball into his own net. Auckland FC went on to win 5–0, securing victory in all three derbies of the season, with Girdwood-Reich playing the full 90 minutes in each match.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rollo |first=Phillip |title=Wellington Phoenix humiliated as own goal sparks 5-0 thrashing by Auckland FC |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/360941786/auckland-fc-embarrass-wellington-phoenix-one-sided-derby-after-goalkeepers-horror-moment |access-date=2026-02-22 |website=www.stuff.co.nz}}</ref> 

Girdwood-Reich scored his first goal for the club in a 2–1 defeat to [[Macarthur FC|Macarthur]] at [[Mount Smart Stadium]], becoming Auckland FC's youngest goalscorer.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ahayes |date=2026-03-22 |title=RD 22 Match Report: Auckland FC 1 - 2 Macarthur FC |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/rd-22-match-report-auckland-fc-1-2-macarthur-fc/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Auckland |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Burgess |first=Michael |title=Auckland FC blow chance to go top with loss to Macarthur |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/football/auckland-fc/auckland-fc-v-macarthur-live-updates-auckland-fc-can-go-top-of-a-league-table-with-win/XEEFTTZIM5BKZKTUTN4IVZTXIM/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=NZ Herald |language=en-NZ}}</ref> He scored once more in a 3–0 victory over [[Adelaide United FC|Adelaide United]] at [[Hindmarsh Stadium]] in the second leg of the [[2026 A-League Men finals series|finals series]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=ibenet |date=2026-05-15 |title=Semi Final Leg 2 Match Report: Adelaide United 0 - 3 Auckland FC (1-4 Aggregate) |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/semi-final-leg-2-match-report-adelaide-united-0-3-auckland-fc-1-4-aggregate/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=Auckland |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Burgess |first=Michael |title=Auckland FC stun Adelaide to reach A-League grand final with brilliant performance |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/football/auckland-fc/auckland-fc-v-adelaide-utd-live-updates-a-league-semi-final-leg-two/NX5TXNVV2FCHRGHTXAZGUC23G4/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=NZ Herald |language=en-NZ}}</ref> helping Auckland progress to the Grand Final before ultimately winning the A-League Men Championship.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burgess |first=Michael |title=Champions! Auckland FC win A-League title |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/football/auckland-fc/auckland-fc-v-sydney-fc-live-updates-a-league-men-grand-final/WHAAI5ZPFFH55JMEHIVR62PHVM/ |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=NZ Herald |language=en-NZ}}</ref>

=== Motherwell ===
On 15 July 2026, Girdwood-Reich joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.]] for an undisclosed fee, signing a three-year contract until 2029.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-15 |title=Motherwell signing Jake Girdwood-Reich 'impressed' by boss Johansson |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c20476e6wy5o |access-date=2026-07-15 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gibson |first=Scott |date=2026-07-15 |title=Jake Girdwood-Reich makes the move to ML1 |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/07/15/jake-girdwood-reich-makes-the-move-to-ml1/ |access-date=2026-07-15 |website=Motherwell Football Club |language=en}}</ref>

== International career ==
First representation honours for Girdwood-Reich came in the COVID affected 2019 U17 FIFA World Cup. After playing in all three games in the qualifying tournament in Hanoi, the finals tournament and the World Cup itself were both cancelled due to COVID-19.<ref name="the-dreams-turning-into-reality-jake-becomes-a-young-socceroo">{{Cite web|url=https://www.jwire.com.au/the-dreams-turning-into-reality-jake-becomes-a-young-socceroo/ |title=The dreams turning into reality: Jake becomes a Young Socceroo |website=jwire.com.au |date=2023-02-10 |access-date=2024-04-12}}</ref>

Jake's first post-COVID-19 opportunity arose in 2023, with selection for the [[2023 AFC U-20 Asian Cup|U20 FIFA World Cup qualifying tournament]] in Uzbekistan at age 18,<ref name="the-dreams-turning-into-reality-jake-becomes-a-young-socceroo"/> where Australia were eliminated by the hosts in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the-afc.com/en/national/afc_u20_asian_cup/fixtures__standings.html |title=AFC U20 Asian Cup 2023 Fixtures & Standings |website=the-afc.com |date=2023-03-18 |access-date=2024-04-12}}</ref>

In 2024, at age 19, Girdwood-Reich was selected for the U23 Olyroos, to compete in the [[2024 WAFF U-23 Championship]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.socceroos.com.au/news/subway-olyroos-participate-waff-u23-championship-saudi-arabia |title=Subway Olyroos to participate in WAFF U23 Championship in Saudi Arabia |website=socceroos.com.au |date=2024-03-07}}</ref> He was subsequently selected again for the squad that competed in the [[2024 AFC U-23 Asian Cup]]<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.footballaustralia.com.au/news/subway-olyroos-squad-afc-u-23-asian-cup-qatar-2024tm-confirmed | title=Subway Olyroos' squad for AFC U-23 Asian Cup Qatar 2024™ confirmed | Football Australia | date=4 April 2024 }}</ref> but did not progress beyond the group stage.

'''Kevin Andrei Ciubotaru''' (born 2 February 2004) is a Romanian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bădulescu |first=Silvian |date=4 July 2023 |title=Dinamo și-a adus un fotbalist care a fost legitimat la Rangers |url=https://www.prosport.ro/fotbal-intern/dinamo-a-adus-un-fotbalist-care-pana-in-aceasta-vara-a-fost-legitimat-la-rangers-cu-prezente-la-loturile-de-juniori-ale-romaniei-fundasul-stanga-a-ajuns-in-cantonamentul-echipei-si-urmeaza-sa-semn-19691605 |access-date=5 July 2023 |website=Prosport |language=ro}}</ref>

==Club career==

Ciubotaru’s early football journey took him from Italy to Austria, where he had a brief stint at [[Rapid Vienna]]. However, he moved to the [[United Kingdom|UK]] in search of better opportunities.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.playsport.ro/exclusiv-kevin-ciubotaru-spune-povestea-transferului-sau-miraculos-la-rangers-m-au-remarcat-intr-un-clip-de-prezentare-dedicat-unui-fost-coleg-abia-astept-sa-joc-alaturi-de-ianis-hagi-111913 |title=Kevin Ciubotaru spune povestea transferului său miraculos la Rangers: ”M-au remarcat într-un clip de prezentare dedicat unui fost coleg. Abia aștept să joc alături de Ianis Hagi |publisher=playsport.ro}}</ref>

In [[England]], Kevin joined Ava Football Club, a Romanian-run football school in London, and began attending trials with clubs such as [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] and others.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.playsport.ro/exclusiv-kevin-ciubotaru-spune-povestea-transferului-sau-miraculos-la-rangers-m-au-remarcat-intr-un-clip-de-prezentare-dedicat-unui-fost-coleg-abia-astept-sa-joc-alaturi-de-ianis-hagi-111913 |title=Kevin Ciubotaru spune povestea transferului său miraculos la Rangers: ”M-au remarcat într-un clip de prezentare dedicat unui fost coleg. Eventually Ciubotaru was invited to join [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] and signed a contract with the club until the summer of 2023, initially joining the U21 squad.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.playsport.ro/exclusiv-kevin-ciubotaru-spune-povestea-transferului-sau-miraculos-la-rangers-m-au-remarcat-intr-un-clip-de-prezentare-dedicat-unui-fost-coleg-abia-astept-sa-joc-alaturi-de-ianis-hagi-111913 |title=Kevin Ciubotaru spune povestea transferului său miraculos la Rangers: ”M-au remarcat într-un clip de prezentare dedicat unui fost coleg. Although he had initially agreed to join Dinamo — having passed the trial and completed the medical. As a result, Ciubotaru opted to join Hermannstadt, who offered him a firm deal following [[Raul Opruț]]’s departure.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/kevin-ciubotaru-contract-hermannstadt-706540.html |title=E oficial. ==International career==

Ciubotaru has represented [[Romania national football team|Romania]] at various youth levels throughout his career.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.sportakm0.com/a-tu-per-tu-l-intervista/con-kevin-ciubotaru-difensore-nazionale-under-16-della-romania-4880 |title=con Kevin Ciubotaru difensore Nazionale Under 16 della Romania |publisher=sportakm.com}}</ref>

On 9 October 2025, Ciubotaru made his senior debut for the Romania national football team in a friendly match against [[Moldova national football team|Moldova]]. His strong internal performances convinced coach [[Mircea Lucescu]] to call him up.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://iamsport.ro/fotbal/echipa-nationala/si-au-facut-debutul-la-nationala-in-meciul-contra-moldovei-id40071.html |title=Și-au făcut debutul la națională în meciul contra Moldovei |publisher=iamsport.ro}}</ref>

==Style of play==

Ciubotaru mainly operates as a dynamic, modern left-back known for his direct, high-energy approach down the left flank.<ref name="uk">{{Cite web |url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/sport/19905755.kevin-ciubotaru-romanian-youngster-determined-break-rangers-first-team/ |title=Who is Rangers signing Kevin Ciubotaru? The Romanian youngster determined to break into the Ibrox first team |publisher=glasgowtimes.co.uk}}</ref>

==Personal life==

He was born to Romanian parents. His father, Silviu Ciubotaru, supported a local amateur team from [[Rome]] called Dacica, where Kevin first began playing. Ciubotaru eventually joined a church-affiliated team, participating in an old inter-congregational tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.playsport.ro/exclusiv-kevin-ciubotaru-spune-povestea-transferului-sau-miraculos-la-rangers-m-au-remarcat-intr-un-clip-de-prezentare-dedicat-unui-fost-coleg-abia-astept-sa-joc-alaturi-de-ianis-hagi-111913 |title=Kevin Ciubotaru spune povestea transferului său miraculos la Rangers: ”M-au remarcat într-un clip de prezentare dedicat unui fost coleg. Abia aștept să joc alături de Ianis Hagi |publisher=playsport.ro}}</ref>

He is a fan of [[AS Roma|Roma]], [[FC Dinamo București|Dinamo București]] and [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]. Ciubotaru is also a fan of [[Theo Hernández]], calling him his idol.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.playsport.ro/exclusiv-kevin-ciubotaru-spune-povestea-transferului-sau-miraculos-la-rangers-m-au-remarcat-intr-un-clip-de-prezentare-dedicat-unui-fost-coleg-abia-astept-sa-joc-alaturi-de-ianis-hagi-111913 |title=Kevin Ciubotaru spune povestea transferului său miraculos la Rangers: ”M-au remarcat într-un clip de prezentare dedicat unui fost coleg. '''Jesse Carmichael Randall''' (born 19 August 2002) is a New Zealand professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] and the [[New Zealand men's national football team|New Zealand national team]].

== Club career ==

=== Early career ===
Randall began his senior career in New Zealand, playing regional football with [[Island Bay United AFC|Island Bay United]] in 2018, where he scored 15 goals in 16 appearances. He moved to [[North Wellington AFC|North Wellington]] in 2019, scoring 41 goals in 44 league matches, and spent time on loan with [[Tasman United]] and [[Hawke's Bay United FC|Hawke's Bay United]] during the 2019–20 and 2020–21 seasons respectively. In 2022, Randall signed for [[Wellington Olympic AFC|Wellington Olympic]], where he scored 17 goals in 22 appearances in the [[New Zealand National League|National League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/domestic/130941044/wellington-footballer-with-an-eye-for-goal-gets-shot-at-pro-contract-in-england|title=Wellington footballer with an eye for goal|publisher=stuff.co.nz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oceaniafootballcenter.org/2020/12/23/young-jesse-randall-in-top-form-for-hawkes-bay-united/|title=Jesse Randall on top form for Hawke's Bay United|date=23 December 2020|publisher=oceaniafootballcenter.org}}</ref>

In January 2023, it was reported that Randall was training with [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] on a week-long trial.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rollo |first=Phillip |date=2023-01-10 |title=Wellington footballer with an eye for goal gets shot at pro contract in England |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/football/domestic/130941044/wellington-footballer-with-an-eye-for-goal-gets-shot-at-pro-contract-in-england |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=Stuff |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=11 January 2023 |title=Olympic winger Jesse Randall training with English League One club Barnsley |url=https://www.friendsoffootballnz.com/2023/01/11/olympic-winger-jesse-randall-training-with-english-league-one-club-barnsley/ |access-date=1 April 2026 |publisher=Friends of Football}}</ref> In March 2023, Randall moved to the United States, signing with [[USL Championship]] side [[Charleston Battery]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.friendsoffootballnz.com/2023/04/26/u-20-international-jesse-randall-makes-big-impression-in-first-start-for-us-club/|title=Jesse Randall makes big impression|date=26 April 2023|publisher=friendsoffootballnz.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uslchampionship.com/news_article/show/1265846-battery-bring-aboard-new-zealand-youth-international-jesse-randall|title=Battery bring aboard New Zealand youth international Jesse Randall|author=USLChampionship com Staff|date=22 March 2023|website=USL Championship}}</ref> He made seven appearances for the club before returning to New Zealand later that year, rejoining Wellington Olympic and scoring seven goals in eight matches in the 2024 season.

=== Auckland FC ===
On 29 May 2024, Randall was announced as one of the first signings for [[Auckland FC]]'s inaugural season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Auckland FC unveil first signings ahead of debut season|url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/auckland-fc-unveil-first-signings-ahead-of-debut-season/|website=Auckland|date=2024-05-29|access-date=2026-01-30|language=en-US|last=}}</ref> He was predominantly deployed as a striker alongside [[Guillermo May]] during the 2024–25 campaign. Randall scored his first goal for the club in a 6–1 win over [[Wellington Phoenix FC|Wellington Phoenix]] and went on to record three goals and one assist in his debut [[A-League Men]] season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=RD 20 Match Report: Auckland FC 6 – 1 Wellington Phoenix|url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/rd-20-match-report-auckland-fc-6-1-wellington-phoenix/|website=Auckland|date=2025-02-22|access-date=2026-01-30|language=en-US|last=}}</ref>

== International career ==

=== Youth ===
Randall has represented [[New Zealand national under-17 football team|New Zealand U-17]] and [[New Zealand national under-23 football team|New Zealand U-23]] at youth level.<ref>{{cite web |title=U-23's through to OFC Men's Olympic Qualifier final |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/132637 |access-date=1 April 2026 |publisher=New Zealand Football}}</ref><ref name="U23callup">{{cite web |date=21 August 2023 |title=Battery's Jesse Randall called up for New Zealand U-23's Olympic Qualifying |url=https://www.uslchampionship.com/news_article/show/1282005 |access-date=1 April 2026 |publisher=USL Championship}}</ref> He was part of the New Zealand squad at the [[2024 Summer Olympics]], scoring against the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] during the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Zealand U23 1-4 USA U23 (Jul 27, 2024) Game Analysis |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/699813 |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Brennan |first=Joe |date=2024-07-27 |title=New Zealand - USA: summary, score, goals, highlights 2024 Olympics soccer |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/new-zealand-usa-live-online-score-stats-and-updates-2024-olympics-soccer-n/ |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=AS USA |language=en-us}}</ref>

=== Senior ===
On 18 June 2024 Randall made his debut for the [[New Zealand men's national football team|New Zealand national football team]] during a 3–1 win over the [[Solomon Islands national football team|Solomon Islands]] in the [[2024 OFC Men's Nations Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Young All Whites side win opening game at OFC Men's Nations Cup with six players making debuts |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/nzfootball |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=www.nzfootball.co.nz}}</ref> He scored his first international goal on 30 June 2024 in a 3–0 win over [[Vanuatu national football team|Vanuatu]] in the final, also providing an assist in the match.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2024-06-30 |title=All Whites win sixth OFC Men's Nations Cup with 3-0 win against Vanuatu |url=https://www.friendsoffootballnz.com/2024/06/30/all-whites-win-sixth-ofc-mens-nations-cup-with-3-0-win-against-vanuatu/ |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=Friends of Football |language=en-NZ}}</ref>

Randall featured for New Zealand during their [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (OFC)|2026 FIFA World Cup qualification]] campaign.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Zealand vs Fiji 7-0 {{!}} Third Round - Semi-final {{!}} FIFA World Cup 26 |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/520/288319/288327/400019142 |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=www.fifa.com}}</ref> He was part of the squad during matches that contributed to New Zealand securing qualification.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Squad Named for All Whites FIFA World Cup Oceania Qualifiers this March |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/nzfootball |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=www.nzfootball.co.nz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-11 |title=Just one change to All Whites squad as they attempt to secure World Cup spot |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/sport/544439/just-one-change-to-all-whites-squad-as-they-attempt-to-secure-world-cup-spot?.com |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=RNZ |language=en-nz}}</ref>

On 30 March 2026, Randall scored his second senior international goal in a 4–1 victory over [[Chile national football team|Chile]] during the [[FIFA Series]]. The result marked New Zealand's first win over a South American ([[CONMEBOL]]) opponent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=All Whites Defeat Chile To Make History At Eden Park In FIFA Series |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/nzfootball |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=www.nzfootball.co.nz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Harrison |first=Brayden |title=All Whites bounce back with ruthless 4-1 victory against Chile |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/03/30/all-whites-bounce-back-with-ruthless-4-1-victory-against-chile/ |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=1News |language=en}}</ref> 

On 14 May, Randall was named in the 26-man New Zealand squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Zealand Squad Named for FIFA World Cup 2026 |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/nzfootball |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=www.nzfootball.co.nz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Powell |first=Alex |title=Wood, Smith make history as All Whites name 26-man World Cup squad |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/football/football-world-cup/fifa-world-cup-live-updates-all-whites-name-squad-for-2026-tournament/VO65EA66YRHJTDPOMT4V2RYVZ4/ |access-date=2026-05-17 |website=NZ Herald |language=en-NZ}}</ref> Randall made his World Cup debut in New Zealand's opening match, a 2–2 draw against [[Iran national football team|Iran]], coming on for [[Sarpreet Singh]] late in the match.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2026-06-16 |title=All Whites draw with Iran at FIFA World Cup |url=https://www.nzsportswire.com/post/all-whites-draw-with-iran-in |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=NZ Sports Wire |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Eli Just double earns All Whites draw with Iran at World Cup |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/06/16/eli-just-double-earns-all-whites-draw-with-iran-at-world-cup/ |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=1News |language=en}}</ref>

'''Neil Yves Farrugia''' (born 19 May 1999) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]]. Born in France, he has represented the Republic of Ireland at youth level.

==Club career==
===Youth career===
Born in [[Paris]], [[France]] to a French father and Irish mother, Farrugia moved to [[Dublin]] aged 7, where he played with St James' Athletic, St Joseph's Boys and [[Belvedere F.C.|Belvedere]] before moving to the youth academy of [[University College Dublin A.F.C.|UCD]] in 2015. He attended secondary school in [[St Andrew's College, Dublin|St Andrew's College]] in [[Blackrock, Dublin]] and was named the FAI Schools Player of the Year for 2016–17.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.faischools.ie/international/news/2018/mar/sun/neil-farrugia-named-republic-ireland-schools-player-year|title=Neil FARRUGIA named Republic of Ireland Schools Player of the Year | FAI Schools|website=www.faischools.ie}}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/neil-farrugia-4483367-Feb2019/|title=UCD prospect Farrugia picks Ireland ahead of Malta, France and Spain|first=Gavin|last=Cooney|date=8 February 2019|website=The 42}}</ref>

===UCD===
On 24 February 2017, Farrugia made his senior debut for [[University College Dublin A.F.C.|UCD]] in the opening game of the [[2017 League of Ireland First Division]] season, in a 1–0 win away to [[Cabinteely F.C.|Cabinteely]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.extratime.com/articles/18406/league-report-cabinteely-0---1-ucd/|title=League Report: Cabinteely 0 - 1 UCD|website=extratime.com}}</ref> He scored the first goal of his senior career on 13 July 2018 in a 3–0 win away to [[Wexford F.C.|Wexford]] at [[Ferrycarrig Park]].<ref>https://leagueofireland.ie/news/report-wexford-03-ucd/id-1902</ref> Farrugia was part of the team that won the [[2018 League of Ireland First Division]] title, gaining promotion to the [[League of Ireland Premier Division|Premier Division]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/national-league/ucd-top-of-the-class-as-they-make-return-to-premier-division-1.3629820|title=UCD top of the class as they make return to Premier Division|website=The Irish Times}}</ref> His first ever Premier Division goal came on 25 February 2019, when he opened the scoring in an eventual 2–1 loss away to reigning champions [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]] at [[Oriel Park]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.extratime.com/articles/22400/league-report-dundalk-2---1-ucd/|title=League Report: Dundalk 2 - 1 UCD|website=extratime.com}}</ref> Farrugia went on trial with the [[Manchester City F.C. EDS and Academy|Manchester City U23]] side during the summer transfer window but opted to remain in Ireland to complete his degree in [[Biomedical sciences|biomedical science]] at [[University College Dublin]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://extra.ie/2019/06/20/sport/soccernews/neil-farrugia-move|title=Ireland's top young prospect star turns away from Man City move to finish university studies - Extra.ie|date=20 June 2019}}</ref>

===Shamrock Rovers===
On 26 June 2019, it was announced that Farrugia had signed for [[Shamrock Rovers F.C.|Shamrock Rovers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/shamrock-rovers-3-4698771-Jun2019/|title=Shamrock Rovers announce signing of highly-rated UCD winger Neil Farrugia|first=Gavin|last=Cooney|date=26 June 2019|website=The 42}}</ref> On 3 November 2019, he came off the bench in the [[2019 FAI Cup Final]], as his side won the trophy after a penalty shootout win over [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]] at the [[Aviva Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2019/1103/1088348-shamrock-rovers-hold-their-nerve-to-end-32-year-wait/|title=Shamrock Rovers hold their nerve to end 32-year wait|first=Ed|last=Leahy|date=3 November 2019|via=www.rte.ie}}</ref> He was part of the squad that won the [[2020 League of Ireland Premier Division]], his first time winning the title.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/league-of-ireland/shamrock-rovers-crowned-2020-loi-premier-division-champions-after-bohs-defeat-to-harps/39664036.html|title=Shamrock Rovers crowned 2020 LOI Premier Division champions after Bohs defeat to Harps|date=24 October 2020|website=Independent.ie}}</ref> His first few years at the club were blighted with injuries, resulting in a large amount of fixtures being missed, with 17 appearances being the highest amount he made in a season up until 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/neil-farrugia-shamrock-rovers-injury-problems-5586657-Oct2021/|title=2 years ago, he was attracting Premier League interest. Now, he just wants to play|first=Paul|last=Fennessy|date=29 October 2021|website=The 42}}</ref> After an impressive campaign in 2022 and continued good form in 2023, Farrugia's form saw him called up to the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] squad for a training camp in May 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishpost.com/sport/shamrock-rovers-star-farrugia-called-up-to-irelands-four-day-training-camp-253648|title=Shamrock Rovers star Farrugia called up to Ireland's four-day training camp|first=Conor|last=O'Donoghue|website=The Irish Post}}</ref>

Farrugia made the most appearances of his career in his last season in Tallaght which included goals in the [[2024–25 UEFA Europa League]] against [[NK Celje]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.shamrockrovers.ie/event/shamrock-rovers-v-nk-celje/|title=Shamrock Rovers v NK Celje}}</ref> and in the [[2024–25 UEFA Conference League]] against [[FK Borac Banja Luka]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.shamrockrovers.ie/event/shamrock-rovers-v-fk-borac-banja-luka/|title=Shamrock Rovers v FK Borac Banja Luka}}</ref> as Rovers became the first Irish side to qualify for the knockout stages of a UEFA club competition.

===Barnsley===
On 3 January 2025, Farrugia signed a two-and-a-half year contract with [[EFL League One]] club [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] on a free transfer, after his contract at [[Shamrock Rovers F.C.|Shamrock Rovers]] had ended at the end of the previous month.<ref>https://www.barnsleyfc.co.uk/news/2025/january/03/neil-farrugia-signs-for-the-reds-/</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2025/0103/1489015-farrugia-departs-shamrock-rovers-for-barnsley/|title=Farrugia departs Shamrock Rovers for Barnsley|date=3 January 2025|via=www.rte.ie}}</ref> On 21 January 2026, he scored his first goal for the club, in a 5–2 win over [[Manchester United F.C. Under-21s and Academy|Manchester United U21]] in an [[EFL Trophy]] game at [[Oakwell]].<ref>https://www.barnsleyfc.co.uk/news/2025/october/21/reds-man-u-report/</ref> He made 30 appearances in all competitions for the club, scoring 1 goal by January 2026, when he was linked with a move away from the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/former-shamrock-rovers-star-neil-farrugia-to-leave-barnsley-for-dundee-united/a124322382.html|title=Former Shamrock Rovers star Neil Farrugia to leave Barnsley for Dundee United|date=11 January 2026|website=www.independent.ie}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
On 14 January 2026, Farrugia signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] for an undisclosed fee on a two-and-a-half year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/9230/NEIL-FARRUGIA-BECOMES-THE-TERRORS-FIRST-ADDITION-OF-2026-.html|title=NEIL FARRUGIA BECOMES THE TERRORS' FIRST ADDITION OF 2026|website=Dundee United Football Club}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/neil-farrugia-signs-dundee-united-6926704-Jan2026/|title=Former Rovers player Neil Farrugia leaves Barnsley for Dundee United|first=Ciarán|last=Kennedy|date=14 January 2026|website=The 42}}</ref>

==International career==
Farrugia is eligible to play for France, Ireland, [[Spain]] and [[Malta]], but opted for Ireland during his youth career and turned down approaches from Malta for an international callup.<ref name="auto1"/> Farrugia represented both the [[Republic of Ireland national under-19 football team|Republic of Ireland U19]] and [[Republic of Ireland national under-21 football team|Republic of Ireland U21]] teams, scoring on his debut for the U21s in a 3–0 win over [[Luxembourg national under-21 football team|Luxembourg U21]] at [[Tallaght Stadium]] on 24 March 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/international-soccer/stephen-kenny-starts-ireland-u21-tenure-with-a-win-as-adam-idah-impresses-against-luxembourg/37946135.html|title=Stephen Kenny starts Ireland U21 tenure with a win as Adam Idah impresses against Luxembourg|date=24 March 2019|website=Independent.ie}}</ref> In May 2023, former U21 manager [[Stephen Kenny (football manager)|Stephen Kenny]] called him up to the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] senior squad for the first time, for a training camp in [[Bristol]], England,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.extratime.com/articles/30520/neil-farrugia-among-league-of-ireland-trio-called-up-to-ireland-training-camp/|title=Neil Farrugia among League of Ireland trio called up to Ireland training camp|first=Andrew|last=Dempsey|website=extratime.com}}</ref> before putting him on standby for the June 2023 fixtures against [[Greece national football team|Greece]] and [[Gibraltar national football team|Gibraltar]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/international-soccer/ill-have-my-boots-with-me-hoops-ace-neil-farrugia-ready-for-call-up/a271465328.html|title='I'll have my boots with me' – Hoops ace Neil Farrugia ready for call-up|date=11 June 2023|website=Independent.ie}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Farrugia completed a degree in [[Biomedical sciences|biomedical science]] at [[University College Dublin]], graduating in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.extratime.com/articles/24930/from-fai-cup-final-to-biomedical-degree-finals-for-neil-farrugia/|title=From FAI Cup Final to Biomedical degree finals for Neil Farrugia|first=Macdara|last=Ferris|website=extratime.com}}</ref>

'''Sebastian Palmer-Houlden''' (born 14 November 2003) is a professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Scottish football updater|Motherwe}} club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]. He was previously on the books of [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] and [[Gillingham F.C.|Gillingham]] and played on loan for [[Chippenham Town F.C.|Chippenham Town]], [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]], [[Newport County A.F.C.|Newport County]], and [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].

==Early life==
His time as a child was split between his mother, Gayle, in [[Knowle, Bristol]] and his father Simon in [[Bath, England|Bath]]. He started playing with Bath City youth teams when he was seven and was briefly playing with Bristol Rovers before he was scouted by Bristol City.<ref>{{cite web|website=Bristol Post|accessdate=30 January 2024|title= Seb Palmer-Houlden: Bristol City talent on Man United, conquering fears and his 'weird journey|date=28 January 2024|first=James|last=Piercy|url= https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/seb-palmer-houlden-bristol-city-9062537}}</ref> He attended [[Wellsway School]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.wellswayschool.com/assets/uploads/files/Ammonite/2022/Ammonite-1031.pdf|website=Wellswayschool.com|accessdate=30 January 2024|title= Ammonite 1031 - 13th May 2022|date=13 May 2022}}</ref>

==Career==
===Bristol City===
Palmer-Houlden started playing for [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] age group teams at eight years-old. He signed a professional contract with the club in May 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bcfc.co.uk/news/new-pro-deals-for-academy-stars|accessdate=10 April 2023|title= NEW PRO DEALS FOR ACADEMY STARS|date=6 May 2022|website=bcfc.co.uk}}</ref>

He spent some time on loan with [[Chippenham Town]] at the start of the 2022–23 season. In September 2022, his contract with Bristol City was extended into 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/bristol-city-deals-deadline-day-7536320.amp|website=Bristol Post|title= Bristol City confirm two top talents sign new deals with the club until 2024 on deadline day|first=Richard|last=Forrester|date=1 September 2022|accessdate=4 July 2023}}</ref> He spent time during 2023 on loan at [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gloverscast.co.uk/owers-and-palmer-houlden-return-to-bristol-city/|accessdate=4 July 2023|website=Gloverscast|title= OWERS AND PALMER-HOULDEN RETURN TO BRISTOL CITY|first=Ben|last=Barrett|date=14 March 2023}}</ref>

In July 2023, Palmer-Holden was included in the Bristol City first-team squad on a pre-season training camp in Austria.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/bristol-city-nigel-pearson-austria-8569120.amp|website=Bristol Post|title=Bristol City leave defensive duo at home as Nigel Pearson takes 11 U21 talents to Austria|accessdate=3 July 2023|date=3 July 2023|first=James|last=Piercy}}</ref> His contract with the club was extended by twelve months.<ref>{{cite web|first=James|last=Piercy|title=Bristol City headlines: Gary Johnson to the rescue while striker signs Robins contract extension|accessdate=15 July 2023|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/bristol-city-headlines-gary-johnson-8601482.amp}}</ref>

In July 2023 Palmer-Houlden joined [[Newport County A.F.C.|Newport County]] of [[EFL League Two]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/bristol-city-loan-talented-strike-8617695.amp|website=Bristol Post|accessdate=21 July 2023|date=21 July 2023|title= Bristol City loan talented strike duo to Newport County and Yeovil Town|first=James|last=Piercy}}</ref> He made his league debut on 5 August 2023 in the starting line-up for Newport against [[Accrington Stanley F.C.|Accrington Stanley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2023/08/05/england/league-two/accrington-stanley-fc/newport-county-afc/4087884/|website=Soccerway|accessdate=5 August 2023|title= ACCRINGTON STANLEY VS. NEWPORT COUNTY}}</ref> Palmer-Houlden scored his first goal for Newport on 8 August 2023 in the 3–1 [[EFL Cup]] First Round win against Charlton Athletic.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66368378 Palmer-Houlden first Newport goal]</ref> In early September 2023 he was ruled out for three months with a hamstring injury.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66681553 Palmer-Houlden injured]</ref> In February 2024, having scored seven goals in 28 appearances in all competitions for Newport, he signed a new contract with Bristol City keeping him at the club until 2027.<ref>{{cite web|title= Palmer-Houlden signs new Bristol City deal|date=21 February 2024|accessdate=22 February 2024|url=
https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68357635|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> In April 2024 Palmer-Houlden was selected as Newport County Young Player of the Year.<ref>[https://www.newport-county.co.uk/news/2024/april/awards-evening-202324/ Townsend player of the year]</ref>

==== Dundee (loan) ====
On 21 June 2024, Palmer-Houlden joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 June 2024 |title=Palmer-Houlden is a Dee |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/palmer-houlden-signs/ |access-date=21 June 2024 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref> Palmer-Houlden made his competitive debut for the "Dark Blues" on 16 July, coming on as a substitute in an away win over [[Arbroath F.C.|Arbroath]] in the [[Scottish League Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arbroath vs Dundee: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4ngzrxwpxzt |access-date=16 July 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He opened his scoring account the following week with a goal over [[Annan Athletic F.C.|Annan Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee vs Annan Athletic: League Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ck5g3x3p7r9t |access-date=23 July 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Four days later, Palmer-Houlden followed that first goal up with a brace in a 6–0 defeat of [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Premier Sports Cup Results {{!}} SPFL |url=https://spfl.co.uk/league/league-cup/results/2441546 |access-date=27 July 2024 |website=spfl.co.uk}}</ref> Palmer-Houlden scored his first league goal for the Dee in their league opener in the [[Dundee derby]] against local rivals [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee United vs Dundee: Scottish Premiership |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/crgkylye462t |access-date=4 August 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> After suffering a knee injury away to [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]] in February 2025 which was initially feared to be significant, Palmer-Houlden returned to the pitch on 5 April as a substitute in a home win over [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cran |first=George |date=2025-02-28 |title='Great news' for Dundee on Seb Palmer-Houlden knee injury as worst fears lifted |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-fc/5192315/great-news-dundee-seb-palmer-houlden-knee-injury/ |access-date=2025-04-05 |website=The Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dundee vs St Mirren: Scottish Premiership report, reaction & stats |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c0el1q37w7xt |access-date=2025-04-05 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> After helping the "Dee" avoid relegation, Palmer-Houlden returned to Bristol City at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-21 |title=Loan departures |url=https://dundeefc.co.uk/news/loan-departures-24-25/ |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=Dundee Football Club - Official Website |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Gillingham===
On 23 May 2025, Palmer-Houlden agreed to join League Two side [[Gillingham F.C.|Gillingham]] on a three-year deal for an undisclosed fee, joining on 1 June when the transfer window opened.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.gillinghamfootballclub.com/news/gills-capture-signing-seb-palmer-houlden|title=Gills capture the signing of Seb Palmer-Houlden|website=www.gillinghamfootballclub.com|date=23 May 2025|accessdate=23 May 2025}}</ref> After struggling with injury issues to start the season, Palmer-Houlden made his first appearance for the side off the bench on 20 September in an away league win over former club [[Newport County A.F.C.|Newport County]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gillingham set club record in comeback win at Newport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c98d9l1eq0mt |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

===Motherwell===
On 19 August 2026, [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] announced the signing of Palmer-Houlden from Gillingham for an undisclosed fee; the player signed a two-year contract with the option of an additional year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/c39e8j1rg7po|title=Palmer-Houlden 'privileged' to join Motherwell from Gillingham|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=19 August 2026|accessdate=19 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Seb Palmer-Houlden is in ML1 |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/08/19/seb-palmer-houlden-is-in-ml1/ |website=motherwellfc.co.uk/ |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=19 August 2026 |date=19 August 2026}}</ref> He made his debut for the ''Steelmen'' the next day as a substitute at home in a [[UEFA Conference League]] qualifying leg against [[Germany|German]] side [[SC Freiburg]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporting |first=Live |title=Motherwell vs Freiburg: UEFA Conference League preview, team news, stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cm5yvvx526y1t |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 2 September, Palmer-Houlden scored his first Motherwell goal in a home league win over [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporting |first=Live |title=Motherwell 3-0 Dundee United: Scottish Premiership updates & report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cqx2z8w8r3xyt |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Jamie Mathieu Knight-Lebel''' (born December 24, 2004) is a Canadian professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[centre-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], on loan from [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] and the [[Canada national soccer team|Canada national team]].

== Early life ==
Knight-Lebel was born in [[Montreal]] to a Canadian father and a Welsh mother, and moved with his family to [[Bristol]], England when he was five years-old.<ref name=canada>{{Canada Soccer player|id=55761}}</ref> He attended [[Fairfield High School, Bristol]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fairfield.excalibur.org.uk/former-student-signs-professional-football-contract-with-bristol-city-fc/|website=[[Fairfield High School, Bristol]]|title=Former student signs professional football contract with Bristol City FC|date=May 23, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/brian-tinnion-bristol-city-talent-9325029.amp|website=Bristol Post|accessdate=6 June 2024|title= To loan or not to loan? Brian Tinnion outlines plan for Bristol City academy talents|first=James|last=Piercey|date=6 June 2024}}</ref>

He began playing youth soccer at age five with Stapleton AFC.<ref name=canada /> He later played with DRG Frenchay and the [[Southampton F.C. Under-21s and Academy|Southampton academy]], before joining the [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] academy at age 14, progressing through various age groups up to the U23 level.<ref name=pro /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://the72.co.uk/2022/04/27/bristol-city-set-to-hand-contract-to-youngster-jamie-knight-lebel/amp/|website=The 72|title=Bristol City set to hand contract to youngster Jamie Knight-Lebel|first=Harry|last=Mail|date=27 April 2022}}</ref> He served as captain of City's U21 team in the 2022–23 and 2023–24 seasons, and was nominated for the 2023 Championship Apprentice of the Season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bcfc.co.uk/news/city-shortlisted-in-four-efl-awards/|title=City shortlisted in four EFL Awards|date=April 11, 2023|publisher=[[Bristol City F.C.]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bcfc.co.uk/academy-news/knight-lebel-praises-injury-time-winner/|publisher=[[Bristol City F.C.]]|first=Ben|last=Thorne|accessdate=19 August 2023|title=Knight-Lebel praises injury-time winner|date=19 August 2023}}</ref>

==Club career==
In May 2022, Knight-Lebel signed a three-year professional contract with [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]].<ref name=pro>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bcfc.co.uk/news/new-pro-deals-for-academy-stars|title=New pro deals for academy stars|date=May 6, 2022|publisher=[[Bristol City F.C.]]}}</ref> On October 28, 2023, he made his league debut away against [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bcfc.co.uk/video/interviews/unforced-errors-cost-us-pearson/|title='Unforced errors cost us' – Pearson|date=October 28, 2023|publisher=[[Bristol City F.C.]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/cardiff-city-v-bristol-city-8865965|website=[[Bristol Post]]|accessdate=29 October 2023|title= Cardiff City v Bristol City - player ratings as teenagers James and Knight-Lebel shine|first=Tristan|last=Cork|date=28 October 2023}}</ref> In March 2024, Knight-Lebel signed a new three-year contract at Bristol City.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morgan |first=Ryan |date=March 15, 2024 |title=Knight-Lebel signs new deal |url=https://www.bcfc.co.uk/news/knight-lebel-signs-new-deal/ |access-date=2024-03-25 |publisher=[[Bristol City F.C.]]}}</ref>

On June 24, 2024, Knight-Lebel signed for [[EFL League Two]] club [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-24 |title=Jamie Knight-Lebel: Crewe sign Bristol City defender on loan |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cw000874zzqo |access-date=2024-06-24 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On August 13, he made his debut for his new club against [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] in the [[2024–25 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.crewealex.net/news/2024/august/13/report---rotherham-2-crewe-1/|date=August 13, 2024|title=Report - Rotherham 2 Crewe 1}}</ref> On December 29, 2024, he scored his first professional goal in Crewe's 1–1 draw at [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|Milton Keynes Dons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://canadiansoccerdaily.com/2024/12/30/watch-canada-defender-jamie-knight-lebel-scores-first-career-goal-for-crewe-alexandra/|title=Canada defender Jamie Knight-Lebel scores first career goal for Crewe Alexandra|date=December 30, 2024|first=Tom|last=Nightingale|work=Canadian Soccer Daily}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Milton Keynes Dons Milton Keynes Dons 1-1 Crewe Alexandra |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ce32ep7lp91t |access-date=2 January 2025 |work=BBC Sport |date=29 December 2024}}</ref> On February 11, 2025, Knight-Lebel conceded a penalty and was red-carded in Crewe's 3–0 defeat at [[AFC Wimbledon]].<ref>{{cite news |title=AFC Wimbledon 3-0 Crewe Alexandra |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/ce8jp3310dzt |access-date=12 February 2025 |work=BBC Sport |date=12 February 2025}}</ref>

Knight-Lebel played regularly on season-long loan at EFL League Two side [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]] during 2025-26, making 35 appearances in all competitions and was named Swindon's Young Player of the Season. He signed a new three-year contract with Bristol City in April 2026.<ref>{{cite web|date=9 April 2026|accessdate=10 April 2026|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c20d8180zyzo |title=Knight-Lebel signs new Bristol City deal|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=8 May 2026|first=Daniel|last=Carter|website=Bristol Post|url= https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/thank-you-everyone-bristol-city-10955058#|title= 'Thank you to everyone' - Bristol City defender bids farewell to Swindon Town after loan spell |accessdate=8 May 2026}}</ref>

Knight-Lebel joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on loan for the 2026–27 season and played for the club in the [[UEFA Conference League]] qualifying rounds.<ref>{{citeweb|url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/07/31/jamie-knight-lebel-arrives-for-26-27/|title=Jamir Knight-Lebel arrives for the 26-27 season|website=Motherwell|date=July 31, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|website=bcfc|accessdate=24 September 2026|title= Loan watch: 2026/27 season
|date=24 September 2026 |url=https://www.bcfc.co.uk/city-men-news/loan-watch-2026-27-season/}}</ref>

==International career==
In April 2022, Knight-Lebel was called up to the [[Canada men's national under-20 soccer team|Canada U20]] team for two friendlies against [[Costa Rica national under-20 football team|Costa Rica]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://northerntribune.ca/canada-u-20-canadian-premier-league-camp/|date=April 5, 2022|title=Six CPL Players Named To Canada U-20 Roster|work=Northern Tribune|first=John|last=Jacques}}</ref> In June 2022, he was named to the squad for the [[2022 CONCACAF U-20 Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Canada announces squad for CONCACAF men's Under-20 Championship|url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/canada-announces-squad-for-concacaf-mens-under-20-championship|website=[[Canadian Soccer Association]]|access-date=5 August 2023|date=10 June 2022}}</ref>

In February 2024, Knight-Lebel was named in the [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada national soccer team]] provisional roster for the [[2024 Copa América qualifying play-offs]] against [[Trinidad and Tobago national football team|Trinidad and Tobago]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Concacaf Nations League Play-In preliminary rosters announced|url=https://www.concacaf.com/nations-league/news/concacaf-nations-league-play-in-preliminary-rosters-announced/|publisher=[[CONCACAF]] |access-date=February 26, 2024 |date=February 26, 2024}}</ref> In October 2024, he was named to the official squad for the first time, for a friendly match against [[Panama national football team|Panama]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://canadiansoccerdaily.com/2024/10/03/marsch-poku-lopez-knight-lebel-canmnt-callups/|title=Jesse Marsch: Calling up Poku, López & Knight-Lebel represents next stage of process for CanMNT|work=Canadian Soccer Daily|date=October 3, 2024}}</ref> On November 19, 2024, he made his senior international debut in a [[CONCACAF Nations League]] match against [[Suriname national football team|Suriname]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://canpl.ca/article/canmnt-cruise-to-concacaf-nations-league-semis-after-comfortable-home-win-over-suriname|title=CanMNT cruise to Concacaf Nations League semis after comfortable home win over Suriname|date=November 19, 2024|work=[[Canadian Premier League]]|first=Mitchell|last=Tierney}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 2024, he was studying for a sports science diploma alongside his playing career.<ref>{{cite web|title=Why homegrown players flourish at Bristol City|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/68628932|date=22 March 2024|website=[[BBC Sport]]|first=Sophie|last=Hurcom}}</ref> In addition to his native [[English language|English]], he can also speak [[French language|French]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Landry |first1=Nicolas |title=Le retour aux sources rêvé de Jamie Knight-Lebel |url=https://www.rds.ca/soccer/le-retour-aux-sources-reve-de-jamie-knight-lebel-1.19388152 |website=rds.ca |publisher=RDS |access-date=4 December 2024 |language=French |date=10 October 2024}}</ref>
