'''Dario Felix Naamo''' ({{langx|ar| داريو فيليكس نعمو}}; born 14 May 2005) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|right-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee United]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 July 2025|title='Technically accomplished' Naamo joins United on season-long loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cpd1988l4l5o|website=BBC Sport|access-date=4 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=25 May 2023|title=FC Hongan Naamo nauttii pääsystä avaukseen - "Tuntui hyvältä saada enemmän vastuuta"
|url=https://www.veikkausliiga.com/uutiset/2023/05/25/fc-hongan-naamo-nauttii-paasysta-avaukseen-tuntui-hyvalta-saada-enemman-vastuuta|website=[[Veikkausliiga]] |language=fi|access-date=10 October 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=5 September 2023|title=Dario Naamo jatkaa Hongassa - 18-vuotias puolustaja noussut jo nyt isoon rooliin|url=https://www.veikkausliiga.com/uutiset/2023/09/05/dario-naamo-jatkaa-hongassa-18-vuotias-puolustaja-noussut-jo-nyt-isoon-rooliin|website=[[Veikkausliiga]] |language=fi|access-date=10 October 2023 }}</ref> Born in Finland, he plays for the [[Iraq national football team|Iraq national team]].

==Early career==
Naamo started playing football for [[Tikkurilan Palloseura]] (TiPS)<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 September 2023|title=U19-pojat ja Wales kohtaavat Eerikkilän perjantai-illassa|url=https://www.palloliitto.fi/ajankohtaista/u19-pojat-ja-wales-kohtaavat-eerikkilan-perjantai-illassa/|website=[[Football Association of Finland|Finnish FA]] |language=fi|access-date=10 October 2023 }}</ref> in [[Vantaa]], before he moved to the renowned [[Käpylän Pallo]] (KäPa) youth academy in [[Helsinki]].<ref>[https://tulospalvelu.palloliitto.fi/person/379869/player/seasons Tulospalvelu Palloliitto]</ref> In 2018, he joined the youth sector of [[FC Honka|Honka]] in [[Espoo]].

==Club career==
===Honka===
Naamo made his debut with Honka first team in [[Veikkausliiga]] on 2 July 2022 at the age of 17, in a 1–1 home draw against [[IFK Mariehamn]].<ref>[https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2022/07/02/finland/veikkausliiga/football-club-honka/idrottsforeningen-kamraterna-mariehamn/3746171/ HONKA VS. MARIEHAMN 1-1], soccerway</ref> On 5 September 2023, he extended his contract with Honka, signing "a new long-term deal", according to the club.<ref>[https://esporthonka.com/2023/09/dario-naamo-jatkaa-hongassa/ Dario Naamo jatkaa Hongassa], [[FC Honka|Honka]], 5 September 2023</ref> He scored his first goal in the league on 28 October 2023, the opening goal on the 3rd minute in a 5–0 home win against [[AC Oulu]].<ref>[https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2023/10/28/finland/veikkausliiga/football-club-honka/oulun-edustusjalkapallo/4265270/ HONKA VS. OULU 5-0], soccerway</ref>

===SJK===
After Honka was declared bankruptcy after the 2023 season,<ref>[https://www.iltalehti.fi/veikkausliiga/a/7202eef5-4a2e-4e1f-a8b0-917046e00862 Espoon sokki-ilmoitus mullistaa markkinan – Nämä pelaajat viedään käsistä], [[Iltalehti]], Anssi Karjalainen, 19 November 2023</ref> it was announced that Naamo had signed a two-year deal with fellow Veikkausliiga club [[Seinäjoen Jalkapallokerho|SJK]] on 27 November 2023.<ref>[https://sjk.fi/uutiset/sopimusuutiset/dario-naamo-pukee-ylleen-kerhon-paidan Dario Naamo pukee ylleen Kerhon paidan], sjk.fi, 27 November 2023/</ref><ref>[https://www.sportti.com/uutinen.asp?CAT=3-1&ID=506773 SJK kaappasi todellisen timantin riveihinsä], sportti.com, 27 November 2023</ref><ref name=suomi-1>[https://www.suomifutis.com/2023/11/kova-kaappaus-sjk-hankki-veikkausliigan-huippulupauksen/ Kova kaappaus! SJK hankki Veikkausliigan huippulupauksen], suomifutis.com, Eetu Ikola, 27 November 2023</ref>

===St. Pölten===
On 9 September 2024, Naamo was loaned out to Austrian club [[SKN St. Pölten]], with an obligation to buy.<ref>[https://sjk.fi/uutiset/sopimusuutiset/dario-naamo-siirtyy-sjksta-itavaltaan/ Dario Naamo siirtyy SJK:sta Itävaltaan], sjk.fi, 9 September 2024</ref>

On 5 November, his move to St. Pölten was made permanent for a €200,000 fee.<ref>[https://sjk.fi/uutiset/dario-naamo-pysyvasti-itavaltaan/ Dario Naamo pysyvästi Itävaltaan], sjk.fi, 5 November 2024</ref><ref>[https://www.mtvuutiset.fi/artikkeli/suomen-huippulupaus-siirtyy-ulkomaille-veikkausliiga-seura-loi-rahoiksi/9002964#gs.hpe7lx Suomen huippulupaus siirtyy ulkomaille – Veikkausliiga-seura löi rahoiksi], mtvuutiset.fi, [[MTV Oy]], 6 September 2024</ref> SJK also secured a sell-on clause. Naamo scored his first goal in 2. Liga on 7 March 2025, in a 3–1 away win over [[Kapfenberger SV]].

===Dundee United===
On 4 July 2025, he joined [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on a season-long loan deal with an option to buy.<ref>[https://www.is.fi/jalkapallo/art-2000011347679.html Skotlannin liigaseura hankki suomalaispelaajan], [[Ilta-Sanomat]], 4 July 2025</ref> However, on 14 August, Dundee United announced that they had signed with Naamo on a permanent basis on a three-year deal.<ref>[https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/9052/DUNDEE-UNITED-TRIGGER-OPTION-TO-BUY-FOR-DARIO-NAAMO.html DUNDEE UNITED TRIGGER OPTION TO BUY FOR DARIO NAAMO], dundeeunitedfc.co.uk, 14 August 2025</ref>

==International career==
A regular Finnish youth international, Naamo has represented [[Finland]] at various youth national team levels.<ref>[https://www.palloliitto.fi/ajankohtaista/dario-naamo-pitaa-vaan-joukkueena-onnistua Dario Naamo: "Pitää vaan joukkueena onnistua"], [[Football Association of Finland|Finnish FA]], 15 October 2024</ref>

He was named in the Finland U17 squad for the [[2022 UEFA European Under-17 Championship qualification]] tournament in October 2021, against [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national under-17 football team|Bosnia-Herzegovina]], [[Switzerland national under-17 football team|Switzerland]] and [[Gibraltar national under-17 football team|Gibraltar]]. Finland finished 2nd in the group and advanced to the [[2022 UEFA European Under-17 Championship qualification#Elite round|Elite round]]. In March 2022, Naamo was part of the Finland U17 squad in the [[2022 UEFA European Under-17 Championship qualification#Elite Round|Elite round]] matches against [[Portugal national under-17 football team|Portugal]], [[Bulgaria national under-17 football team|Bulgaria]] and [[Republic of Ireland national under-17 football team|Ireland]].<ref>[https://tulospalvelu.palloliitto.fi/category/U17ECQ!maajp2022/results EM-karsinnat U17-pojat MAAOTTELUT 2022], [[Football Association of Finland|Finnish FA]]/ Palloliitto</ref>

Naamo was part of the Finland U18 squad winning the friendly tournament Baltic Cup in June 2023.<ref>[https://www.palloliitto.fi/ajankohtaista/u18-pojat-nimetty-kesakuun-baltic-cupiin U18-pojat nimetty kesäkuun Baltic Cupiin], [[Football Association of Finland]], 30 May 2023</ref>

In October 2023, Naamo was named in the Finland U19 squad in the [[2024 UEFA European Under-19 Championship qualification#Qualifying round|2024 UEFA European Under-19 Championship qualification]] tournament, in three games against [[Romania national under-19 football team|Romania]], [[Czech Republic national under-19 football team|Czech Republic]] and [[San Marino national under-19 football team|San Marino]].<ref>[https://www.palloliitto.fi/ajankohtaista/u19-pojat-nimetty-lokakuun-em-karsintaturnaukseen U19-pojat nimetty lokakuun EM-karsintaturnaukseen], [[Football Association of Finland|Finnish FA]]/ Palloliitto, 25 September 2023</ref>

On 7 November 2023, Naamo got his first call-up to the [[Finland national under-21 football team|Finland under-21 national team]], for a friendly match against [[Sweden national under-21 football team|Sweden]], and for a [[2025 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification|UEFA Under-21 Euro Championship qualifying]] match against [[Armenia national under-21 football team|Armenia]].<ref>[https://www.palloliitto.fi/ajankohtaista/pikkuhuuhkajat-nimetty-marraskuun-otteluihin Pikkuhuuhkajat nimetty marraskuun otteluihin], [[Football Association of Finland|Finnish FA]]/Palloliitto, 7 November 2023</ref> He made his U21 debut in a 3–0 friendly loss to Sweden on 16 November 2023. Naamo was named in the Finland U21 squad for the [[2025 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2025 UEFA U21 Euro]] final tournament.

On 11 May 2026, Naamo's request to switch allegiance to Iraq was approved by [[FIFA]].<ref name="FIFA-Change">{{Cite web|url=https://knowledge.fifa.com/change-of-association-platform|title=FIFA Change of Association Platform|accessdate=11 May 2026}}</ref> On 19 May, Naamo was called up to the [[Iraq men's national football team|Iraq national team]] preliminary training camp squad before the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>[https://x.com/IraqNT_EN/status/2056771613392003532 راهام ارنولد يعلن لكم القائمة النهائية للمنتخب الوطني العراقي لخوض المعسكر التدريبي في إسبانيا قبل المغادرة إلى نهائيات كأس العالم Graham Arnold announces the squad of the Iraqi National Team for the Spain camp before the 2026 World Cup], Iraq National Team</ref>

==Personal life==
Born in Finland to a Finnish mother and an [[Iraqis in Finland|Iraqi]] [[Kurds in Finland|Kurdish]] father,<ref>[https://www.iltalehti.fi/jalkapallo/a/ef82239d-8972-4596-a02e-8c7ed85c8f75 Suomen futislupaus valitsemassa Irakin – Palloliitto taistelee vastaan: ”Teemme kaikkemme”], [[Iltalehti]], 8 May 2026</ref> Naamo is also eligible to represent Iraq.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/dundee-united/5284761/dario-naamo-dundee-united-endorsement-ilmari-niskanen/ |title=EXCLUSIVE: Dario Naamo reveals ex-Dundee United man's glowing endorsement that paved way to Tannadice |last=Temple |first=Alan |date=8 July 2025 |website=[[The Courier (Dundee)|The Courier]] |access-date=20 July 2025}}</ref> He holds a dual Finnish-Iraqi citizenship.{{r|suomi-1}} After Naamo was allegedly contacted by the [[Iraq Football Association]],<ref>[https://www.mtvuutiset.fi/artikkeli/suomen-maajoukkue-vaarassa-menettaa-superlahjakkuutensa/8882800#gs.7lorb7 Suomen maajoukkue vaarassa menettää superlahjakkuutensa], mtvuutiset.fi, [[MTV Oy]], Eetu Ikola, 20 February 2024</ref> he confirmed this in an interview in April 2024, and stated that his main goal was to represent Finland.<ref>[https://www.mtvuutiset.fi/artikkeli/irakin-maajoukkue-yrittaa-kaapata-suomalaisen-superlupauksen-18-vuotias-kommentoi-nyt-tilannettaan/8913014#gs.7lqv3l Irakin maajoukkue yrittää kaapata suomalaisen superlupauksen – 18-vuotias kommentoi nyt tilannettaan], [[MTV Oy]], mtvuutiset.fi, Eetu Ikola, 7 April 2024</ref>

'''Michael Forbes''' (born 29 April 2004) is a Northern Irish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] for [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] and the [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland national team]].

==Club career==
===West Ham United===
Forbes is a youth product of Ardboe, [[Cookstown Youth F.C.|Cookstown Youth]], and  [[Dungannon Swifts F.C.|Dungannon Swifts]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/irish-league/dungannon-star-forbes-tipped-for-top-career-after-premier-league-move/39168138.html|title=Dungannon star Forbes tipped for top career after Premier League move|date=29 April 2020|via=www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk}}</ref> He joined the youth academy of [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] on 24 July 2020 when he signed a scholarship contract with the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newsletter.co.uk/sport/football/northern-ireland/dungannon-swifts-starlet-joins-west-ham-2558186|title=Dungannon Swifts starlet joins West Ham |date=29 April 2020 }}</ref> The following season, he captained the U18s and debuted with the U23s in December 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.whufc.com/player/129|title=M. Forbes | West Ham United F.C.|website=www.whufc.com}}</ref> He signed his first professional contract with the club on 31 May 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.belfastlive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/ni-teenager-awarded-first-professional-24116440|title=NI teen awarded pro contract after impressing at West Ham United|first=Darren|last=Fullerton|date=1 June 2022|website=Belfast Live}}</ref> He made his first appearance on the senior West Ham squad for a [[UEFA Conference League]] match against [[FCSB]] on 3 November 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.football.london/west-ham-united-fc/west-ham-confirmed-11-fcsb-25428857|title=West Ham team news as Oliver Scarles and Divin Mubama make debuts vs FCSB|first=Jonty|last=Colman|date=3 November 2022|website=Football London}}</ref>

On 5 July 2024, Forbes joined [[EFL League One|League One]] club [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bristolrovers.co.uk/news/michael-forbes-joins-bristol-rovers-loan|title=Michael Forbes joins Bristol Rovers on loan|website=www.bristolrovers.co.uk|date=5 July 2024|accessdate=5 July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c51yr5xg8keo|title=Michael Forbes: West Ham defender joins Bristol Rovers on loan|date=5 July 2024|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He was recalled on 3 January 2025 to continue rehabilitation from a hamstring injury suffered two weeks prior.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.bristolrovers.co.uk/news/garrett-forbes-return-blackburn-rovers-and-west-ham-united|title=Garrett & Forbes return to Blackburn Rovers and West Ham United|website=www.bristolrovers.co.uk|date=3 January 2025|accessdate=3 January 2025}}</ref> On 30 January 2025, he joined [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Colchester United F.C.|Colchester United]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.cu-fc.com/news/2025/january/30/u-s-take-west-ham-s-forbes/|title=U'S TAKE WEST HAM'S FORBES|website=www.cu-fc.com|date=30 January 2025|accessdate=30 January 2025}}</ref> During an in-house training match, he once again suffered a hamstring injury requiring surgery, returning to West Ham United in March 2025.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/news/24978022.michael-forbes-returned-west-ham-due-injury/|title=Michael Forbes has returned to West Ham due to injury|publisher=Essex County Standard|last=Waldron|first=Jonathan|date=3 March 2025|accessdate=29 March 2025}}</ref>

On 25 July 2025, Forbes joined League One side [[Northampton Town F.C.|Northampton Town]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.ntfc.co.uk/news/2025/july/25/michael-forbes-signs-for-northampton-town/|title=MICHAEL FORBES SIGNS FOR NORTHAMPTON TOWN|website=www.ntfc.co.uk|date=25 July 2025|accessdate=25 July 2025}}</ref>
He made his Northampton debut on 2 August scoring in a 3–1 away defeat to [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Forbes on target in Northampton debut | website=West Ham United F.C. | date=4 August 2025 | url=https://www.whufc.com/news/loan-watch-forbes-target-northampton-debut | access-date=4 August 2025}}</ref>

Forbes was released by West Ham United upon the expiry of his contract at the end of the [[2025–26 West Ham United F.C. season|2025–26 season]].<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.whufc.com/en/news/west-ham-united-issue-retained-list-at-end-of-2025-26-season|title=West Ham United issue Retained List at end of 2025/26 season|website=www.whufc.com|date=10 June 2026|accessdate=14 August 2026}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
On 16 June 2026, Forbes agreed to join [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on an initial two-year deal.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/9395/NORTHERN-IRELAND-INTERNATIONAL-MICHAEL-FORBES-JOINS-THE-TERRORS.html|title=NORTHERN IRELAND INTERNATIONAL MICHAEL FORBES JOINS THE TERRORS|website=www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk|date=16 June 2026|accessdate=14 August 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Forbes is a youth international for Northern Ireland, having played up to the [[Northern Ireland national under-21 football team|Northern Ireland U21]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sunday-life/sport/michael-forbes-vows-to-seize-next-chance-with-west-ham-and-northern-ireland/a1157040493.html|title=Michael Forbes vows to seize next chance with West Ham and Northern Ireland|date=23 October 2023|via=www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk}}</ref> After injuries to the senior squad in November 2021, he was called up to train with the senior national team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.westhamzone.com/news/west-ham-united-michael-forbes-handed-northern-ireland-opportunity-after-tuesday-development-emerges/|title=West Ham: Michael Forbes handed int'l chance after Tuesday development|date=14 November 2023|website=West Ham Zone}}</ref> He debuted with the senior [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland national team]] as a late substitute in a 4–0 [[UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying]] loss to [[Finland national football team|Finland]] on 17 November 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67376194|title=Injury-hit NI suffer further misery in Finland|work=BBC Sport |date=17 November 2023 }}</ref>

'''Emmanuel Agyei''' (born 3 November 2004) is a Ghanaian [[Professional sports|professional]] [[footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] or [[centre-back]] for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] and the [[Ghana national football team|Ghana national team]].

== Club career ==

=== Shalom FC ===
In 2016, Agyei started his career with Shalom FC in the Eastern Region of the [[Division Two League, Ghana|Division Two League]], the Ghanaian second tier.

=== Dreams FC ===
In October 2021, Agyei signed for [[Ghana Premier League]] club [[Dreams F.C.|Dreams FC]] on a four-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SIGNED & SEALED |url=https://www.facebook.com/share/Pgnrppng9NJjW6mH/ |access-date=18 October 2024 |website=Dreams FC Facebook}}</ref> He made his debut on 7 November 2021 in a 3–1 away win against [[Elmina Sharks F.C.|Elmina Sharks FC]], coming on in the 85th minute.<ref>{{Cite web |title=match/soccer/2021-11-07/elmina-sharks-fc-vs-dreams-fc |url=https://globalsportsarchive.com/match/soccer/2021-11-07/elmina-sharks-fc-vs-dreams-fc/2509796/ |access-date=18 October 2024 |website=Global Sports Archive}}</ref>

=== F.C. Ashdod ===
On 22 August 2024, Agyei signed for [[Israeli Premier League]] club [[F.C. Ashdod]] on a five-year contract.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Israeli club Ashdod complete signing of Dreams FC midfielder Emmanuel Agyei |url=https://ghanasoccernet.com/israeli-club-ashdod-complete-signing-of-dreams-fc-midfielder-emmanuel-agyei |access-date=17 October 2024 |website=ghanasoccernet.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=We hereby confirm the transfer of Emmanuel Agyei to Ashdod FC. |url=https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1ohVxTD2GTpxgqyh/ |access-date=18 October 2024 |website=Dreams FC Facebook}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=הקשר האחורי עמנואל אג'יי חתם במועדון לחמש שנים. |url=https://www.facebook.com/share/p/PcLEDDzbuzAwyWBT/ |access-date=18 October 2024 |website=F.C. Ashdod Facebook}}</ref>

=== Dundee United FC ===
On 2 February 2026, Agyei signed for Scottish Premiership club Dundee United until 30 June 2029.<ref>{{Cite web |title=UNITED CONFIRM SIGNING OF GHANAIAN MIDFIELDER EMMANUEL AGYEI |url=https://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/news/9269/UNITED-CONFIRM-SIGNING-OF-GHANAIAN-MIDFIELDER-EMMANUEL-AGYEI.html |access-date=2026-03-25 |website=Dundee United Football Club |language=en}}</ref> He made his Debut against Falkirk FC on the 6th of March 2026 in a 2–1 loss in the Scottish cup quarter final.He scored his first professional goal for United on 22 March 2026 in a 2–0 win against Celtic, in the 66th minute.

'''Oscar James Moncrieff Priestman''' (born 25 March 2003) is an Australian professional [[Association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell FC]].

==Club career==
Priestman started his career with the [[Sydney FC Youth|reserve team]] of Australian side [[Sydney FC]], where he made twenty-six league appearances and scored one goal. Priestman also made his professional debut for [[Sydney FC]] having appeared in two [[Australia Cup]] matches in 2022.

Ahead of the [[2023–24 Western Sydney Wanderers FC season|2023–24 season]], he signed for Australian side [[Western Sydney Wanderers FC]], where he made fifty-one league appearances and scored two goals and helped the club achieve qualification for the [[2025 A-League Men finals series]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://aleagues.com.au/news/western-sydney-wanderers-sell-oscar-priestman-to-motherwell-details-reaction-a-league-transfer-news/|title=European club lure ‘big talent’ via Western Sydney: ‘Our next success story from Down Under’|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[A-League Men]]|date=26 August 2025|access-date=1 September 2025}}</ref> Following his stint there, he signed for Scottish side [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell FC]] during the summer of 2025.<ref name=soccerway/>

==International career==
Priestman is an Australia youth international. On 19 March 2025, he debuted for the [[Australia men's national under-23 soccer team]] during a 2–1 away [[Exhibition match|friendly]] win over the [[Croatia national under-21 football team]]. 

==Style of play==
Priestman plays as a [[midfielder]] and is right-footed. Danish manager [[Jens Berthel Askou]] said in 2025 that "he's shown his big talent and potential as a dynamic and athletic central midfielder with good feet, solid body language and a great workrate".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/cgqn5799k2eo|title='Big talent & potential' - Motherwell buy Australian midfielder Priestman|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=26 August 2025|access-date=1 September 2025}}</ref>

'''Eythor Martin Vigerust Bjørgolfsson''' (born 25 August 2000) is a Norwegian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]. 

==Early life==
Bjørgolfsson was born on 25 August 2000. Born in [[Norway]], he is the son of an [[Iceland]]ic father and a [[Norway|Norwegian]] mother.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mbl.is/sport/fotbolti/2025/11/03/islendingur_a_medal_theirra_markahaestu/|title=Íslendingur á meðal þeirra markahæstu|trans-title=Icelander among the top scorers|language=is|publisher=[[Morgunblaðið]]|date=3 November 2025|access-date=2 February 2026}}</ref> 

==Career==
Bjørgolfsson started his career with Norwegian side [[Ullensaker/Kisa IL|Ull/Kisa 2]], where he made twenty-one league appearances and scored thirteen goals.{{cn|date=February 2026}} He moved to the United States in 2019 and played four seasons of [[college soccer]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's soccer|University of Kentucky Wildcats]], where he scored 24 goals.<ref name="Motherwell"/> During his senior season in 2023, Bjørgolfsson scored ten goals and was a semifinalist for the [[Hermann Trophy]].<ref>{{cite press release |date=21 December 2022 |title=Sounders FC Selects Eythor Bjørgolfsson and Blake Bowen in the 2023 MLS SuperDraft Presented by Adidas |url=https://www.soundersfc.com/news/sounders-fc-selects-eythor-bjorgolfsson-and-blake-bowen-in-the-2023-mls-superdra |publisher=[[Seattle Sounders FC]] |accessdate=5 February 2026}}</ref> During the summer of 2021, he signed for Norwegian side [[Nardo FK|Nardo]], where he made four league appearances and scored two goals.{{cn|date=February 2026}} Bjørgolfsson signed with [[Vermont Green FC]] for the 2022 summer season and scored the club's first-ever goal on 15 May 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Record Book |url=https://vermontgreenfc.com/records/ |publisher=[[Vermont Green FC]] |accessdate=5 February 2026}}</ref> He finished the season with six goals.<ref name="Motherwell"/>

He was selected in the second round of the [[2023 MLS SuperDraft]] by [[Seattle Sounders FC]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Evans |first=Jayda |date=21 December 2022 |title=MLS SuperDraft: Sounders deal top pick; UW's Ilijah Paul selected by RSL |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/sounders/mls-superdraft-sounders-deal-top-pick-uws-ilijah-paul-selected-by-rsl/ |work=[[The Seattle Times]] |accessdate=5 February 2026}}</ref> On 2 February 2023, Bjørgolfsson signed with Seattle's reserve team, the [[Tacoma Defiance]], and played in the [[2023 MLS Next Pro season|2023 season]] of [[MLS Next Pro]].<ref>{{cite press release |date=2 February 2023 |title=Tacoma Defiance Signs Forward Eythor Bjørgolfsson and Defender Blake Bowen |url=https://www.soundersfc.com/tacoma-defiance/news/tacoma-defiance-signs-forward-eythor-bjorgolfsson-and-defender-blake-bowen |publisher=[[Tacoma Defiance]] |accessdate=5 February 2026}}</ref> He made sixteen appearances in league play and scored two goals.{{cn|date=February 2026}} Bjørgolfsson was called up to the Sounders for a [[2023 U.S. Open Cup|U.S. Open Cup]] match against the [[LA Galaxy]].<ref name="Motherwell"/>

One year later, he signed for Norwegian side [[Moss FK|Moss]], where he made seventeen league appearances and scored three goals. The same year, he was sent on loan to Norwegian side [[IK Start|Start]], where he made six league appearances and scored one goal. Six months later, he signed for Swedish side [[Umeå FC]], where he made twenty-nine league appearances and scored fifteen goals and suffered [[Promotion and relegation|relegation]] from the [[Superettan|second tier]] to the [[Ettan Fotboll|third tier]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/local-sport/motherwell-sign-eythor-bjrgolfsson-boss-36578066|title=Motherwell sign Eythor Bjørgolfsson as boss praises Norwegian striker's 'standout data'|language=en|work=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|date=19 January 2026|access-date=2 February 2026}}</ref> 

===Motherwell===
On 19 January 2026, [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] announced the signing of Bjørgolfsson from [[Umeå FC|Umeå]] to a two-and-a-half-year contract.<ref name="Motherwell">{{cite web |title=Eythor Bjørgolfsson is our first January recruit |url=https://www.motherwellfc.co.uk/2026/01/19/eythor-bjorgolfsson-is-our-first-january-recruit/ |publisher=Motherwell F.C. |access-date=20 January 2026 |date=19 January 2026}}</ref>

'''Willy Gabriel Vogt Veigantes''' (born 1 June 2002) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] or [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]. Born in Brazil, he has represented Switzerland at youth level.

==Early life==
Vogt was born on 1 June 2002 in [[Guarapuava]], Brazil. The nephew of Brazilian footballer [[Paulo Vogt]], he grew up in [[Freienbach]], Switzerland.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kicker.de/trotz-zwei-abstiegen-in-serie-bringt-sich-vogt-in-der-super-league-ins-gespraech-1231475/artikel|title=Trotz zwei Abstiegen in Serie bringt sich Vogt in der Super League ins Gespräch|trans-title=Despite two consecutive relegations, Vogt is making headlines in the Super League|language=de|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|date=26 June 2026|access-date=21 August 2026}}</ref> Growing up, he started playing football at the age of six.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://schaffhausen24.ch/articles/285437-wie-wird-man-profisportler|title=Wie wird man Profisportler?|trans-title=How does one become a professional athlete?|language=de|publisher=Schaffhausen24|date=26 November 2024|access-date=21 August 2026}}</ref>

==Club career==
As a youth player, Vogt joined the [[youth academy]] of Swiss side [[Grasshopper Club Zurich|GC]]. In the summer of 2021, he signed for [[FC Basel|FC Basel U21]], where he made twelve league appearances and scored one goal before joining [[FC Winterthur|Winterthur U21]] in 2022, where he made twelve league appearances and scored seven goals.<ref name="net">{{WorldFootball.net|new_id=pe530962}}</ref> 

That same year, he joined [[FC Schaffhausen]], where he made sixty league appearances and scored nine goals, suffering relegation from the [[Swiss Challenge League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.shn.ch/sport/fussball/2026-03-26/erst-mit-dem-fc-schaffhausen-jetzt-mit-der-ac-bellinzona-willy-vogt-hat|title=Erst mit dem FC Schaffhausen, jetzt mit der AC Bellinzona: Willy Vogt hat den nächsten Abstieg ganz dicht vor Augen|trans-title=First with FC Schaffhausen, now with AC Bellinzona: Willy Vogt is facing another relegation very close to home|language=de|publisher={{ill|Schaffhauser Nachrichten|de}}|date=26 March 2026|access-date=21 August 2026}}</ref> He subsequently signed for [[AC Bellinzona|Bellinzona]] in 2025, where he made thirty league appearances and scored eleven goals, getting relegated from the Challenge League again.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/crr81r5dj4ko|title='Impactful' Vogt joins Well after second relegation in row|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=3 July 2026|access-date=21 August 2026}}</ref> Ahead of the [[2026–27 Motherwell F.C. season|2026–27 season]], he signed for Scottish side [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], where he played in the [[UEFA Conference League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/im-brazilian-birth-meeting-neymar-37518818|title=I'm Brazilian by birth and meeting Neymar is my ultimate ambition but I'm just as excited by Motherwell move|trans-title=|language=en|publisher=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|date=5 August 2026|access-date=21 August 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Vogt is a Switzerland youth international and has represented the country internationally at under-16 and under-18 level and is eligible to represent [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] internationally. 

On 19 September 2017, he made his debut for the [[Switzerland national under-16 football team|Swiss under-16 national team]] during a 2–0 [[Exhibition match|friendly]] win against [[Italy national under-16 football team|Italy]]. Two days later, he scored his first goal for the under-16s in a 1–1 draw with Italy. In total, he made three appearances at under-16 level, scoring once.<ref name="net"/>

On 8 October 2019, he made his debut for the [[Switzerland national under-18 football team|Swiss under-18 national team]], where he scored in a 2–2 draw against [[Denmark national under-18 football team|Denmark]].<ref name="net"/>
